chapters.title: The Two Ways
chapters.html:
Psalms 1

1Blessed is the man
who does not walk in the counsel of the wicked,
nor stand in the way of sinners,
nor sit in the seat of scoffers;

2but his delight is in the law of the LORD,
and on His law he meditates day and night.

3He will be like a tree
planted by streams of water,
that yields its fruit in its season,
and its leaf does not wither;
in all that he does, he prospers.

4The wicked are not so,
but are like chaff that the wind drives away.

5Therefore the wicked will not stand in the judgment,
nor sinners in the congregation of the righteous;

6for the LORD knows the way of the righteous,
but the way of the wicked will perish.

Notes

  • The text of the Psalms — rendered from the Hebrew. The Ethiopian Psalter, like the Greek, has a hundred and fifty-one psalms; Psalm 151 is rendered from the Greek. Verse numbers follow the English: where the Hebrew counts a psalm's title as verse 1, the title stands above the psalm without a number, and the English verse 1 is the Hebrew verse 2.

  • v1 "Blessed is the man" — ashrei ha-ish, happy, how fortunate, the first word of the Psalter. Walking, standing and sitting: each line goes one step further into the company of the wicked.

  • v6 "the LORD knows the way of the righteous" — yodea, knows with care and favor (Nahum 1:7). The psalm opens with blessed and ends with perish: the two ways of Deuteronomy 30:15–20.

speech.text: Psalms 1
Blessed is the man who does not walk in the counsel of the wicked, nor stand in the way of sinners, nor sit in the seat of scoffers;
but his delight is in the law of the LORD, and on His law he meditates day and night.
He will be like a tree planted by streams of water, that yields its fruit in its season, and its leaf does not wither; in all that he does, he prospers.
The wicked are not so, but are like chaff that the wind drives away.
Therefore the wicked will not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the congregation of the righteous;
for the LORD knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked will perish.

chapters.title: You Are My Son
chapters.html:
Psalms 2

1Why do the nations rage,
and the peoples plot in vain?

2The kings of the earth take their stand,
and the rulers take counsel together,
against the LORD and against His anointed:

3"Let us burst their bonds apart
and cast their cords away from us."

4He who sits in the heavens laughs;
the Lord holds them in derision.

5Then He will speak to them in His anger
and terrify them in His fury:

6"As for Me, I have set My king
on Zion, My holy mountain."

7I will tell of the decree of the LORD.
He said to me, "You are My son;
today I have fathered you.

8Ask of Me, and I will make the nations your inheritance,
and the ends of the earth your possession.

9You will break them with a rod of iron
and dash them in pieces like a potter's vessel."

10Now therefore, kings, be wise;
be warned, judges of the earth.

11Serve the LORD with fear,
and rejoice with trembling.

12Kiss the son, or he will be angry, and you will perish in the way,
for his anger is quickly kindled.
Blessed are all who take refuge in him.

Notes

  • v2 "His anointed" — meshicho, His messiah, the king anointed with oil (1 Samuel 16:13). The apostles read the psalm of Jesus: the kings of the earth set themselves… against the Lord and against His Anointed (Acts 4:25–27). The psalm itself is rendered as the Old Testament has it, with lowercase for the king; the New Testament quotations will capitalize.

  • v7 "You are My son; today I have fathered you" — the king becomes God's son on the day of his anointing: I will be to him a father, and he shall be to Me a son (2 Samuel 7:14). The voice from heaven at Jesus' baptism, You are My beloved Son (Mark 1:11), and Acts 13:33 and Hebrews 1:5; 5:5 take up these words.

  • v12 "Kiss the son" — nashqu var: bar is the Aramaic word for son, where the Hebrew word is ben (v7). The kiss is the act of homage to a king (1 Samuel 10:1). The Greek reads take hold of instruction; others read kiss purely, or move the words: with trembling kiss his feet. Whether he in the rest of the verse is the LORD or the son is not certain.

speech.text: Psalms 2
Why do the nations rage, and the peoples plot in vain?
The kings of the earth take their stand, and the rulers take counsel together, against the LORD and against His anointed:
"Let us burst their bonds apart and cast their cords away from us."
He who sits in the heavens laughs; the Lord holds them in derision.
Then He will speak to them in His anger and terrify them in His fury:
"As for Me, I have set My king on Zion, My holy mountain."
I will tell of the decree of the LORD. He said to me, "You are My son; today I have fathered you.
Ask of Me, and I will make the nations your inheritance, and the ends of the earth your possession.
You will break them with a rod of iron and dash them in pieces like a potter's vessel."
Now therefore, kings, be wise; be warned, judges of the earth.
Serve the LORD with fear, and rejoice with trembling.
Kiss the son, or he will be angry, and you will perish in the way, for his anger is quickly kindled. Blessed are all who take refuge in him.

chapters.title: Salvation Belongs to the LORD
chapters.html:
Psalms 3

A psalm of David, when he fled from Absalom his son.

1LORD, how many are my foes!
Many are rising against me;

2many are saying of my soul,
"There is no salvation for him in God." Selah

3But You, LORD, are a shield around me,
my glory, and the one who lifts up my head.

4I cried aloud to the LORD,
and He answered me from His holy mountain. Selah

5I lay down and slept;
I woke again, for the LORD sustains me.

6I will not be afraid of the tens of thousands of people
who have set themselves against me all around.

7Arise, LORD!
Save me, my God!
For You strike all my enemies on the cheek;
You break the teeth of the wicked.

8Salvation belongs to the LORD;
Your blessing be on Your people! Selah

Notes

  • The title and the numbering — the Hebrew counts the title as verse 1, so the Hebrew numbers are one ahead of the English through the psalm.

  • The title "when he fled from Absalom his son" — the flight of David over the Mount of Olives (2 Samuel 15:13–30). It is the first psalm with a title, and the first linked to a moment in David's life.

  • v2 "Selah" — a word of uncertain meaning, found seventy-one times in the Psalms and three times in Habakkuk 3; perhaps a direction to the singers or players, a pause or a lifting up. It is kept as it stands, in italics, where the Hebrew puts it.

speech.text: Psalms 3
LORD, how many are my foes! Many are rising against me;
many are saying of my soul, "There is no salvation for him in God." Selah
But You, LORD, are a shield around me, my glory, and the one who lifts up my head.
I cried aloud to the LORD, and He answered me from His holy mountain. Selah
I lay down and slept; I woke again, for the LORD sustains me.
I will not be afraid of the tens of thousands of people who have set themselves against me all around.
Arise, LORD! Save me, my God! For You strike all my enemies on the cheek; You break the teeth of the wicked.
Salvation belongs to the LORD; Your blessing be on Your people! Selah

chapters.title: In Peace I Will Lie Down
chapters.html:
Psalms 4

For the director: with stringed instruments. A psalm of David.

1Answer me when I call, God of my righteousness!
You gave me room when I was in distress;
be gracious to me and hear my prayer.

2Sons of men, how long will my honor be turned to shame?
How long will you love emptiness and seek after lies? Selah

3Know that the LORD has set apart the faithful for Himself;
the LORD hears when I call to Him.

4Tremble, and do not sin;
speak in your hearts on your beds, and be silent. Selah

5Offer sacrifices of righteousness,
and trust in the LORD.

6Many are saying, "Who will show us good?"
Lift up the light of Your face on us, LORD.

7You have put joy in my heart,
more than when their grain and new wine abound.

8In peace I will both lie down and sleep,
for You alone, LORD, make me dwell in safety.

Notes

  • v4 "Tremble, and do not sin" — rigzu, tremble with anger or with fear. The Greek has Be angry, and do not sin, which Paul quotes (Ephesians 4:26).

speech.text: Psalms 4
Answer me when I call, God of my righteousness! You gave me room when I was in distress; be gracious to me and hear my prayer.
Sons of men, how long will my honor be turned to shame? How long will you love emptiness and seek after lies? Selah
Know that the LORD has set apart the faithful for Himself; the LORD hears when I call to Him.
Tremble, and do not sin; speak in your hearts on your beds, and be silent. Selah
Offer sacrifices of righteousness, and trust in the LORD.
Many are saying, "Who will show us good?" Lift up the light of Your face on us, LORD.
You have put joy in my heart, more than when their grain and new wine abound.
In peace I will both lie down and sleep, for You alone, LORD, make me dwell in safety.

chapters.title: In the Morning You Hear My Voice
chapters.html:
Psalms 5

For the director: for the flutes. A psalm of David.

1Listen to my words, LORD;
consider my sighing.

2Pay attention to the sound of my cry,
my King and my God,
for to You I pray.

3LORD, in the morning You hear my voice;
in the morning I set it out before You, and watch.

4For You are not a God who delights in wickedness;
evil cannot live as a guest with You.

5The boastful will not stand before Your eyes;
You hate all who do iniquity.

6You destroy those who speak lies;
the LORD abhors the man of bloodshed and deceit.

7But I, through the greatness of Your loyal love, will enter Your house;
I will bow down toward Your holy temple in fear of You.

8Lead me, LORD, in Your righteousness because of those who watch me;
make Your way straight before me.

9For there is nothing reliable in their mouth;
their inner part is ruin;
their throat is an open grave;
they make their tongue smooth.

10Hold them guilty, God;
let them fall by their own counsels;
for their many transgressions drive them out,
for they have rebelled against You.

11But let all who take refuge in You rejoice;
let them sing for joy forever,
and shelter them,
so that those who love Your name may exult in You.

12For You bless the righteous, LORD;
You surround him with favor as with a shield.

Notes

  • v9 "their throat is an open grave" — quoted by Paul among the verses showing that none is righteous (Romans 3:13).

speech.text: Psalms 5
Listen to my words, LORD; consider my sighing.
Pay attention to the sound of my cry, my King and my God, for to You I pray.
LORD, in the morning You hear my voice; in the morning I set it out before You, and watch.
For You are not a God who delights in wickedness; evil cannot live as a guest with You.
The boastful will not stand before Your eyes; You hate all who do iniquity.
You destroy those who speak lies; the LORD abhors the man of bloodshed and deceit.
But I, through the greatness of Your loyal love, will enter Your house; I will bow down toward Your holy temple in fear of You.
Lead me, LORD, in Your righteousness because of those who watch me; make Your way straight before me.
For there is nothing reliable in their mouth; their inner part is ruin; their throat is an open grave; they make their tongue smooth.
Hold them guilty, God; let them fall by their own counsels; for their many transgressions drive them out, for they have rebelled against You.
But let all who take refuge in You rejoice; let them sing for joy forever, and shelter them, so that those who love Your name may exult in You.
For You bless the righteous, LORD; You surround him with favor as with a shield.

chapters.title: Do Not Rebuke Me in Your Anger
chapters.html:
Psalms 6

For the director: with stringed instruments, on the eighth. A psalm of David.

1LORD, do not rebuke me in Your anger,
nor discipline me in Your wrath.

2Be gracious to me, LORD, for I am fading away;
heal me, LORD, for my bones are shaken.

3My soul also is greatly shaken.
But You, LORD, how long?

4Turn, LORD, rescue my soul;
save me for the sake of Your loyal love.

5For in death there is no remembrance of You;
in Sheol who will praise You?

6I am weary with my sighing;
every night I make my bed swim;
I drench my couch with my tears.

7My eye wastes away with grief;
it grows old because of all my foes.

8Depart from me, all who do iniquity,
for the LORD has heard the sound of my weeping.

9The LORD has heard my plea;
the LORD accepts my prayer.

10All my enemies will be put to shame and greatly shaken;
they will turn back and be put to shame in a moment.

Notes

  • The psalm — the first of the seven psalms the Church has prayed as the penitential psalms (6, 32, 38, 51, 102, 130, 143).

  • v8 "Depart from me, all who do iniquity" — the words Jesus will say on the last day (Matthew 7:23; Luke 13:27).

speech.text: Psalms 6
LORD, do not rebuke me in Your anger, nor discipline me in Your wrath.
Be gracious to me, LORD, for I am fading away; heal me, LORD, for my bones are shaken.
My soul also is greatly shaken. But You, LORD, how long?
Turn, LORD, rescue my soul; save me for the sake of Your loyal love.
For in death there is no remembrance of You; in Sheol who will praise You?
I am weary with my sighing; every night I make my bed swim; I drench my couch with my tears.
My eye wastes away with grief; it grows old because of all my foes.
Depart from me, all who do iniquity, for the LORD has heard the sound of my weeping.
The LORD has heard my plea; the LORD accepts my prayer.
All my enemies will be put to shame and greatly shaken; they will turn back and be put to shame in a moment.

chapters.title: God Is a Righteous Judge
chapters.html:
Psalms 7

A Shiggaion of David, which he sang to the LORD concerning Cush, a Benjaminite.

1LORD my God, in You I take refuge;
save me from all who pursue me, and rescue me,

2or like a lion they will tear my soul,
dragging it away, with no one to rescue.

3LORD my God, if I have done this,
if there is injustice in my hands,

4if I have repaid with evil the one at peace with me,
or plundered my enemy without cause,

5let the enemy pursue my soul and overtake it,
and trample my life to the ground,
and lay my honor in the dust. Selah

6Arise, LORD, in Your anger;
lift Yourself up against the fury of my foes;
awake for me; You have commanded judgment.

7Let the assembly of the peoples gather around You,
and over it return on high.

8The LORD judges the peoples;
judge me, LORD, according to my righteousness
and according to the integrity that is in me.

9Let the evil of the wicked come to an end,
and establish the righteous,
You who test hearts and minds, righteous God.

10My shield is with God,
who saves the upright in heart.

11God is a righteous judge,
and a God who is angry every day.

12If a man does not turn back, He will sharpen His sword;
He has bent His bow and made it ready.

13He has prepared for him the weapons of death;
He makes His arrows into fiery shafts.

14The wicked man is in labor with iniquity;
he has conceived trouble and given birth to falsehood.

15He dug a pit and hollowed it out,
and fell into the hole he was making.

16His trouble returns on his own head,
and his violence comes down on his own skull.

17I will give thanks to the LORD for His righteousness,
and sing praise to the name of the LORD Most High.

Notes

  • v4 "or plundered my enemy without cause" — va-achalletsah, which can also mean rescued: I who rescued my enemy without cause, as David spared Saul (1 Samuel 24:10–11).

speech.text: Psalms 7
LORD my God, in You I take refuge; save me from all who pursue me, and rescue me,
or like a lion they will tear my soul, dragging it away, with no one to rescue.
LORD my God, if I have done this, if there is injustice in my hands,
if I have repaid with evil the one at peace with me, or plundered my enemy without cause,
let the enemy pursue my soul and overtake it, and trample my life to the ground, and lay my honor in the dust. Selah

Let the assembly of the peoples gather around You, and over it return on high.
The LORD judges the peoples; judge me, LORD, according to my righteousness and according to the integrity that is in me.
Let the evil of the wicked come to an end, and establish the righteous, You who test hearts and minds, righteous God.
My shield is with God, who saves the upright in heart.
God is a righteous judge, and a God who is angry every day.
If a man does not turn back, He will sharpen His sword; He has bent His bow and made it ready.
He has prepared for him the weapons of death; He makes His arrows into fiery shafts.
The wicked man is in labor with iniquity; he has conceived trouble and given birth to falsehood.
He dug a pit and hollowed it out, and fell into the hole he was making.
His trouble returns on his own head, and his violence comes down on his own skull.
I will give thanks to the LORD for His righteousness, and sing praise to the name of the LORD Most High.

chapters.title: What Is Man?
chapters.html:
Psalms 8

For the director: on the Gittith. A psalm of David.

1LORD, our Lord,
how majestic is Your name in all the earth!
You have set Your glory above the heavens.

2Out of the mouth of children and nursing infants
You have founded strength because of Your foes,
to silence the enemy and the avenger.

3When I look at Your heavens, the work of Your fingers,
the moon and the stars, which You have set in place,

4what is man, that You remember him,
and the son of man, that You visit him?

5Yet You have made him little less than God
and crown him with glory and honor.

6You make him ruler over the works of Your hands;
You have put all things under his feet,

7all sheep and oxen,
and also the beasts of the field,

8the birds of the heavens and the fish of the sea,
whatever passes along the paths of the seas.

9LORD, our Lord,
how majestic is Your name in all the earth!

Notes

  • v2 "Out of the mouth of children and nursing infants" — the Greek has You have prepared praise, which Jesus quotes when the children cry out in the temple (Matthew 21:16).

  • v5 "little less than God" — me-Elohim, which the Greek renders than the angels; Hebrews 2:6–9 quotes the Greek and applies the verses to Jesus.

speech.text: Psalms 8
LORD, our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth! You have set Your glory above the heavens.
Out of the mouth of children and nursing infants You have founded strength because of Your foes, to silence the enemy and the avenger.
When I look at Your heavens, the work of Your fingers, the moon and the stars, which You have set in place,
what is man, that You remember him, and the son of man, that You visit him?
Yet You have made him little less than God and crown him with glory and honor.
You make him ruler over the works of Your hands; You have put all things under his feet,
all sheep and oxen, and also the beasts of the field,
the birds of the heavens and the fish of the sea, whatever passes along the paths of the seas.
LORD, our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth!

chapters.title: The LORD Sits Enthroned Forever
chapters.html:
Psalms 9

For the director: on Muth-labben. A psalm of David.

1I will give thanks to the LORD with my whole heart;
I will tell of all Your wonders.

2I will be glad and exult in You;
I will sing praise to Your name, Most High.

3When my enemies turn back,
they stumble and perish before You.

4For You have upheld my right and my cause;
You sat on the throne, judging in righteousness.

5You have rebuked the nations; You have destroyed the wicked;
You have blotted out their name forever and ever.

6The enemy has come to an end in ruins forever;
You have uprooted their cities;
the very memory of them has perished.

7But the LORD sits enthroned forever;
He has set up His throne for judgment,

8and He will judge the world in righteousness;
He will judge the peoples with uprightness.

9The LORD will be a stronghold for the oppressed,
a stronghold in times of trouble.

10Those who know Your name put their trust in You,
for You, LORD, have not forsaken those who seek You.

11Sing praises to the LORD, who dwells in Zion!
Tell among the peoples His deeds!

12For He who avenges blood remembers them;
He does not forget the cry of the afflicted.

13Be gracious to me, LORD!
See my affliction from those who hate me,
You who lift me up from the gates of death,

14so that I may tell of all Your praises
in the gates of the daughter of Zion
and rejoice in Your salvation.

15The nations have sunk in the pit they made;
in the net they hid, their own foot has been caught.

16The LORD has made Himself known; He has carried out judgment;
the wicked is snared in the work of his own hands. Higgaion. Selah

17The wicked will return to Sheol,
all the nations that forget God.

18For the needy will not always be forgotten,
nor the hope of the poor perish forever.

19Arise, LORD! Let not man prevail;
let the nations be judged before You!

20Put them in fear, LORD!
Let the nations know that they are only men! Selah

Notes

  • v1 and Psalm 10 — Psalms 9 and 10 are one poem in the Hebrew, an alphabetic acrostic whose lines begin with the letters of the alphabet in turn, broken in places; Psalm 10 has no title of its own. The Greek, and the Ethiopian Psalter with it, count the two as one psalm, so from Psalm 10 to Psalm 147 their numbers run one behind the Hebrew and English. The English numbering is followed here.

  • vv12, 18 "the afflicted… the poor" — the written text has aniyyim, the afflicted, where the read form has anavim, the humble, and the reverse in v18; the two words are near in meaning, and the read form is followed.

speech.text: Psalms 9
I will give thanks to the LORD with my whole heart; I will tell of all Your wonders.
I will be glad and exult in You; I will sing praise to Your name, Most High.
When my enemies turn back, they stumble and perish before You.
For You have upheld my right and my cause; You sat on the throne, judging in righteousness.
You have rebuked the nations; You have destroyed the wicked; You have blotted out their name forever and ever.
The enemy has come to an end in ruins forever; You have uprooted their cities; the very memory of them has perished.
But the LORD sits enthroned forever; He has set up His throne for judgment,
and He will judge the world in righteousness; He will judge the peoples with uprightness.
The LORD will be a stronghold for the oppressed, a stronghold in times of trouble.
Those who know Your name put their trust in You, for You, LORD, have not forsaken those who seek You.
Sing praises to the LORD, who dwells in Zion! Tell among the peoples His deeds!
For He who avenges blood remembers them; He does not forget the cry of the afflicted.
Be gracious to me, LORD! See my affliction from those who hate me, You who lift me up from the gates of death,
so that I may tell of all Your praises in the gates of the daughter of Zion and rejoice in Your salvation.
The nations have sunk in the pit they made; in the net they hid, their own foot has been caught.
The LORD has made Himself known; He has carried out judgment; the wicked is snared in the work of his own hands. Higgaion. Selah
The wicked will return to Sheol, all the nations that forget God.
For the needy will not always be forgotten, nor the hope of the poor perish forever.
Arise, LORD! Let not man prevail; let the nations be judged before You!
Put them in fear, LORD! Let the nations know that they are only men! Selah

chapters.title: Why Do You Stand Far Away?
chapters.html:
Psalms 10

1Why, LORD, do You stand far away?
Why do You hide Yourself in times of trouble?

2In arrogance the wicked hotly pursue the poor;
let them be caught in the schemes they have devised.

3For the wicked boasts of the desires of his soul,
and the greedy man curses and despises the LORD.

4The wicked, in the pride of his face, does not seek Him;
all his thoughts are, "There is no God."

5His ways prosper at all times;
Your judgments are on high, out of his sight;
as for all his foes, he snorts at them.

6He says in his heart, "I will not be moved;
through all generations I will not meet trouble."

7His mouth is full of cursing, deceit and oppression;
under his tongue are trouble and iniquity.

8He sits in ambush in the villages;
in hiding places he murders the innocent;
his eyes watch in secret for the helpless.

9He lies in wait in secret like a lion in his thicket;
he lies in wait to seize the poor;
he seizes the poor when he draws him into his net.

10The helpless is crushed, he sinks down,
and falls by his might.

11He says in his heart, "God has forgotten;
He has hidden His face; He will never see it."

12Arise, LORD; God, lift up Your hand;
do not forget the afflicted.

13Why does the wicked despise God
and say in his heart, "You will not require it"?

14But You do see, for You look on trouble and grief,
to take it into Your hand;
the helpless commits himself to You;
You have been the helper of the fatherless.

15Break the arm of the wicked and the evildoer;
seek out his wickedness until You find none.

16The LORD is King forever and ever;
the nations perish from His land.

17LORD, You hear the desire of the humble;
You strengthen their heart; You incline Your ear

18to do justice to the fatherless and the oppressed,
so that man, who is of the earth, may terrify no more.

Notes

  • v3 "the greedy man curses and despises the LORD" — botsea berekh, blesses, the scribes' substitute for curses (as in Job 1:5). It can also be read the greedy man blesses himself.

  • v7 "His mouth is full of cursing" — quoted by Paul in Romans 3:14.

speech.text: Psalms 10
Why, LORD, do You stand far away? Why do You hide Yourself in times of trouble?

The helpless is crushed, he sinks down, and falls by his might.
He says in his heart, "God has forgotten; He has hidden His face; He will never see it."
Arise, LORD; God, lift up Your hand; do not forget the afflicted.
Why does the wicked despise God and say in his heart, "You will not require it"?

chapters.title: In the LORD I Take Refuge
chapters.html:
Psalms 11

For the director. Of David.

1In the LORD I take refuge;
how can you say to my soul,
"Flee like a bird to your mountain,

2for the wicked bend the bow;
they have set their arrow on the string
to shoot in the dark at the upright in heart;

3if the foundations are torn down,
what can the righteous do?"

4The LORD is in His holy temple;
the LORD, His throne is in heaven;
His eyes see, His eyelids test the children of man.

5The LORD tests the righteous,
but His soul hates the wicked and the one who loves violence.

6On the wicked He will rain coals,
fire and sulfur and a scorching wind
will be the portion of their cup.

7For the LORD is righteous; He loves righteous deeds;
the upright will see His face.

Notes

  • v1 and the title — here, as in Psalms 14 and 15, the short title shares the first verse with the opening words in the Hebrew, so the verse numbers of Hebrew and English agree.

  • v6 "He will rain coals, fire and sulfur" — the Hebrew has pachim, snares; read with one vowel changed, pachamei, coals of, as the Greek has it. The fire and sulfur of Sodom (Genesis 19:24).

speech.text: Psalms 11
In the LORD I take refuge; how can you say to my soul, "Flee like a bird to your mountain,
for the wicked bend the bow; they have set their arrow on the string to shoot in the dark at the upright in heart;
if the foundations are torn down, what can the righteous do?"
The LORD is in His holy temple; the LORD, His throne is in heaven; His eyes see, His eyelids test the children of man.
The LORD tests the righteous, but His soul hates the wicked and the one who loves violence.
On the wicked He will rain coals, fire and sulfur and a scorching wind will be the portion of their cup.
For the LORD is righteous; He loves righteous deeds; the upright will see His face.

chapters.title: The Words of the LORD Are Pure
chapters.html:
Psalms 12

For the director: on the eighth. A psalm of David.

1Save, LORD, for the faithful one is gone;
the trustworthy have vanished from among the children of man.

2Everyone speaks emptiness to his neighbor;
with smooth lips and a double heart they speak.

3May the LORD cut off all smooth lips,
the tongue that speaks great things,

4those who say, "With our tongue we will prevail;
our lips are our own; who is master over us?"

5"Because the poor are plundered, because the needy groan,
now I will arise," says the LORD;
"I will set him in the safety he longs for."

6The words of the LORD are pure words,
silver refined in a furnace in the earth,
purified seven times.

7You, LORD, will keep them;
You will guard him from this generation forever.

8On every side the wicked prowl,
when vileness is exalted among the children of man.

Notes

  • v6 "silver refined… purified seven times" — God's words against the empty words of v2: every word of God proves true (Proverbs 30:5; 18:30).

speech.text: Psalms 12
Save, LORD, for the faithful one is gone; the trustworthy have vanished from among the children of man.
Everyone speaks emptiness to his neighbor; with smooth lips and a double heart they speak.
May the LORD cut off all smooth lips, the tongue that speaks great things,
those who say, "With our tongue we will prevail; our lips are our own; who is master over us?"
"Because the poor are plundered, because the needy groan, now I will arise," says the LORD; "I will set him in the safety he longs for."
The words of the LORD are pure words, silver refined in a furnace in the earth, purified seven times.
You, LORD, will keep them; You will guard him from this generation forever.
On every side the wicked prowl, when vileness is exalted among the children of man.

chapters.title: How Long, LORD?
chapters.html:
Psalms 13

For the director. A psalm of David.

1How long, LORD? Will You forget me forever?
How long will You hide Your face from me?

2How long must I take counsel in my soul,
with sorrow in my heart all the day?
How long will my enemy be exalted over me?

3Look on me and answer me, LORD my God;
light up my eyes, or I will sleep the sleep of death,

4and my enemy will say, "I have overcome him,"
and my foes will rejoice because I am shaken.

5But I have trusted in Your loyal love;
my heart will rejoice in Your salvation.

6I will sing to the LORD,
because He has dealt bountifully with me.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "How long?" — ad anah, four times: the cry of the lament psalms (6:3; 74:10; 89:46). The psalm moves in three steps, from complaint (vv1–2) to prayer (vv3–4) to trust (vv5–6).

speech.text: Psalms 13
How long, LORD? Will You forget me forever? How long will You hide Your face from me?
How long must I take counsel in my soul, with sorrow in my heart all the day? How long will my enemy be exalted over me?
Look on me and answer me, LORD my God; light up my eyes, or I will sleep the sleep of death,
and my enemy will say, "I have overcome him," and my foes will rejoice because I am shaken.
But I have trusted in Your loyal love; my heart will rejoice in Your salvation.
I will sing to the LORD, because He has dealt bountifully with me.

chapters.title: The Fool Says in His Heart
chapters.html:
Psalms 14

For the director. Of David.

1The fool says in his heart, "There is no God."
They are corrupt; they do detestable deeds;
there is no one who does good.

2The LORD looks down from heaven on the children of man,
to see if there is anyone who understands,
who seeks God.

3They have all turned aside; together they have become corrupt;
there is no one who does good,
not even one.

4Do they have no knowledge, all who do iniquity,
who eat up my people as they eat bread,
and do not call on the LORD?

5There they are in great terror,
for God is with the generation of the righteous.

6You would put to shame the counsel of the poor,
but the LORD is his refuge.

7Oh that the salvation of Israel would come out of Zion!
When the LORD restores the fortunes of His people,
let Jacob rejoice, let Israel be glad.

Notes

  • The psalm — repeated almost word for word as Psalm 53, which uses God (Elohim) where this psalm has the LORD, and differs in vv5–6.

  • vv1–3 "there is no one who does good, not even one" — Paul gathers these lines with others into one charge, None is righteous, no, not one (Romans 3:10–12). The Greek of the psalm adds after v3 the lines Paul goes on to quote in Romans 3:13–18; they come from Psalms 5, 140, 10 and 36 and Isaiah 59, and are not in the Hebrew here.

speech.text: Psalms 14
The fool says in his heart, "There is no God." They are corrupt; they do detestable deeds; there is no one who does good.
The LORD looks down from heaven on the children of man, to see if there is anyone who understands, who seeks God.
They have all turned aside; together they have become corrupt; there is no one who does good, not even one.
Do they have no knowledge, all who do iniquity, who eat up my people as they eat bread, and do not call on the LORD?
There they are in great terror, for God is with the generation of the righteous.
You would put to shame the counsel of the poor, but the LORD is his refuge.
Oh that the salvation of Israel would come out of Zion! When the LORD restores the fortunes of His people, let Jacob rejoice, let Israel be glad.

chapters.title: Who Shall Live as a Guest in Your Tent?
chapters.html:
Psalms 15

A psalm of David.

1LORD, who shall live as a guest in Your tent?
Who shall dwell on Your holy mountain?

2The one who walks blamelessly and does what is right
and speaks truth in his heart;

3who does not slander with his tongue,
does no evil to his neighbor,
nor takes up a reproach against his friend;

4in whose eyes a vile person is despised,
but who honors those who fear the LORD;
who swears to his own hurt and does not change;

5who does not lend his money at interest,
nor take a bribe against the innocent.
The one who does these things will never be moved.

Notes

  • v1 "who shall live as a guest in Your tent?" — yagur, from gur: even the righteous are guests in God's house, received by His welcome (5:4; 39:12). The question was asked at the gate of the temple, and the answer is given in ten marks of the righteous (compare 24:3–6; Isaiah 33:14–16).

speech.text: Psalms 15
LORD, who shall live as a guest in Your tent? Who shall dwell on Your holy mountain?
The one who walks blamelessly and does what is right and speaks truth in his heart;
who does not slander with his tongue, does no evil to his neighbor, nor takes up a reproach against his friend;
in whose eyes a vile person is despised, but who honors those who fear the LORD; who swears to his own hurt and does not change;
who does not lend his money at interest, nor take a bribe against the innocent. The one who does these things will never be moved.

chapters.title: You Will Not Abandon My Soul
chapters.html:
Psalms 16

A Miktam of David.

1Keep me, God, for in You I take refuge.

2I say to the LORD, "You are my Lord;
I have no good apart from You."

3As for the holy ones who are in the land,
they are the noble, in whom is all my delight.

4The sorrows of those who run after another god will multiply;
I will not pour out their drink offerings of blood
or take their names on my lips.

5The LORD is my allotted portion and my cup;
You hold my lot.

6The lines have fallen for me in pleasant places;
indeed, my inheritance is beautiful to me.

7I bless the LORD who gives me counsel;
even in the nights my heart instructs me.

8I have set the LORD always before me;
because He is at my right hand, I will not be moved.

9Therefore my heart is glad, and my glory rejoices;
my flesh also will dwell in safety.

10For You will not abandon my soul to Sheol,
nor let Your faithful one see the pit.

11You make known to me the path of life;
in Your presence is fullness of joy;
at Your right hand are pleasures forever.

Notes

  • v2 "I say to the LORD" — the Hebrew has amart, you have said, as though the psalmist speaks to his own soul; the Greek and many Hebrew manuscripts read amarti, I say, followed here.

  • v9 "my glory rejoices" — kevodi, the soul or the self (7:5; 30:12); the Greek reads my tongue, which Peter quotes (Acts 2:26).

  • v10 "nor let Your faithful one see the pit" — shachat, the pit, the grave; the Greek reads diaphthora, corruption. Peter and Paul apply the verse to the resurrection of Jesus, whose body did not see corruption (Acts 2:25–31; 13:35–37). The psalm is rendered as the Old Testament has it; the quotations in Acts will capitalize.

  • v11 "the path of life" — Peter quotes the Greek, You have made known to me the paths of life (Acts 2:28). Pleasures forever at God's right hand is the end of the way that began in Psalm 1, the way of the righteous.

speech.text: Psalms 16
Keep me, God, for in You I take refuge.
I say to the LORD, "You are my Lord; I have no good apart from You."
As for the holy ones who are in the land, they are the noble, in whom is all my delight.
The sorrows of those who run after another god will multiply; I will not pour out their drink offerings of blood or take their names on my lips.
The LORD is my allotted portion and my cup; You hold my lot.
The lines have fallen for me in pleasant places; indeed, my inheritance is beautiful to me.
I bless the LORD who gives me counsel; even in the nights my heart instructs me.
I have set the LORD always before me; because He is at my right hand, I will not be moved.
Therefore my heart is glad, and my glory rejoices; my flesh also will dwell in safety.
For You will not abandon my soul to Sheol, nor let Your faithful one see the pit.
You make known to me the path of life; in Your presence is fullness of joy; at Your right hand are pleasures forever.

chapters.title: Hide Me in the Shadow of Your Wings
chapters.html:
Psalms 17

A prayer of David.

1Hear a just cause, LORD; listen to my cry;
give ear to my prayer from lips without deceit.

2Let my vindication come from Your presence;
let Your eyes see what is right.

3You have tested my heart; You have visited me by night;
You have refined me, and You find nothing;
I have resolved that my mouth will not transgress.

4As for the deeds of men, by the word of Your lips
I have kept myself from the paths of the violent.

5My steps have held fast to Your tracks;
my feet have not slipped.

6I call on You, for You will answer me, God;
incline Your ear to me; hear my words.

7Show the wonders of Your loyal love,
You who save by Your right hand
those who take refuge from those who rise against them.

8Keep me as the apple of Your eye;
hide me in the shadow of Your wings,

9from the wicked who plunder me,
my deadly enemies who surround me.

10They have closed up their fat hearts;
with their mouths they speak proudly.

11They have now surrounded our steps;
they set their eyes to bring us down to the ground.

12He is like a lion eager to tear,
like a young lion lurking in hiding places.

13Arise, LORD! Confront him; make him bow down;
rescue my soul from the wicked by Your sword,

14from men by Your hand, LORD,
from men of the world, whose portion is in this life.
You fill their belly with what You have stored up;
their sons are satisfied,
and they leave what remains to their little ones.

15As for me, I will see Your face in righteousness;
when I awake, I will be satisfied with Your likeness.

Notes

  • v15 "when I awake, I will be satisfied with Your likeness" — temunah, the form of the LORD that Moses saw (Numbers 12:8). The awakening may be from the night of v3, or, as the Church has read it, from death (Daniel 12:2).

speech.text: Psalms 17
Hear a just cause, LORD; listen to my cry; give ear to my prayer from lips without deceit.
Let my vindication come from Your presence; let Your eyes see what is right.
You have tested my heart; You have visited me by night; You have refined me, and You find nothing; I have resolved that my mouth will not transgress.
As for the deeds of men, by the word of Your lips I have kept myself from the paths of the violent.
My steps have held fast to Your tracks; my feet have not slipped.
I call on You, for You will answer me, God; incline Your ear to me; hear my words.
Show the wonders of Your loyal love, You who save by Your right hand those who take refuge from those who rise against them.

from the wicked who plunder me, my deadly enemies who surround me.
They have closed up their fat hearts; with their mouths they speak proudly.
They have now surrounded our steps; they set their eyes to bring us down to the ground.
He is like a lion eager to tear, like a young lion lurking in hiding places.
Arise, LORD! Confront him; make him bow down; rescue my soul from the wicked by Your sword,

from men by Your hand, LORD, from men of the world, whose portion is in this life. You fill their belly with what You have stored up; their sons are satisfied, and they leave what remains to their little ones.
As for me, I will see Your face in righteousness; when I awake, I will be satisfied with Your likeness.

chapters.title: The LORD My Rock
chapters.html:
Psalms 18

For the director. Of the servant of the LORD, of David, who spoke to the LORD the words of this song on the day the LORD delivered him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul. He said:

The LORD My Rock

1I love You, LORD, my strength.

2The LORD is my rock, my fortress and my deliverer,
my God, my rock, in whom I take refuge,
my shield and the horn of my salvation, my stronghold.

3I call on the LORD, who is worthy to be praised,
and I am saved from my enemies.

Out of Many Waters

4The cords of death surrounded me;
the torrents of worthlessness terrified me.

5The cords of Sheol were around me;
the snares of death confronted me.

6In my distress I called on the LORD;
to my God I cried for help.
From His temple He heard my voice,
and my cry before Him came into His ears.

7Then the earth shook and quaked;
the foundations of the mountains trembled
and shook, because He was angry.

8Smoke went up from His nostrils,
and devouring fire from His mouth;
coals blazed out from Him.

9He bent the heavens and came down,
with thick darkness under His feet.

10He rode on a cherub and flew;
He swooped on the wings of the wind.

11He made darkness His covering,
His shelter around Him,
darkness of waters, thick clouds of the skies.

12From the brightness before Him His thick clouds passed,
hail and coals of fire.

13The LORD thundered in the heavens,
and the Most High uttered His voice,
hail and coals of fire.

14He sent out His arrows and scattered them,
lightnings in abundance, and routed them.

15The channels of water were seen,
and the foundations of the world were laid bare
at Your rebuke, LORD,
at the blast of the breath of Your nostrils.

16He reached from on high and took me;
He drew me out of many waters.

17He delivered me from my strong enemy,
from those who hated me,
for they were too mighty for me.

18They confronted me on the day of my calamity,
but the LORD was my support.

19He brought me out into a broad place;
He rescued me, because He delighted in me.

"With the Loyal You Show Yourself Loyal"

20The LORD rewarded me according to my righteousness;
according to the cleanness of my hands He repaid me.

21For I have kept the ways of the LORD,
and have not wickedly departed from my God.

22For all His judgments were before me,
and His statutes I did not put away from me.

23I was blameless before Him,
and I kept myself from my guilt.

24So the LORD repaid me according to my righteousness,
according to the cleanness of my hands in His sight.

25With the loyal You show Yourself loyal;
with the blameless man You show Yourself blameless.

26With the pure You show Yourself pure,
and with the crooked You show Yourself twisted.

27For You save a humble people,
but haughty eyes You bring down.

28For You light my lamp;
the LORD my God lights up my darkness.

29For by You I can run against a troop;
by my God I can leap over a wall.

30This God — His way is blameless;
the word of the LORD is refined.
He is a shield to all who take refuge in Him.

31For who is God but the LORD?
Who is a rock except our God?

The God Who Trains My Hands

32This God girds me with strength
and has made my way blameless.

33He makes my feet like the feet of a deer
and sets me on my high places.

34He trains my hands for war,
so that my arms can bend a bow of bronze.

35You have given me the shield of Your salvation;
Your right hand upholds me,
and Your humility has made me great.

36You made room for my steps under me,
and my ankles did not give way.

37I pursued my enemies and overtook them;
I did not turn back until they were consumed.

38I struck them through, so that they could not rise;
they fell under my feet.

39You girded me with strength for battle;
You made those who rose against me bow under me.

40You made my enemies turn their backs to me;
those who hated me I destroyed.

41They cried for help, but there was no one to save them;
to the LORD, but He did not answer them.

42I beat them fine as dust before the wind;
I poured them out like the mud of the streets.

43You delivered me from the strife of the people;
You made me the head of nations.
A people I did not know serve me.

44As soon as they hear, they obey me;
foreigners come cringing to me.

45Foreigners lose heart
and come trembling out of their strongholds.

"The LORD Lives"

46The LORD lives! Blessed be my rock,
and exalted be the God of my salvation,

47the God who gives me vengeance
and subdues peoples under me,

48who delivers me from my enemies.
You exalt me above those who rise against me;
You deliver me from the man of violence.

49Therefore I will give thanks to You, LORD, among the nations,
and sing praises to Your name.

50He makes great the salvation of His king,
and shows loyal love to His anointed,
to David and to his seed forever.

Notes

  • The title and 2 Samuel 22 — the song stands also in 2 Samuel 22, with the same occasion; the two copies differ in many small places. The Hebrew counts the title as verse 1.

  • v50 "He makes great the salvation of His king" — the written text has migdol, a tower, the read form magdil, He makes great, followed here; 2 Samuel 22:51 is the reverse. Paul quotes v49 of the Gentiles praising God (Romans 15:9).

chapters.title: The Heavens Declare the Glory of God
chapters.html:
Psalms 19

For the director. A psalm of David.

The Heavens

1The heavens declare the glory of God,
and the sky proclaims the work of His hands.

2Day to day pours out speech,
and night to night makes knowledge known.

3There is no speech, and there are no words;
their voice is not heard.

4Yet their line has gone out through all the earth,
and their words to the end of the world.
In them He has set a tent for the sun,

5which comes out like a bridegroom from his chamber,
and rejoices like a strong man to run his course.

6Its going out is from the end of the heavens,
and its circuit to their other end,
and nothing is hidden from its heat.

The Law of the LORD

7The law of the LORD is perfect,
bringing back the soul;
the testimony of the LORD is sure,
making wise the simple;

8the precepts of the LORD are right,
making the heart glad;
the commandment of the LORD is pure,
giving light to the eyes;

9the fear of the LORD is clean,
standing forever;
the judgments of the LORD are true,
and righteous altogether.

10They are more to be desired than gold,
than much fine gold,
sweeter also than honey
and the drippings of the honeycomb.

11By them also Your servant is warned;
in keeping them there is great reward.

12Who can discern his errors?
Clear me of hidden faults.

13Keep back Your servant also from willful sins;
let them not rule over me.
Then I will be blameless
and innocent of great transgression.

14Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart
be acceptable before You,
LORD, my rock and my redeemer.

Notes

  • The psalm — two halves: the voice of creation (vv1–6), where God is El, and the voice of the law (vv7–14), where He is YHWH, named seven times. The sun, which rules the sky, gives way to the law, which rules the soul.

  • v1 "the sky" — raqia, the expanse of Genesis 1:6–8, the dome of the heavens.

which comes out like a bridegroom from his chamber, and rejoices like a strong man to run his course.

chapters.title: Some Trust in Chariots
chapters.html:
Psalms 20

For the director. A psalm of David.

1May the LORD answer you in the day of trouble;
may the name of the God of Jacob set you on high.

2May He send you help from the sanctuary
and support you from Zion.

3May He remember all your offerings
and accept your burnt offering as rich. Selah

4May He give you your heart's desire
and fulfill all your plans.

5May we shout for joy over your salvation,
and in the name of our God set up our banners.
May the LORD fulfill all your requests.

6Now I know that the LORD saves His anointed;
He will answer him from His holy heaven
with the saving might of His right hand.

7Some trust in chariots and some in horses,
but we call on the name of the LORD our God.

8They have bowed down and fallen,
but we have risen and stand upright.

9LORD, save the king!
May He answer us on the day we call.

Notes

  • The psalm — a prayer for the king before battle, spoken by the people (vv1–5), answered by a single voice, perhaps a priest or prophet (v6), and closed by the people again (vv7–9). Psalm 21 is the thanksgiving after the victory.

  • v9 "LORD, save the king!" — following the accents of the Hebrew text; the Greek divides the line differently: LORD, save the king, and answer us on the day we call. With another division it can be read LORD, save; may the King answer us, the King being God.

speech.text: Psalms 20
May the LORD answer you in the day of trouble; may the name of the God of Jacob set you on high.
May He send you help from the sanctuary and support you from Zion.
May He remember all your offerings and accept your burnt offering as rich. Selah
May He give you your heart's desire and fulfill all your plans.
May we shout for joy over your salvation, and in the name of our God set up our banners. May the LORD fulfill all your requests.
Now I know that the LORD saves His anointed; He will answer him from His holy heaven with the saving might of His right hand.
Some trust in chariots and some in horses, but we call on the name of the LORD our God.
They have bowed down and fallen, but we have risen and stand upright.
LORD, save the king! May He answer us on the day we call.

chapters.title: In Your Strength the King Rejoices
chapters.html:
Psalms 21

For the director. A psalm of David.

1LORD, in Your strength the king rejoices,
and in Your salvation how greatly he exults!

2You have given him his heart's desire
and have not withheld the request of his lips. Selah

3For You meet him with blessings of good;
You set a crown of fine gold on his head.

4He asked You for life; You gave it to him,
length of days forever and ever.

5His glory is great through Your salvation;
You lay splendor and majesty on him.

6For You make him a blessing forever;
You make him glad with the joy of Your presence.

7For the king trusts in the LORD,
and through the loyal love of the Most High he will not be moved.

8Your hand will find all your enemies;
your right hand will find those who hate you.

9You will make them like a blazing oven
at the time of your appearing.
The LORD will swallow them up in His anger,
and fire will consume them.

10You will destroy their fruit from the earth,
and their offspring from among the children of man.

11Though they intended evil against you
and devised a scheme, they will not succeed.

12For you will make them turn their backs;
you will aim your bowstrings at their faces.

13Be exalted, LORD, in Your strength!
We will sing and praise Your might.

Notes

  • The psalm — the thanksgiving after victory that answers Psalm 20: there the people asked May He give you your heart's desire (20:4); here You have given him his heart's desire (v2).

speech.text: Psalms 21
LORD, in Your strength the king rejoices, and in Your salvation how greatly he exults!
You have given him his heart's desire and have not withheld the request of his lips. Selah
For You meet him with blessings of good; You set a crown of fine gold on his head.
He asked You for life; You gave it to him, length of days forever and ever.
His glory is great through Your salvation; You lay splendor and majesty on him.
For You make him a blessing forever; You make him glad with the joy of Your presence.
For the king trusts in the LORD, and through the loyal love of the Most High he will not be moved.
Your hand will find all your enemies; your right hand will find those who hate you.
You will make them like a blazing oven at the time of your appearing. The LORD will swallow them up in His anger, and fire will consume them.
You will destroy their fruit from the earth, and their offspring from among the children of man.
Though they intended evil against you and devised a scheme, they will not succeed.
For you will make them turn their backs; you will aim your bowstrings at their faces.
Be exalted, LORD, in Your strength! We will sing and praise Your might.

chapters.title: My God, My God
chapters.html:
Psalms 22

For the director: on "The Doe of the Dawn." A psalm of David.

Why Have You Forsaken Me?

1My God, my God, why have You forsaken me?
Far from my salvation are the words of my groaning.

2My God, I cry by day, and You do not answer,
and by night, and there is no rest for me.

3Yet You are holy,
enthroned on the praises of Israel.

4In You our fathers trusted;
they trusted, and You rescued them.

5To You they cried out and were delivered;
in You they trusted and were not put to shame.

6But I am a worm and not a man,
scorned by men and despised by the people.

7All who see me mock me;
they make mouths at me; they shake their heads:

8"He committed himself to the LORD; let Him rescue him;
let Him deliver him, for He delights in him!"

9Yet You are the one who drew me from the womb;
You made me trust at my mother's breasts.

10On You I was cast from birth;
from my mother's womb You have been my God.

11Do not be far from me,
for trouble is near,
and there is no one to help.

Like Water Poured Out

12Many bulls surround me;
strong bulls of Bashan encircle me;

13they open their mouths wide at me,
like a lion tearing and roaring.

14I am poured out like water,
and all my bones are out of joint;
my heart has become like wax;
it is melted within me.

15My strength is dried up like a piece of pottery,
and my tongue clings to my jaws;
You lay me in the dust of death.

16For dogs surround me;
a company of evildoers encircles me;
they have pierced my hands and my feet.

17I can count all my bones;
they look and stare at me;

18they divide my garments among them,
and for my clothing they cast lots.

19But You, LORD, do not be far away;
my strength, hurry to help me.

20Rescue my soul from the sword,
my only life from the power of the dog.

21Save me from the mouth of the lion;
from the horns of the wild oxen You have answered me.

In the Great Congregation

22I will tell of Your name to my brothers;
among the congregation I will praise You.

23You who fear the LORD, praise Him;
all you descendants of Jacob, glorify Him;
stand in awe of Him, all you descendants of Israel.

24For He has not despised or loathed the affliction of the afflicted,
nor hidden His face from him,
but heard when he cried to Him.

25From You comes my praise in the great congregation;
I will pay my vows before those who fear Him.

26The humble will eat and be satisfied;
those who seek Him will praise the LORD.
May your hearts live forever!

27All the ends of the earth will remember and turn to the LORD,
and all the families of the nations will bow down before You.

28For the kingdom belongs to the LORD,
and He rules over the nations.

29All the prosperous of the earth will eat and bow down;
before Him will kneel all who go down to the dust,
and the one who cannot keep his soul alive.

30Offspring will serve Him;
it will be told of the Lord to the generation to come.

31They will come and declare His righteousness
to a people yet to be born, that He has done it.

Notes

  • v1 "My God, my God, why have You forsaken me?" — Eli Eli lamah azavtani. Jesus cried these words from the cross in Aramaic, Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani (Mark 15:34; Matthew 27:46). The psalm moves from abandonment (vv1–21) to praise (vv22–31).

  • v8 "He committed himself to the LORD; let Him rescue him" — the words the mockers spoke at the cross (Matthew 27:43). Committed is gol, roll (your way) onto the LORD (37:5).

  • v16 "they have pierced my hands and my feet" — the Leningrad text has ka'ari, like a lion, like a lion my hands and my feet, a line with no verb. The Greek, the Syriac and the Latin read they have pierced (or dug), and one of the oldest Hebrew copies, found near the Dead Sea, has ka'aru, a verb; the reading of the witnesses is followed here (witness rule 2).

  • v18 "they divide my garments among them" — fulfilled at the cross, as John says in quoting the line (John 19:23–24; Mark 15:24).

  • v22 "I will tell of Your name to my brothers" — quoted in Hebrews 2:12 as the words of Jesus. The turn from lament to praise is sudden: You have answered me (v21).

speech.text: Psalms 22
Why Have You Forsaken Me?
My God, my God, why have You forsaken me? Far from my salvation are the words of my groaning.
My God, I cry by day, and You do not answer, and by night, and there is no rest for me.
Yet You are holy, enthroned on the praises of Israel.
In You our fathers trusted; they trusted, and You rescued them.
To You they cried out and were delivered; in You they trusted and were not put to shame.
But I am a worm and not a man, scorned by men and despised by the people.
All who see me mock me; they make mouths at me; they shake their heads:
"He committed himself to the LORD; let Him rescue him; let Him deliver him, for He delights in him!"
Yet You are the one who drew me from the womb; You made me trust at my mother's breasts.
On You I was cast from birth; from my mother's womb You have been my God.
Do not be far from me, for trouble is near, and there is no one to help.
Like Water Poured Out
Many bulls surround me; strong bulls of Bashan encircle me;
they open their mouths wide at me, like a lion tearing and roaring.
I am poured out like water, and all my bones are out of joint; my heart has become like wax; it is melted within me.
My strength is dried up like a piece of pottery, and my tongue clings to my jaws; You lay me in the dust of death.
For dogs surround me; a company of evildoers encircles me; they have pierced my hands and my feet.
I can count all my bones; they look and stare at me;
they divide my garments among them, and for my clothing they cast lots.
But You, LORD, do not be far away; my strength, hurry to help me.
Rescue my soul from the sword, my only life from the power of the dog.
Save me from the mouth of the lion; from the horns of the wild oxen You have answered me.
In the Great Congregation
I will tell of Your name to my brothers; among the congregation I will praise You.
You who fear the LORD, praise Him; all you descendants of Jacob, glorify Him; stand in awe of Him, all you descendants of Israel.
For He has not despised or loathed the affliction of the afflicted, nor hidden His face from him, but heard when he cried to Him.
From You comes my praise in the great congregation; I will pay my vows before those who fear Him.
The humble will eat and be satisfied; those who seek Him will praise the LORD. May your hearts live forever!
All the ends of the earth will remember and turn to the LORD, and all the families of the nations will bow down before You.
For the kingdom belongs to the LORD, and He rules over the nations.
All the prosperous of the earth will eat and bow down; before Him will kneel all who go down to the dust, and the one who cannot keep his soul alive.
Offspring will serve Him; it will be told of the Lord to the generation to come.
They will come and declare His righteousness to a people yet to be born, that He has done it.

chapters.title: The LORD Is My Shepherd
chapters.html:
Psalms 23

A psalm of David.

1The LORD is my shepherd; I lack nothing.

2He makes me lie down in green pastures;
He leads me beside still waters.

3He brings back my soul;
He guides me in paths of righteousness
for His name's sake.

4Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death,
I fear no evil, for You are with me;
Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me.

5You prepare a table before me
in the presence of my enemies;
You anoint my head with oil;
my cup overflows.

6Surely goodness and loyal love will pursue me
all the days of my life,
and I will dwell in the house of the LORD
for length of days.

Notes

  • v1 "The LORD is my shepherd" — YHWH ro'i: the king as shepherd of his people (2 Samuel 5:2), and God as Israel's shepherd (80:1; Genesis 48:15; Ezekiel 34:11–16). David was a shepherd before he was a king (1 Samuel 16:11). I am the good shepherd (John 10:11).

  • v4 "the valley of the shadow of death" — gei tsalmavet, a valley of deep darkness (Job 10:21–22; Jeremiah 2:6). Rod and staff: the club against beasts and the crook to guide.

  • v6 "I will dwell in the house of the LORD" — the Hebrew has ve-shavti, and I will return; the Greek and most translations read ve-yashavti, and I will dwell, as in 27:4, followed here. For length of days, le-orekh yamim, is for all one's life.

speech.text: Psalms 23
The LORD is my shepherd; I lack nothing.
He makes me lie down in green pastures; He leads me beside still waters.
He brings back my soul; He guides me in paths of righteousness for His name's sake.
Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I fear no evil, for You are with me; Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me.
You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies; You anoint my head with oil; my cup overflows.
Surely goodness and loyal love will pursue me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the house of the LORD for length of days.

chapters.title: The King of Glory
chapters.html:
Psalms 24

Of David. A psalm.

1The earth is the LORD's, and all that fills it,
the world and those who live in it,

2for He has founded it on the seas
and established it on the rivers.

3Who shall go up the mountain of the LORD?
Who shall stand in His holy place?

4The one who has clean hands and a pure heart,
who has not lifted up his soul to what is false
and has not sworn deceitfully.

5He will receive a blessing from the LORD
and righteousness from the God of his salvation.

6Such is the generation of those who seek Him,
who seek Your face, God of Jacob. Selah

7Lift up your heads, you gates,
and be lifted up, you everlasting doors,
that the King of glory may come in.

8Who is this King of glory?
The LORD, strong and mighty,
the LORD, mighty in battle.

9Lift up your heads, you gates,
and lift them up, you everlasting doors,
that the King of glory may come in.

10Who is He, this King of glory?
The LORD of hosts,
He is the King of glory. Selah

Notes

  • v1 "The earth is the LORD's, and all that fills it" — quoted by Paul of food offered to idols: everything is the Lord's (1 Corinthians 10:26; Exodus 19:5).

  • v4 "who has not lifted up his soul to what is false" — the written text has nafsho, his soul, followed here; the read form has nafshi, My soul, God's own life, as in you shall not take up the name of the LORD your God in vain (Exodus 20:7).

  • v6 "God of Jacob" — the Hebrew has only Jacob: who seek Your face, Jacob; the Greek and Syriac read the face of the God of Jacob, followed here, since Jacob is not the one being sought.

  • vv7–10 "Lift up your heads, you gates" — the ark of the LORD coming up into Jerusalem (2 Samuel 6:12–15), the gates told to grow tall for the King who enters. The Church has sung the verses of Christ's ascension.

speech.text: Psalms 24
The earth is the LORD's, and all that fills it, the world and those who live in it,
for He has founded it on the seas and established it on the rivers.
Who shall go up the mountain of the LORD? Who shall stand in His holy place?
The one who has clean hands and a pure heart, who has not lifted up his soul to what is false and has not sworn deceitfully.
He will receive a blessing from the LORD and righteousness from the God of his salvation.
Such is the generation of those who seek Him, who seek Your face, God of Jacob. Selah
Lift up your heads, you gates, and be lifted up, you everlasting doors, that the King of glory may come in.
Who is this King of glory? The LORD, strong and mighty, the LORD, mighty in battle.
Lift up your heads, you gates, and lift them up, you everlasting doors, that the King of glory may come in.
Who is He, this King of glory? The LORD of hosts, He is the King of glory. Selah

chapters.title: To You, LORD, I Lift Up My Soul
chapters.html:
Psalms 25

Of David.

1To You, LORD, I lift up my soul.

2My God, in You I trust;
let me not be put to shame;
let not my enemies exult over me.

3Indeed, none who wait for You will be put to shame;
those who are treacherous without cause will be put to shame.

4Make Your ways known to me, LORD;
teach me Your paths.

5Lead me in Your truth and teach me,
for You are the God of my salvation;
for You I wait all the day.

6Remember Your compassion, LORD, and Your loyal love,
for they have been from of old.

7Do not remember the sins of my youth or my transgressions;
according to Your loyal love remember me,
for the sake of Your goodness, LORD.

8Good and upright is the LORD;
therefore He instructs sinners in the way.

9He leads the humble in what is right
and teaches the humble His way.

10All the paths of the LORD are loyal love and faithfulness
for those who keep His covenant and His testimonies.

11For Your name's sake, LORD,
pardon my iniquity, for it is great.

12Who is the man who fears the LORD?
He will instruct him in the way he should choose.

13His soul will lodge in good things,
and his offspring will inherit the land.

14The friendship of the LORD is for those who fear Him,
and He makes His covenant known to them.

15My eyes are always toward the LORD,
for He will bring my feet out of the net.

16Turn to me and be gracious to me,
for I am alone and afflicted.

17The troubles of my heart have grown wide;
bring me out of my distress.

18See my affliction and my trouble,
and forgive all my sins.

19See how many are my enemies,
and with what violent hatred they hate me.

20Guard my soul and rescue me;
let me not be put to shame, for I take refuge in You.

21Let integrity and uprightness keep me,
for I wait for You.

22Redeem Israel, God,
out of all his troubles.

Notes

  • The psalm — an acrostic: each verse begins with the next letter of the Hebrew alphabet, with a few letters missing or doubled. The last verse stands outside the alphabet, a prayer for all Israel; Psalm 34 ends the same way.

speech.text: Psalms 25
To You, LORD, I lift up my soul.
My God, in You I trust; let me not be put to shame; let not my enemies exult over me.
Indeed, none who wait for You will be put to shame; those who are treacherous without cause will be put to shame.
Make Your ways known to me, LORD; teach me Your paths.
Lead me in Your truth and teach me, for You are the God of my salvation; for You I wait all the day.
Remember Your compassion, LORD, and Your loyal love, for they have been from of old.
Do not remember the sins of my youth or my transgressions; according to Your loyal love remember me, for the sake of Your goodness, LORD.
Good and upright is the LORD; therefore He instructs sinners in the way.
He leads the humble in what is right and teaches the humble His way.
All the paths of the LORD are loyal love and faithfulness for those who keep His covenant and His testimonies.
For Your name's sake, LORD, pardon my iniquity, for it is great.
Who is the man who fears the LORD? He will instruct him in the way he should choose.
His soul will lodge in good things, and his offspring will inherit the land.
The friendship of the LORD is for those who fear Him, and He makes His covenant known to them.
My eyes are always toward the LORD, for He will bring my feet out of the net.
Turn to me and be gracious to me, for I am alone and afflicted.
The troubles of my heart have grown wide; bring me out of my distress.
See my affliction and my trouble, and forgive all my sins.
See how many are my enemies, and with what violent hatred they hate me.
Guard my soul and rescue me; let me not be put to shame, for I take refuge in You.
Let integrity and uprightness keep me, for I wait for You.
Redeem Israel, God, out of all his troubles.

chapters.title: I Have Walked in My Integrity
chapters.html:
Psalms 26

Of David.

1Vindicate me, LORD,
for I have walked in my integrity,
and I have trusted in the LORD without wavering.

2Test me, LORD, and try me;
refine my mind and my heart.

3For Your loyal love is before my eyes,
and I walk in Your faithfulness.

4I do not sit with men of falsehood,
nor do I go in with those who hide what they are.

5I hate the assembly of evildoers,
and I will not sit with the wicked.

6I wash my hands in innocence
and go around Your altar, LORD,

7to make the sound of thanksgiving heard
and tell of all Your wonders.

8LORD, I love the dwelling of Your house
and the place where Your glory lives.

9Do not gather my soul away with sinners,
nor my life with men of bloodshed,

10in whose hands are evil schemes,
and whose right hand is full of bribes.

11But as for me, I walk in my integrity;
redeem me, and be gracious to me.

12My foot stands on level ground;
in the assemblies I will bless the LORD.

Notes

  • v1 "my integrity" — tummi, the word of Job 2:3 and 27:5; it frames the psalm (v11).

speech.text: Psalms 26
Vindicate me, LORD, for I have walked in my integrity, and I have trusted in the LORD without wavering.
Test me, LORD, and try me; refine my mind and my heart.
For Your loyal love is before my eyes, and I walk in Your faithfulness.
I do not sit with men of falsehood, nor do I go in with those who hide what they are.
I hate the assembly of evildoers, and I will not sit with the wicked.
I wash my hands in innocence and go around Your altar, LORD,
to make the sound of thanksgiving heard and tell of all Your wonders.
LORD, I love the dwelling of Your house and the place where Your glory lives.
Do not gather my soul away with sinners, nor my life with men of bloodshed,
in whose hands are evil schemes, and whose right hand is full of bribes.
But as for me, I walk in my integrity; redeem me, and be gracious to me.
My foot stands on level ground; in the assemblies I will bless the LORD.

chapters.title: The LORD Is My Light
chapters.html:
Psalms 27

Of David.

1The LORD is my light and my salvation;
whom shall I fear?
The LORD is the stronghold of my life;
of whom shall I be afraid?

2When evildoers closed in on me to eat up my flesh,
my adversaries and my enemies,
they stumbled and fell.

3Though an army camp against me,
my heart will not fear;
though war rise against me,
even then I will be confident.

4One thing I have asked of the LORD;
that I will seek:
to dwell in the house of the LORD
all the days of my life,
to gaze on the beauty of the LORD
and to inquire in His temple.

5For He will hide me in His shelter
in the day of trouble;
He will conceal me in the hiding place of His tent;
He will lift me high on a rock.

6Now my head will be lifted up
above my enemies around me,
and I will offer in His tent
sacrifices with shouts of joy;
I will sing and make music to the LORD.

7Hear, LORD, my voice when I call;
be gracious to me and answer me.

8My heart says of You, "Seek My face."
Your face, LORD, I will seek.

9Do not hide Your face from me;
do not turn Your servant away in anger;
You have been my help.
Do not cast me off or forsake me,
God of my salvation.

10For my father and my mother have forsaken me,
but the LORD will take me in.

11Teach me Your way, LORD,
and lead me on a level path
because of those who watch me.

12Do not give me up to the will of my adversaries,
for false witnesses have risen against me,
and they breathe out violence.

13If I had not believed that I would see the goodness of the LORD
in the land of the living —

14Wait for the LORD;
be strong, and let your heart take courage;
wait for the LORD!

Notes

  • v13 "If I had not believed" — lule, marked in the Hebrew text with special dots above and below, the scribes' sign of a doubtful word; the Greek lacks it, and reads I believe that I will see. With the word, the sentence breaks off: If I had not believed… (I would have perished).

speech.text: Psalms 27
The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? The LORD is the stronghold of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
When evildoers closed in on me to eat up my flesh, my adversaries and my enemies, they stumbled and fell.
Though an army camp against me, my heart will not fear; though war rise against me, even then I will be confident.
One thing I have asked of the LORD; that I will seek: to dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to gaze on the beauty of the LORD and to inquire in His temple.
For He will hide me in His shelter in the day of trouble; He will conceal me in the hiding place of His tent; He will lift me high on a rock.
Now my head will be lifted up above my enemies around me, and I will offer in His tent sacrifices with shouts of joy; I will sing and make music to the LORD.
Hear, LORD, my voice when I call; be gracious to me and answer me.
My heart says of You, "Seek My face." Your face, LORD, I will seek.
Do not hide Your face from me; do not turn Your servant away in anger; You have been my help. Do not cast me off or forsake me, God of my salvation.
For my father and my mother have forsaken me, but the LORD will take me in.
Teach me Your way, LORD, and lead me on a level path because of those who watch me.
Do not give me up to the will of my adversaries, for false witnesses have risen against me, and they breathe out violence.
If I had not believed that I would see the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living —
Wait for the LORD; be strong, and let your heart take courage; wait for the LORD!

chapters.title: The LORD Is My Strength and My Shield
chapters.html:
Psalms 28

Of David.

1To You, LORD, I call;
my rock, do not be deaf to me,
or, if You are silent to me,
I will become like those who go down to the pit.

2Hear the sound of my pleas for mercy
when I cry to You for help,
when I lift up my hands
toward Your holy inner sanctuary.

3Do not drag me away with the wicked,
with those who do iniquity,
who speak peace with their neighbors
while evil is in their hearts.

4Give to them according to their work
and according to the evil of their deeds;
give to them according to the work of their hands;
pay them back what they deserve.

5Because they do not consider the deeds of the LORD
or the work of His hands,
He will tear them down and not build them up.

6Blessed be the LORD,
for He has heard the sound of my pleas for mercy.

7The LORD is my strength and my shield;
in Him my heart trusts, and I am helped;
my heart exults,
and with my song I give thanks to Him.

8The LORD is their strength;
He is the saving stronghold of His anointed.

9Save Your people and bless Your inheritance;
shepherd them and carry them forever.

Notes

  • v8 "The LORD is their strength" — oz lamo, strength to them, His people; the Greek, Syriac and some Hebrew manuscripts read le-ammo, the strength of His people. His anointed is the king (2:2; 20:6).

speech.text: Psalms 28
To You, LORD, I call; my rock, do not be deaf to me, or, if You are silent to me, I will become like those who go down to the pit.
Hear the sound of my pleas for mercy when I cry to You for help, when I lift up my hands toward Your holy inner sanctuary.
Do not drag me away with the wicked, with those who do iniquity, who speak peace with their neighbors while evil is in their hearts.
Give to them according to their work and according to the evil of their deeds; give to them according to the work of their hands; pay them back what they deserve.
Because they do not consider the deeds of the LORD or the work of His hands, He will tear them down and not build them up.
Blessed be the LORD, for He has heard the sound of my pleas for mercy.
The LORD is my strength and my shield; in Him my heart trusts, and I am helped; my heart exults, and with my song I give thanks to Him.
The LORD is their strength; He is the saving stronghold of His anointed.
Save Your people and bless Your inheritance; shepherd them and carry them forever.

chapters.title: The Voice of the LORD
chapters.html:
Psalms 29

A psalm of David.

1Ascribe to the LORD, you sons of God,
ascribe to the LORD glory and strength.

2Ascribe to the LORD the glory of His name;
bow down to the LORD in the splendor of holiness.

3The voice of the LORD is over the waters;
the God of glory thunders,
the LORD, over many waters.

4The voice of the LORD is in power;
the voice of the LORD is in majesty.

5The voice of the LORD breaks the cedars;
the LORD breaks the cedars of Lebanon.

6He makes them skip like a calf,
Lebanon and Sirion like a young wild ox.

7The voice of the LORD strikes out flames of fire.

8The voice of the LORD shakes the wilderness;
the LORD shakes the wilderness of Kadesh.

9The voice of the LORD makes the deer give birth
and strips the forests bare,
and in His temple all say, "Glory!"

10The LORD sat enthroned over the flood;
the LORD sits enthroned as King forever.

11The LORD will give strength to His people;
the LORD will bless His people with peace.

Notes

  • vv3–9 "The voice of the LORD" — qol YHWH, seven times, the seven peals of the thunderstorm. The storm rolls in from the Mediterranean (many waters), over the mountains of the north (Lebanon and Sirion), and into the southern wilderness (Kadesh).

The voice of the LORD is over the waters; the God of glory thunders, the LORD, over many waters.
The voice of the LORD is in power; the voice of the LORD is in majesty.
The voice of the LORD breaks the cedars; the LORD breaks the cedars of Lebanon.
He makes them skip like a calf, Lebanon and Sirion like a young wild ox.
The voice of the LORD strikes out flames of fire.
The voice of the LORD shakes the wilderness; the LORD shakes the wilderness of Kadesh.
The voice of the LORD makes the deer give birth and strips the forests bare, and in His temple all say, "Glory!"
