The LORD will give strength to His people; the LORD will bless His people with peace.

chapters.title: Joy Comes in the Morning
chapters.html:
Psalms 30

A psalm. A song at the dedication of the house. Of David.

1I will exalt You, LORD, for You have drawn me up
and have not let my enemies rejoice over me.

2LORD my God, I cried to You for help,
and You healed me.

3LORD, You brought up my soul from Sheol;
You kept me alive, so that I did not go down to the pit.

4Sing praise to the LORD, you His faithful ones,
and give thanks to the remembrance of His holiness.

5For His anger is for a moment,
His favor for a lifetime.
Weeping may lodge for the evening,
but at morning there is a shout of joy.

6As for me, I said in my ease,
"I will never be moved."

7LORD, by Your favor
You had set my mountain firm;
You hid Your face; I was dismayed.

8To You, LORD, I called,
and to the Lord I pleaded for mercy:

9"What profit is there in my blood,
if I go down to the pit?
Will the dust praise You?
Will it tell of Your faithfulness?

10Hear, LORD, and be gracious to me;
LORD, be my helper."

11You have turned my mourning into dancing for me;
You have loosed my sackcloth
and clothed me with gladness,

12so that my glory may sing praise to You and not be silent.
LORD my God, I will give thanks to You forever.

Notes

  • The title "A song at the dedication of the house" — chanukkat ha-bayit: perhaps David's own house (2 Samuel 5:11), or the site of the temple (1 Chronicles 22:1); later sung at the rededication of the temple, the feast of Hanukkah.

  • v11 "You have turned my mourning into dancing" — you will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will turn into joy (John 16:20; Jeremiah 31:13).

chapters.title: Into Your Hand I Commit My Spirit
chapters.html:
Psalms 31

For the director. A psalm of David.

1In You, LORD, I take refuge;
let me never be put to shame;
in Your righteousness rescue me.

2Incline Your ear to me;
deliver me quickly;
be a rock of refuge for me,
a strong fortress to save me.

3For You are my rock and my fortress;
for Your name's sake You lead me and guide me.

4You bring me out of the net they have hidden for me,
for You are my refuge.

5Into Your hand I commit my spirit;
You have redeemed me, LORD, God of truth.

6I hate those who hold to empty idols,
but I trust in the LORD.

7I will rejoice and be glad in Your loyal love,
because You have seen my affliction;
You have known the distress of my soul,

8and You have not handed me over to the enemy;
You have set my feet in a broad place.

9Be gracious to me, LORD, for I am in distress;
my eye wastes away with grief,
my soul and my body also.

10For my life is spent with sorrow,
and my years with sighing;
my strength stumbles because of my iniquity,
and my bones waste away.

11Because of all my adversaries I have become a reproach,
above all to my neighbors,
and a dread to those who know me;
those who see me in the street flee from me.

12I am forgotten like the dead, out of mind;
I have become like a broken vessel.

13For I hear the whispering of many,
terror on every side,
as they plot together against me,
as they scheme to take my life.

14But I trust in You, LORD;
I say, "You are my God."

15My times are in Your hand;
rescue me from the hand of my enemies and from those who pursue me.

16Make Your face shine on Your servant;
save me in Your loyal love.

17LORD, let me not be put to shame, for I call on You;
let the wicked be put to shame;
let them be silent in Sheol.

18Let the lying lips be mute,
which speak arrogantly against the righteous
in pride and contempt.

19How great is Your goodness,
which You have stored up for those who fear You
and worked for those who take refuge in You
in the sight of the children of man!

20In the shelter of Your presence You hide them
from the plots of men;
You keep them safe in Your shelter
from the strife of tongues.

21Blessed be the LORD,
for He has shown me the wonder of His loyal love
in a city under siege.

22As for me, I said in my alarm,
"I am cut off from Your sight."
But You heard the sound of my pleas for mercy
when I cried to You for help.

23Love the LORD, all you His faithful ones!
The LORD keeps the faithful
and repays in full the one who acts in pride.

24Be strong, and let your heart take courage,
all you who wait for the LORD!

Notes

  • v5 "Into Your hand I commit my spirit" — ruchi, the psalmist's own spirit, his life, placed in God's keeping. Jesus prayed these words on the cross, adding Father (Luke 23:46); Stephen prayed them to Jesus (Acts 7:59).

  • v22 "I am cut off from Your sight" — nigrazti, as Jonah said, I am driven away from Your sight (Jonah 2:4).

chapters.title: Blessed Is the One Whose Transgression Is Forgiven
chapters.html:
Psalms 32

Of David. A Maskil.

1Blessed is the one whose transgression is forgiven,
whose sin is covered.

2Blessed is the man to whom the LORD counts no iniquity,
and in whose spirit there is no deceit.

3When I kept silent, my bones wasted away
through my groaning all day long.

4For day and night Your hand was heavy on me;
my strength was dried up as by the heat of summer. Selah

5I made my sin known to You,
and I did not cover my iniquity;
I said, "I will confess my transgressions to the LORD,"
and You forgave the iniquity of my sin. Selah

6Therefore let everyone who is faithful pray to You
at a time when You may be found;
surely in the rush of great waters
they will not reach him.

7You are a hiding place for me;
You keep me from trouble;
You surround me with shouts of deliverance. Selah

8I will instruct you and teach you in the way you should go;
I will counsel you with My eye on you.

9Do not be like a horse or a mule, without understanding,
whose trappings must be bit and bridle to hold it in,
or it will not come near you.

10Many are the sorrows of the wicked,
but loyal love surrounds the one who trusts in the LORD.

11Be glad in the LORD and rejoice, you righteous;
shout for joy, all you upright in heart!

Notes

  • The psalm — the second of the seven penitential psalms (see 6).

  • vv1–2 "Blessed is the one whose transgression is forgiven" — three words for sin (pesha, transgression; chata'ah, sin; avon, iniquity) and three for forgiveness (forgiven, nesui, lifted away; covered; not counted). Paul quotes the verses of righteousness counted apart from works (Romans 4:6–8).

I will instruct you and teach you in the way you should go; I will counsel you with My eye on you.

Many are the sorrows of the wicked, but loyal love surrounds the one who trusts in the LORD.

chapters.title: Sing to Him a New Song
chapters.html:
Psalms 33

1Shout for joy in the LORD, you righteous;
praise is fitting for the upright.

2Give thanks to the LORD with the lyre;
make music to Him with the ten-stringed harp.

3Sing to Him a new song;
play skillfully, with shouts of joy.

4For the word of the LORD is upright,
and all His work is done in faithfulness.

5He loves righteousness and justice;
the earth is full of the loyal love of the LORD.

6By the word of the LORD the heavens were made,
and by the breath of His mouth all their host.

7He gathers the waters of the sea as a heap;
He puts the deeps in storehouses.

8Let all the earth fear the LORD;
let all the inhabitants of the world stand in awe of Him.

9For He spoke, and it came to be;
He commanded, and it stood firm.

10The LORD brings the counsel of the nations to nothing;
He frustrates the plans of the peoples.

11The counsel of the LORD stands forever,
the plans of His heart to all generations.

12Blessed is the nation whose God is the LORD,
the people He has chosen as His inheritance.

13The LORD looks down from heaven;
He sees all the children of man;

14from the place where He sits enthroned He looks out
on all the inhabitants of the earth,

15He who forms the hearts of them all
and understands all their deeds.

16The king is not saved by his great army;
a warrior is not rescued by his great strength.

17The horse is a false hope for victory,
and by its great might it cannot rescue.

18The eye of the LORD is on those who fear Him,
on those who hope in His loyal love,

19to deliver their soul from death
and keep them alive in famine.

20Our soul waits for the LORD;
He is our help and our shield.

21For our heart is glad in Him,
because we trust in His holy name.

22Let Your loyal love, LORD, be upon us,
even as we hope in You.

Notes

  • v6 "By the word of the LORD the heavens were made" — And God said… and it was so (Genesis 1:6–9). The breath of His mouth is ruach piv: the Church Fathers read the verse of the Word and the Spirit together at creation (Genesis 1:2; John 1:1–3).

chapters.title: Taste and See
chapters.html:
Psalms 34

Of David, when he changed his behavior before Abimelech, who drove him out, and he went away.

1I will bless the LORD at all times;
His praise will always be in my mouth.

2My soul makes its boast in the LORD;
let the humble hear and be glad.

3Magnify the LORD with me,
and let us exalt His name together.

4I sought the LORD, and He answered me
and delivered me from all my fears.

5Those who look to Him are radiant,
and their faces will never be ashamed.

6This poor man cried, and the LORD heard
and saved him out of all his troubles.

7The messenger of the LORD camps
around those who fear Him, and rescues them.

8Taste and see that the LORD is good;
blessed is the man who takes refuge in Him.

9Fear the LORD, you His holy ones,
for those who fear Him lack nothing.

10The young lions suffer want and hunger,
but those who seek the LORD lack no good thing.

11Come, children, listen to me;
I will teach you the fear of the LORD.

12Who is the man who desires life
and loves many days, to see good?

13Keep your tongue from evil
and your lips from speaking deceit.

14Turn away from evil and do good;
seek peace and pursue it.

15The eyes of the LORD are toward the righteous,
and His ears toward their cry.

16The face of the LORD is against those who do evil,
to cut off the memory of them from the earth.

17They cry, and the LORD hears
and delivers them out of all their troubles.

18The LORD is near to the brokenhearted
and saves the crushed in spirit.

19Many are the troubles of the righteous,
but the LORD delivers him out of them all.

20He keeps all his bones;
not one of them is broken.

21Evil will kill the wicked,
and those who hate the righteous will be held guilty.

22The LORD redeems the soul of His servants;
none who take refuge in Him will be held guilty.

Notes

  • The title "when he changed his behavior before Abimelech" — David's feigned madness before the king of Gath, called Achish in 1 Samuel 21:10–15. Abimelech, my father is king, may have been a royal title of the Philistine kings (Genesis 20:2; 26:1).

  • vv12–16 — quoted in full by Peter (1 Peter 3:10–12).

  • v20 "not one of them is broken" — quoted by John of Jesus on the cross, whose legs were not broken (John 19:36), with the law of the Passover lamb (Exodus 12:46).

chapters.title: Contend, LORD, with Those Who Contend with Me
chapters.html:
Psalms 35

Of David.

1Contend, LORD, with those who contend with me;
fight against those who fight against me.

2Take hold of shield and buckler
and rise up to help me.

3Draw out the spear and close the way against those who pursue me;
say to my soul, "I am your salvation."

4Let them be put to shame and disgraced
who seek my life;
let them be turned back and confounded
who devise evil against me.

5Let them be like chaff before the wind,
with the messenger of the LORD driving them on.

6Let their way be dark and slippery,
with the messenger of the LORD pursuing them.

7For without cause they hid their net for me;
without cause they dug a pit for my soul.

8Let ruin come on him when he does not know it,
and let the net he hid catch him;
let him fall into it, to his ruin.

9My soul will rejoice in the LORD,
exulting in His salvation.

10All my bones will say,
"LORD, who is like You,
who rescues the poor from one too strong for him,
the poor and needy from the one who robs him?"

11Violent witnesses rise up;
they ask me of things I do not know.

12They repay me evil for good;
my soul is bereaved.

13But I, when they were sick, was clothed in sackcloth;
I afflicted my soul with fasting,
and my prayer returned to my own bosom.

14I went about as for my friend or my brother;
as one who mourns for his mother, I bowed down in mourning.

15But at my stumbling they rejoiced and gathered;
they gathered against me, the lame I did not know;
they tore at me and did not stop.

16Like godless mockers at a feast,
they gnash their teeth at me.

17Lord, how long will You look on?
Bring back my soul from their ruin,
my only life from the young lions.

18I will give You thanks in the great congregation;
among a mighty people I will praise You.

19Let not those who are my enemies without reason rejoice over me,
nor those who hate me without cause wink the eye.

20For they do not speak peace,
but against the quiet ones of the land
they devise words of deceit.

21They open their mouths wide against me;
they say, "Aha, aha! Our eyes have seen it!"

22You have seen, LORD; do not keep silent!
Lord, do not be far from me!

23Wake up and rouse Yourself for my right,
my God and my Lord, for my cause!

24Vindicate me, LORD my God, according to Your righteousness,
and let them not rejoice over me.

25Let them not say in their hearts, "Aha, our desire!"
Let them not say, "We have swallowed him up."

26Let them be put to shame and confounded together
who rejoice at my trouble;
let them be clothed with shame and disgrace
who make themselves great against me.

27Let those who delight in my righteousness shout for joy and be glad,
and say always, "Great is the LORD,
who delights in the peace of His servant!"

28Then my tongue will tell of Your righteousness,
of Your praise all the day long.

Notes

  • v19 "those who hate me without cause" — sone'ai chinnam, quoted by Jesus of Himself: They hated Me without a cause (John 15:25; 69:4).

  • v23 "my God and my Lord" — Elohai va-Adonai; Thomas's confession of the risen Jesus, My Lord and my God (John 20:28).

chapters.title: In Your Light We See Light
chapters.html:
Psalms 36

For the director. Of the servant of the LORD, of David.

1Transgression speaks to the wicked
deep within my heart;
there is no fear of God
before his eyes.

2For he flatters himself in his own eyes
that his iniquity will not be found out and hated.

3The words of his mouth are trouble and deceit;
he has stopped acting wisely and doing good.

4He plots trouble on his bed;
he sets himself on a way that is not good;
he does not reject evil.

5LORD, Your loyal love is in the heavens,
Your faithfulness reaches to the clouds.

6Your righteousness is like the mountains of God;
Your judgments are a great deep;
man and beast You save, LORD.

7How precious is Your loyal love, God!
The children of man take refuge in the shadow of Your wings.

8They are filled with the abundance of Your house,
and You give them drink from the river of Your delights.

9For with You is the fountain of life;
in Your light we see light.

10Continue Your loyal love to those who know You,
and Your righteousness to the upright in heart.

11Let not the foot of pride come against me,
nor the hand of the wicked drive me away.

12There the doers of iniquity have fallen;
they are thrust down and cannot rise.

Notes

  • v1 "there is no fear of God before his eyes" — the last line of Paul's charge against all mankind (Romans 3:18).

  • v9 "in Your light we see light" — the Church has read it of the Son, light from light, the true light that gives light to everyone (John 1:4–9).

Transgression speaks to the wicked deep within my heart; there is no fear of God before his eyes.
For he flatters himself in his own eyes that his iniquity will not be found out and hated.

He plots trouble on his bed; he sets himself on a way that is not good; he does not reject evil.

For with You is the fountain of life; in Your light we see light.
Continue Your loyal love to those who know You, and Your righteousness to the upright in heart.

Psalms 37

Of David.

1Do not fret because of evildoers;
do not envy those who do wrong.

2For they will soon wither like the grass
and fade like the green plant.

3Trust in the LORD and do good;
dwell in the land and feed on faithfulness.

4Delight yourself in the LORD,
and He will give you the desires of your heart.

5Commit your way to the LORD;
trust in Him, and He will act.

6He will bring out your righteousness like the light,
and your justice like the noonday.

7Be still before the LORD and wait patiently for Him;
do not fret because of the one who prospers in his way,
because of the man who carries out his schemes.

8Refrain from anger and forsake wrath;
do not fret; it leads only to evil.

9For evildoers will be cut off,
but those who wait for the LORD will inherit the land.

10In a little while the wicked will be no more;
you will look carefully at his place, and he will not be there.

11But the humble will inherit the land
and delight themselves in abundant peace.

12The wicked plots against the righteous
and gnashes his teeth at him,

13but the Lord laughs at him,
for He sees that his day is coming.

14The wicked have drawn the sword and bent their bow
to bring down the poor and needy,
to slaughter those whose way is upright;

15their sword will enter their own heart,
and their bows will be broken.

16Better is the little that the righteous has
than the abundance of many wicked.

17For the arms of the wicked will be broken,
but the LORD upholds the righteous.

18The LORD knows the days of the blameless,
and their inheritance will last forever;

19they will not be put to shame in an evil time;
in days of famine they will be satisfied.

20But the wicked will perish;
the enemies of the LORD are like the glory of the pastures;
they vanish; like smoke they vanish away.

21The wicked borrows and does not repay,
but the righteous is gracious and gives;

22for those He blesses will inherit the land,
but those He curses will be cut off.

23The steps of a man are established by the LORD,
when He delights in his way;

24though he falls, he will not be cast down,
for the LORD holds his hand.

25I have been young, and now I am old,
yet I have not seen the righteous forsaken
or his children begging for bread.

26All day long he is gracious and lends,
and his children become a blessing.

27Turn away from evil and do good,
and you will dwell forever.

28For the LORD loves justice
and will not forsake His faithful ones.
They are kept forever,
but the children of the wicked will be cut off.

29The righteous will inherit the land
and dwell on it forever.

30The mouth of the righteous utters wisdom,
and his tongue speaks justice.

31The law of his God is in his heart;
his steps do not slip.

32The wicked watches for the righteous
and seeks to put him to death.

33The LORD will not leave him in his hand
or let him be condemned when he is judged.

34Wait for the LORD and keep His way,
and He will lift you up to inherit the land;
you will look on when the wicked are cut off.

35I have seen a wicked man, ruthless,
spreading himself like a green tree in its native soil.

36He passed away, and he was gone;
I sought him, and he could not be found.

37Watch the blameless and see the upright,
for there is a future for the man of peace.

38But transgressors will be destroyed together;
the future of the wicked will be cut off.

39The salvation of the righteous is from the LORD;
He is their stronghold in the time of trouble.

40The LORD helps them and rescues them;
He rescues them from the wicked and saves them,
because they take refuge in Him.

Notes

  • The psalm — an acrostic in pairs of verses, each pair beginning with the next letter of the alphabet: a wisdom psalm, like Proverbs, teaching patience while the wicked prosper (73).

  • vv9, 11, 22, 29, 34 "inherit the land" — five times, the promise to Abraham's children; v11 is the beatitude, Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth (Matthew 5:5).

chapters.title: Do Not Forsake Me, LORD
chapters.html:
Psalms 38

A psalm of David, to bring to remembrance.

1LORD, do not rebuke me in Your wrath,
nor discipline me in Your fury.

2For Your arrows have sunk into me,
and Your hand has come down on me.

3There is no soundness in my flesh because of Your indignation;
there is no peace in my bones because of my sin.

4For my iniquities have gone over my head;
like a heavy burden, they are too heavy for me.

5My wounds stink and fester
because of my folly.

6I am bent and bowed down greatly;
all the day I go about mourning.

7For my loins are filled with burning,
and there is no soundness in my flesh.

8I am numb and greatly crushed;
I groan because of the turmoil of my heart.

9Lord, all my longing is before You;
my sighing is not hidden from You.

10My heart throbs; my strength has left me,
and the light of my eyes, even that is gone from me.

11My friends and companions stand aloof from my affliction,
and my neighbors stand far off.

12Those who seek my life lay snares;
those who seek my harm speak of ruin
and plot deceit all day long.

13But I am like a deaf man; I do not hear,
like a mute who does not open his mouth.

14I have become like a man who does not hear,
in whose mouth are no rebukes.

15For in You, LORD, I hope;
You will answer, Lord my God.

16For I said, "Let them not rejoice over me,
who make themselves great against me when my foot slips."

17For I am ready to fall,
and my pain is always before me.

18I confess my iniquity;
I am troubled because of my sin.

19My enemies are alive and strong,
and many are those who hate me without reason.

20Those who repay evil for good
accuse me because I follow what is good.

21Do not forsake me, LORD;
my God, do not be far from me.

22Hurry to help me,
Lord, my salvation.

Notes

  • The psalm — the third of the penitential psalms (see 6). It opens with the words of 6:1.

chapters.title: A Guest with You
chapters.html:
Psalms 39

For the director: for Jeduthun. A psalm of David.

1I said, "I will guard my ways,
so that I do not sin with my tongue;
I will keep a muzzle on my mouth
while the wicked are in front of me."

2I was mute and silent;
I held my peace, to no good,
and my pain was stirred up.

3My heart grew hot within me;
as I mused, the fire burned;
then I spoke with my tongue:

4"LORD, make me know my end,
and what is the measure of my days;
let me know how fleeting I am.

5You have made my days a few handbreadths,
and my lifetime is as nothing before You.
Surely every man, even standing firm, is only a breath. Selah

6Surely a man walks about as a shadow;
surely for a breath they are in turmoil;
he heaps up, and does not know who will gather.

7Now, Lord, what do I wait for?
My hope is in You.

8Rescue me from all my transgressions;
do not make me the scorn of the fool.

9I am mute; I do not open my mouth,
for You are the one who has done it.

10Take away Your stroke from me;
I am worn out by the blows of Your hand.

11With rebukes for iniquity You discipline a man;
You consume like a moth what he holds dear;
surely every man is a breath. Selah

12Hear my prayer, LORD,
and listen to my cry;
do not be silent at my tears.
For I am a guest with You,
a resident, like all my fathers.

13Look away from me, that I may smile again,
before I go and am no more."

Notes

  • v12 "a guest with You, a resident" — ger and toshav: the land is Mine; for you are guests and residents with Me (Leviticus 25:23; 1 Chronicles 29:15; Hebrews 11:13).

chapters.title: I Delight to Do Your Will
chapters.html:
Psalms 40

For the director. Of David. A psalm.

1I waited patiently for the LORD;
He inclined to me and heard my cry.

2He drew me up from the pit of ruin,
out of the miry clay,
and set my feet on a rock,
making my steps secure.

3He put a new song in my mouth,
a song of praise to our God.
Many will see and fear,
and will trust in the LORD.

4Blessed is the man who makes the LORD his trust,
who does not turn to the proud,
to those who go astray after falsehood.

5You have done many things, LORD my God,
Your wonders and Your thoughts toward us;
none can compare with You.
If I would declare and speak of them,
they are more than can be counted.

6Sacrifice and offering You did not desire;
ears You have dug for me;
burnt offering and sin offering You did not ask for.

7Then I said, "Here I have come;
in the scroll of the book it is written of me.

8I delight to do Your will, my God;
Your law is within my inmost being."

9I have told the good news of righteousness in the great congregation;
I have not held back my lips,
as You know, LORD.

10I have not hidden Your righteousness within my heart;
I have spoken of Your faithfulness and Your salvation;
I have not concealed Your loyal love and Your truth
from the great congregation.

11As for You, LORD, do not hold back Your compassion from me;
let Your loyal love and Your truth always keep me.

12For evils without number have surrounded me;
my iniquities have overtaken me, and I cannot see;
they are more than the hairs of my head,
and my heart has failed me.

13Be pleased, LORD, to rescue me;
LORD, hurry to help me.

14Let them be put to shame and confounded together
who seek my life to sweep it away;
let them be turned back and disgraced
who delight in my harm.

15Let them be appalled because of their shame
who say to me, "Aha, aha!"

16But let all who seek You
rejoice and be glad in You;
let those who love Your salvation
say always, "Great is the LORD!"

17As for me, I am poor and needy,
but the Lord thinks of me.
You are my help and my deliverer;
my God, do not delay.

Notes

  • v6 "ears You have dug for me" — oznayim karita li: God has opened the psalmist's ears to hear and obey, which He wants more than sacrifice (1 Samuel 15:22; Isaiah 50:5). The Greek reads a body You have prepared for me, and Hebrews 10:5–7 quotes the Greek of vv6–8 as the words of Christ coming into the world.

  • v7 "Here I have come; in the scroll of the book it is written of me" — the obedient servant presents himself; the scroll may be the law that the king was to copy and keep (Deuteronomy 17:18–19).

  • vv13–17 — repeated, with small differences, as Psalm 70.

I waited patiently for the LORD; He inclined to me and heard my cry.
He drew me up from the pit of ruin, out of the miry clay, and set my feet on a rock, making my steps secure.
He put a new song in my mouth, a song of praise to our God. Many will see and fear, and will trust in the LORD.
Blessed is the man who makes the LORD his trust, who does not turn to the proud, to those who go astray after falsehood.

But let all who seek You rejoice and be glad in You; let those who love Your salvation say always, "Great is the LORD!"
As for me, I am poor and needy, but the Lord thinks of me. You are my help and my deliverer; my God, do not delay.

chapters.title: Blessed Is the One Who Considers the Poor
chapters.html:
Psalms 41

For the director. A psalm of David.

1Blessed is the one who considers the poor;
in the day of trouble the LORD delivers him;

2the LORD keeps him and keeps him alive;
he is called blessed in the land;
You do not give him up to the will of his enemies.

3The LORD sustains him on his sickbed;
in his illness You turn over all his bed.

4As for me, I said, "LORD, be gracious to me;
heal my soul, for I have sinned against You."

5My enemies speak evil of me:
"When will he die, and his name perish?"

6If one comes to see me, he speaks emptiness;
his heart gathers trouble for itself;
he goes out and speaks of it.

7All who hate me whisper together against me;
they plot harm against me:

8"A thing of worthlessness is poured into him;
now that he lies down, he will not rise again."

9Even the man of my peace, in whom I trusted,
who ate my bread, has lifted up his heel against me.

10But You, LORD, be gracious to me and raise me up,
so that I may repay them.

11By this I know that You delight in me:
my enemy does not shout in triumph over me.

12As for me, You uphold me in my integrity
and set me before Your face forever.

13Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel,
from everlasting to everlasting.
Amen and Amen.

Notes

  • v9 "the man of my peace… has lifted up his heel against me" — ish shelomi, a trusted friend, as Ahithophel was to David (2 Samuel 15:12). Jesus quotes the verse of Judas, He who ate My bread has lifted his heel against Me (John 13:18).

  • v13 "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel… Amen and Amen" — the doxology that closes the first of the five books of the Psalms (1–41); the others end at 72, 89, 106 and 150.

The LORD sustains him on his sickbed; in his illness You turn over all his bed.
As for me, I said, "LORD, be gracious to me; heal my soul, for I have sinned against You."
My enemies speak evil of me: "When will he die, and his name perish?"
If one comes to see me, he speaks emptiness; his heart gathers trouble for itself; he goes out and speaks of it.

By this I know that You delight in me: my enemy does not shout in triumph over me.

chapters.title: As a Deer Longs for Streams of Water
chapters.html:
Psalms 42

For the director. A Maskil of the sons of Korah.

1As a deer longs for streams of water,
so my soul longs for You, God.

2My soul thirsts for God, for the living God.
When shall I come and appear before God?

3My tears have been my bread day and night,
while they say to me all day long,
"Where is your God?"

4These things I remember as I pour out my soul within me:
how I would pass along with the throng
and lead them in procession to the house of God,
with the sound of shouts of joy and thanksgiving,
a multitude keeping the feast.

5Why are you bowed down, my soul,
and why are you in turmoil within me?
Hope in God, for I will yet praise Him
for the salvation of His presence.

6My God, my soul is bowed down within me;
therefore I remember You
from the land of the Jordan and the Hermons,
from Mount Mizar.

7Deep calls to deep
at the roar of Your waterfalls;
all Your breakers and Your waves
have gone over me.

8By day the LORD commands His loyal love,
and at night His song is with me,
a prayer to the God of my life.

9I will say to God my rock,
"Why have You forgotten me?
Why do I go about mourning
because of the oppression of the enemy?"

10As with a shattering in my bones, my adversaries taunt me,
while they say to me all day long,
"Where is your God?"

11Why are you bowed down, my soul,
and why are you in turmoil within me?
Hope in God, for I will yet praise Him,
the salvation of my face and my God.

Notes

  • v1 and the second book of the Psalms (42–72) — in these psalms God is mostly called Elohim, God, where the first book has YHWH, the LORD.

  • v5 and Psalm 43 — Psalms 42 and 43 are one poem in three parts, with the same refrain (42:5, 11; 43:5); Psalm 43 has no title, and many Hebrew manuscripts join the two.

speech.text: Psalms 42
As a deer longs for streams of water, so my soul longs for You, God.
My soul thirsts for God, for the living God. When shall I come and appear before God?
My tears have been my bread day and night, while they say to me all day long, "Where is your God?"

These things I remember as I pour out my soul within me: how I would pass along with the throng and lead them in procession to the house of God, with the sound of shouts of joy and thanksgiving, a multitude keeping the feast.
Why are you bowed down, my soul, and why are you in turmoil within me? Hope in God, for I will yet praise Him for the salvation of His presence.
My God, my soul is bowed down within me; therefore I remember You from the land of the Jordan and the Hermons, from Mount Mizar.
Deep calls to deep at the roar of Your waterfalls; all Your breakers and Your waves have gone over me.
By day the LORD commands His loyal love, and at night His song is with me, a prayer to the God of my life.
I will say to God my rock, "Why have You forgotten me? Why do I go about mourning because of the oppression of the enemy?"
As with a shattering in my bones, my adversaries taunt me, while they say to me all day long, "Where is your God?"
Why are you bowed down, my soul, and why are you in turmoil within me? Hope in God, for I will yet praise Him, the salvation of my face and my God.

chapters.title: Send Out Your Light and Your Truth
chapters.html:
Psalms 43

1Vindicate me, God, and plead my cause
against an unfaithful nation;
from the man of deceit and injustice rescue me.

2For You are the God of my stronghold;
why have You rejected me?
Why do I go about mourning
because of the oppression of the enemy?

3Send out Your light and Your truth; let them lead me;
let them bring me to Your holy mountain
and to Your dwellings.

4Then I will come to the altar of God,
to God, my exceeding joy,
and I will praise You with the lyre,
God, my God.

5Why are you bowed down, my soul,
and why are you in turmoil within me?
Hope in God, for I will yet praise Him,
the salvation of my face and my God.

Notes

  • The psalm — the third part of the poem begun in Psalm 42 (see the note there); it has no title of its own.

speech.text: Psalms 43

For You are the God of my stronghold; why have You rejected me? Why do I go about mourning because of the oppression of the enemy?
Send out Your light and Your truth; let them lead me; let them bring me to Your holy mountain and to Your dwellings.
Then I will come to the altar of God, to God, my exceeding joy, and I will praise You with the lyre, God, my God.

chapters.title: For Your Sake We Are Killed All Day Long
chapters.html:
Psalms 44

For the director. Of the sons of Korah. A Maskil.

1God, we have heard with our ears;
our fathers have told us
the work You did in their days,
in the days of old.

2You with Your own hand drove out the nations,
but them You planted;
You afflicted the peoples,
but them You set free.

3For not by their own sword did they win the land,
nor did their own arm save them,
but Your right hand and Your arm
and the light of Your face,
for You delighted in them.

4You are my King, God;
command victories for Jacob.

5Through You we push back our foes;
through Your name we trample those who rise against us.

6For I do not trust in my bow,
and my sword does not save me.

7But You have saved us from our foes
and have put to shame those who hate us.

8In God we have boasted all day long,
and we will give thanks to Your name forever. Selah

9Yet You have rejected us and disgraced us
and do not go out with our armies.

10You make us turn back from the foe,
and those who hate us have taken plunder for themselves.

11You have given us like sheep to be eaten
and have scattered us among the nations.

12You sell Your people for nothing
and have made no profit by their price.

13You have made us a reproach to our neighbors,
the scorn and derision of those around us.

14You have made us a byword among the nations,
a shaking of the head among the peoples.

15All day long my disgrace is before me,
and the shame of my face has covered me

16at the voice of the one who taunts and reviles,
at the sight of the enemy and the avenger.

17All this has come on us, though we have not forgotten You
and have not been false to Your covenant.

18Our heart has not turned back,
nor have our steps strayed from Your path,

19that You should crush us in the place of jackals
and cover us with deep shadow.

20If we had forgotten the name of our God
or spread out our hands to a strange god,

21would not God search this out?
For He knows the secrets of the heart.

22Yet for Your sake we are killed all day long;
we are counted as sheep for the slaughter.

23Wake up! Why do You sleep, Lord?
Rouse Yourself; do not reject us forever.

24Why do You hide Your face
and forget our affliction and our oppression?

25For our soul is bowed down to the dust;
our body clings to the ground.

26Rise up; come to our help,
and redeem us for the sake of Your loyal love.

Notes

  • v4 "command victories for Jacob" — the Hebrew has You are He, my King, God; command; the Greek reads my God, who commands.

  • v22 "for Your sake we are killed all day long" — Paul quotes the verse of Christ's people in their sufferings, and answers: in all these things we are more than conquerors through Him who loved us (Romans 8:36–37).

speech.text: Psalms 44
God, we have heard with our ears; our fathers have told us the work You did in their days, in the days of old.
You with Your own hand drove out the nations, but them You planted; You afflicted the peoples, but them You set free.
For not by their own sword did they win the land, nor did their own arm save them, but Your right hand and Your arm and the light of Your face, for You delighted in them.
You are my King, God; command victories for Jacob.
Through You we push back our foes; through Your name we trample those who rise against us.
For I do not trust in my bow, and my sword does not save me.
But You have saved us from our foes and have put to shame those who hate us.
In God we have boasted all day long, and we will give thanks to Your name forever. Selah
Yet You have rejected us and disgraced us and do not go out with our armies.
You make us turn back from the foe, and those who hate us have taken plunder for themselves.
You have given us like sheep to be eaten and have scattered us among the nations.
You sell Your people for nothing and have made no profit by their price.
You have made us a reproach to our neighbors, the scorn and derision of those around us.
You have made us a byword among the nations, a shaking of the head among the peoples.
All day long my disgrace is before me, and the shame of my face has covered me
at the voice of the one who taunts and reviles, at the sight of the enemy and the avenger.
All this has come on us, though we have not forgotten You and have not been false to Your covenant.
Our heart has not turned back, nor have our steps strayed from Your path,
that You should crush us in the place of jackals and cover us with deep shadow.
If we had forgotten the name of our God or spread out our hands to a strange god,
would not God search this out? For He knows the secrets of the heart.
Yet for Your sake we are killed all day long; we are counted as sheep for the slaughter.
Wake up! Why do You sleep, Lord? Rouse Yourself; do not reject us forever.
Why do You hide Your face and forget our affliction and our oppression?
For our soul is bowed down to the dust; our body clings to the ground.
Rise up; come to our help, and redeem us for the sake of Your loyal love.

chapters.title: A Song for the King
chapters.html:
Psalms 45

For the director: on "Lilies." Of the sons of Korah. A Maskil. A love song.

1My heart overflows with a good word;
I speak my verses to the king;
my tongue is the pen of a skillful scribe.

2You are the most handsome of the sons of men;
grace is poured on your lips;
therefore God has blessed you forever.

3Gird your sword on your thigh, mighty one,
your splendor and your majesty.

4In your majesty ride on victoriously
for the cause of truth and humility and righteousness;
let your right hand teach you fearsome deeds.

5Your arrows are sharp;
peoples fall under you;
they fall in the heart of the king's enemies.

6Your throne, O God, is forever and ever;
the scepter of your kingdom is a scepter of uprightness.

7You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness;
therefore God, your God, has anointed you
with the oil of gladness above your companions.

8All your robes are myrrh and aloes and cassia;
from palaces of ivory, stringed instruments make you glad.

9Daughters of kings are among your honored women;
at your right hand stands the queen in gold of Ophir.

10Listen, daughter, and see, and incline your ear:
forget your people and your father's house,

11and the king will desire your beauty.
Since he is your lord, bow down to him.

12The daughter of Tyre will come with a gift;
the richest of the people will seek your favor.

13All glorious is the king's daughter within;
her clothing is woven with gold.

14In embroidered robes she is led to the king,
with the young women, her companions, following her;
they are brought to you.

15With joy and gladness they are led along;
they enter the palace of the king.

16In place of your fathers will be your sons;
you will make them princes in all the earth.

17I will make your name remembered in all generations;
therefore peoples will praise you forever and ever.

Notes

  • v6 "Your throne, O God, is forever and ever" — the king addressed as Elohim, God, as rulers are called gods in 82:6; the line may also be read Your throne is God's, forever and ever, or your divine throne. Hebrews 1:8–9 quotes vv6–7 of the Son: Your throne, O God, is forever and ever. The psalm is rendered as the Old Testament has it, with the king in lowercase.

  • v7 "God, your God, has anointed you" — the king anointed with the oil of gladness, above the other kings; Messiah means Anointed (2:2).

  • v17 "therefore peoples will praise you forever" — the Church has sung the psalm of Christ and His bride, the Church; the Ethiopian Church also sings it of the Virgin Mary, the queen at the King's right hand.

chapters.title: God Is Our Refuge and Strength
chapters.html:
Psalms 46

For the director. Of the sons of Korah. On Alamoth. A song.

1God is our refuge and strength,
a help in trouble, found very near.

2Therefore we will not fear though the earth gives way,
though the mountains slip into the heart of the seas,

3though its waters roar and foam,
though the mountains tremble at its swelling. Selah

4There is a river whose streams make glad the city of God,
the holy dwelling place of the Most High.

5God is within her; she will not be moved;
God will help her at the break of morning.

6Nations rage; kingdoms totter;
He lifts His voice; the earth melts.

7The LORD of hosts is with us;
the God of Jacob is our fortress. Selah

8Come, see the works of the LORD,
who has brought desolations on the earth.

9He makes wars cease to the end of the earth;
He breaks the bow and snaps the spear;
He burns the chariots with fire.

10"Be still, and know that I am God.
I will be exalted among the nations;
I will be exalted in the earth."

11The LORD of hosts is with us;
the God of Jacob is our fortress. Selah

Notes

  • v4 "There is a river" — Jerusalem had no river, only the spring of Gihon; the river is the river of God's presence, the river of Your delights (36:8; Ezekiel 47:1–12; Revelation 22:1–2).

  • vv7, 11 "The LORD of hosts is with us" — YHWH tseva'ot immanu: immanu, with us, the word of Immanuel, God with us (Isaiah 7:14; 8:8–10).

chapters.title: God Has Gone Up with a Shout
chapters.html:
Psalms 47

For the director. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.

1Clap your hands, all you peoples;
shout to God with the voice of joy.

2For the LORD, the Most High, is to be feared,
a great King over all the earth.

3He subdued peoples under us,
and nations under our feet.

4He chose our inheritance for us,
the pride of Jacob, whom He loves. Selah

5God has gone up with a shout,
the LORD with the sound of the horn.

6Sing praises to God, sing praises;
sing praises to our King, sing praises.

7For God is the King of all the earth;
sing praises with a Maskil.

8God reigns over the nations;
God sits on His holy throne.

9The nobles of the peoples have gathered
as the people of the God of Abraham.
For the shields of the earth belong to God;
He is highly exalted.

Notes

  • The psalm — a hymn to God as King of all the earth, perhaps sung as the ark was carried up to the temple (24:7–10; 2 Samuel 6:15).

For the LORD, the Most High, is to be feared, a great King over all the earth.

chapters.title: The City of the Great King
chapters.html:
Psalms 48

A song. A psalm of the sons of Korah.

1Great is the LORD and greatly to be praised
in the city of our God, His holy mountain.

2Beautiful in height, the joy of all the earth,
is Mount Zion, the heights of the north,
the city of the great King.

3In her citadels God
has made Himself known as a stronghold.

4For the kings assembled;
they came on together.

5They saw it, and they were astounded;
they were terrified; they fled in haste.

6Trembling took hold of them there,
anguish as of a woman in labor,

7as when the east wind
shatters the ships of Tarshish.

8As we have heard, so we have seen
in the city of the LORD of hosts, in the city of our God;
God will establish her forever. Selah

9We have pondered Your loyal love, God,
within Your temple.

10As Your name, God,
so Your praise reaches to the ends of the earth;
Your right hand is full of righteousness.

11Let Mount Zion be glad;
let the daughters of Judah rejoice
because of Your judgments.

12Walk around Zion, go all around her;
count her towers;

13set your heart on her ramparts;
go through her citadels,
so that you may tell the generation to come

14that this is God,
our God forever and ever;
He will guide us beyond death.

Notes

  • v2 "the heights of the north" — yarketei tsafon, the far north, where the mountain of the gods was said to stand in the old Canaanite poems (Isaiah 14:13); here Zion is that mountain. The city of the great King is quoted by Jesus (Matthew 5:35).

For the kings assembled; they came on together.

set your heart on her ramparts; go through her citadels, so that you may tell the generation to come

chapters.title: No Man Can Ransom Another
chapters.html:
Psalms 49

For the director. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.

1Hear this, all you peoples;
listen, all who live in the world,

2both low and high,
rich and poor together.

3My mouth will speak wisdom;
the meditation of my heart will be understanding.

4I will incline my ear to a proverb;
I will open my riddle on the lyre.

5Why should I fear in days of trouble,
when the iniquity of those who dog my heels surrounds me,

6those who trust in their wealth
and boast of the abundance of their riches?

7Truly no man can ransom his brother
or give to God the price of his life,

8for the ransom of their soul is costly,
and it must be given up forever,

9that he should live on forever
and never see the pit.

10For he sees that even the wise die;
the fool and the stupid alike perish
and leave their wealth to others.

11Their graves are their homes forever,
their dwellings to all generations,
though they named lands after themselves.

12Man in his splendor does not stay the night;
he is like the beasts that perish.

13This is the way of those who have foolish confidence,
and of those after them who approve their words. Selah

14Like sheep they are appointed for Sheol;
death will shepherd them,
and the upright will rule over them in the morning;
their form will waste away in Sheol, far from their dwelling.

15But God will ransom my soul from the hand of Sheol,
for He will take me. Selah

16Do not be afraid when a man becomes rich,
when the glory of his house increases.

17For when he dies he will take nothing away;
his glory will not go down after him.

18Though while he lives he counts his soul blessed,
and men praise you when you do well for yourself,

19he will go to the generation of his fathers,
who will never again see the light.

20Man in his splendor, without understanding,
is like the beasts that perish.

Notes

  • v11 "Their graves are their homes forever" — the Greek and Syriac read qivram, their graves; the Hebrew has qirbam, their inward thought: their inward thought is that their houses are forever. The witnesses are followed here.

  • v15 "for He will take me" — yiqqacheni, the verb used of Enoch, God took him (Genesis 5:24), and of Elijah (2 Kings 2:3): the hope of life with God beyond Sheol (73:24).

chapters.title: God Himself Is Judge
chapters.html:
Psalms 50

A psalm of Asaph.

1The Mighty One, God, the LORD, has spoken
and summoned the earth
from the rising of the sun to its setting.

2Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty,
God shines out.

3Our God comes and does not keep silent;
before Him is a devouring fire,
and around Him a mighty storm.

4He calls to the heavens above
and to the earth, to judge His people:

5"Gather to Me My faithful ones,
who made a covenant with Me by sacrifice."

6The heavens declare His righteousness,
for God Himself is judge. Selah

7"Hear, My people, and I will speak;
Israel, I will testify against you.
I am God, your God.

8Not for your sacrifices do I rebuke you;
your burnt offerings are always before Me.

9I will not take a bull from your house
or goats from your folds.

10For every beast of the forest is Mine,
the cattle on a thousand hills.

11I know every bird of the mountains,
and all that moves in the field is Mine.

12If I were hungry, I would not tell you,
for the world and all that fills it are Mine.

13Do I eat the flesh of bulls
or drink the blood of goats?

14Offer to God a sacrifice of thanksgiving,
and pay your vows to the Most High,

15and call on Me in the day of trouble;
I will rescue you, and you will glorify Me."

16But to the wicked God says:
"What right have you to recite My statutes
or take My covenant on your lips?

17For you hate discipline
and throw My words behind you.

18When you see a thief, you are pleased with him,
and your portion is with adulterers.

19You let your mouth loose for evil,
and your tongue weaves deceit.

20You sit and speak against your brother;
you slander your own mother's son.

21These things you have done, and I kept silent;
you thought I was altogether like you.
I will rebuke you and set it out before your eyes.

22Understand this, you who forget God,
or I will tear you apart, and there will be no one to rescue.

23The one who offers thanksgiving as his sacrifice glorifies Me;
to the one who sets his way aright
I will show the salvation of God."

Notes

  • v21 "you thought I was altogether like you" — heyot ehyeh khamokha, with ehyeh, the verb of God's name, I AM WHO I AM (Exodus 3:14): because God was silent, they thought Him no better than themselves.

chapters.title: Create in Me a Clean Heart
chapters.html:
Psalms 51

For the director. A psalm of David, when Nathan the prophet came to him, after he had gone in to Bathsheba.

1Be gracious to me, God, according to Your loyal love;
according to the greatness of Your compassion, blot out my transgressions.

2Wash me thoroughly from my iniquity,
and cleanse me from my sin.

3For I know my transgressions,
and my sin is always before me.

4Against You, You only, have I sinned
and done what is evil in Your sight,
so that You are right when You speak
and blameless when You judge.

5I was brought forth in iniquity,
and in sin my mother conceived me.

6You desire truth in the inward parts,
and in the hidden place You teach me wisdom.

7Purge me with hyssop, and I will be clean;
wash me, and I will be whiter than snow.

8Let me hear joy and gladness;
let the bones You have crushed rejoice.

9Hide Your face from my sins,
and blot out all my iniquities.

10Create in me a clean heart, God,
and renew a steadfast spirit within me.

11Do not cast me away from Your presence,
and do not take Your Holy Spirit from me.

12Restore to me the joy of Your salvation,
and uphold me with a willing spirit.

13Then I will teach transgressors Your ways,
and sinners will return to You.

14Deliver me from bloodguilt, God,
the God of my salvation,
and my tongue will sing aloud of Your righteousness.

15Lord, open my lips,
and my mouth will declare Your praise.

16For You do not delight in sacrifice, or I would give it;
You are not pleased with burnt offering.

17The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit;
a broken and crushed heart, God, You will not despise.

18Do good to Zion in Your good pleasure;
build the walls of Jerusalem.

19Then You will delight in sacrifices of righteousness,
in burnt offering and whole offering;
then bulls will be offered on Your altar.

Notes

  • The title — David's repentance after Nathan's parable (2 Samuel 12:1–13); the Hebrew title takes two verses, so the Hebrew numbers run two ahead. The fourth of the penitential psalms (see 6).

  • v10 "Create in me a clean heart" — bera, the verb of Genesis 1:1, used only of God's own work: a new creation (Ezekiel 36:26; 2 Corinthians 5:17).

  • v11 "Your Holy Spirit" — ruach qodshekha; one of only three places in the Old Testament with this name (Isaiah 63:10–11). David remembered Saul, from whom the Spirit departed (1 Samuel 16:14).

Wash me thoroughly from my iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin.

chapters.title: Like a Green Olive Tree
chapters.html:
Psalms 52

For the director. A Maskil of David, when Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul, "David has come to the house of Ahimelech."

1Why do you boast of evil, mighty man?
The loyal love of God endures all day long.

2Your tongue plots ruin,
like a sharpened razor, you worker of deceit.

3You love evil more than good,
lying more than speaking what is right. Selah

4You love all words that devour,
you deceitful tongue.

5God will also break you down forever;
He will snatch you and tear you away from your tent;
He will uproot you from the land of the living. Selah

6The righteous will see and fear,
and will laugh at him:

7"Here is the man who would not make God his stronghold,
but trusted in the abundance of his riches
and grew strong in his ruin."

8But I am like a green olive tree in the house of God;
I trust in the loyal love of God forever and ever.

9I will give thanks to You forever, because You have done it;
I will wait for Your name, for it is good, in the presence of Your faithful ones.

Notes

  • The title — Doeg the Edomite, Saul's chief herdsman, saw David at Nob and told Saul, and then killed the priests of Nob at Saul's command (1 Samuel 21:7; 22:9–19). The Hebrew title takes two verses.

speech.text: Psalms 52
Why do you boast of evil, mighty man? The loyal love of God endures all day long.
Your tongue plots ruin, like a sharpened razor, you worker of deceit.
You love evil more than good, lying more than speaking what is right. Selah
You love all words that devour, you deceitful tongue.
God will also break you down forever; He will snatch you and tear you away from your tent; He will uproot you from the land of the living. Selah
The righteous will see and fear, and will laugh at him:
"Here is the man who would not make God his stronghold, but trusted in the abundance of his riches and grew strong in his ruin."
But I am like a green olive tree in the house of God; I trust in the loyal love of God forever and ever.
I will give thanks to You forever, because You have done it; I will wait for Your name, for it is good, in the presence of Your faithful ones.

chapters.title: The Fool Says in His Heart
chapters.html:
Psalms 53

For the director: on Mahalath. A Maskil of David.

1The fool says in his heart, "There is no God."
They are corrupt; they do detestable injustice;
there is no one who does good.

2God looks down from heaven on the children of man,
to see if there is anyone who understands,
who seeks God.

3They have all fallen away; together they have become corrupt;
there is no one who does good,
not even one.

4Do they have no knowledge, those who do iniquity,
who eat up my people as they eat bread,
and do not call on God?

5There they are in great terror,
where there was no terror,
for God has scattered the bones of the one who camps against you;
you have put them to shame, for God has rejected them.

6Oh that the salvation of Israel would come out of Zion!
When God restores the fortunes of His people,
let Jacob rejoice, let Israel be glad.

Notes

  • The psalm — Psalm 14 again, as the second book of the Psalms has it: God (Elohim) for the LORD (YHWH), and other changes. The English is that of Psalm 14 where the Hebrew is the same, and differs where it differs.

speech.text: Psalms 53
The fool says in his heart, "There is no God." They are corrupt; they do detestable injustice; there is no one who does good.
God looks down from heaven on the children of man, to see if there is anyone who understands, who seeks God.
They have all fallen away; together they have become corrupt; there is no one who does good, not even one.
Do they have no knowledge, those who do iniquity, who eat up my people as they eat bread, and do not call on God?
There they are in great terror, where there was no terror, for God has scattered the bones of the one who camps against you; you have put them to shame, for God has rejected them.
Oh that the salvation of Israel would come out of Zion! When God restores the fortunes of His people, let Jacob rejoice, let Israel be glad.

chapters.title: God Is My Helper
chapters.html:
Psalms 54

For the director: with stringed instruments. A Maskil of David, when the Ziphites came and said to Saul, "Is not David hiding among us?"

1God, save me by Your name,
and vindicate me by Your might.

2God, hear my prayer;
listen to the words of my mouth.

3For strangers have risen against me,
and ruthless men seek my life;
they have not set God before them. Selah

4God is my helper;
the Lord is among those who uphold my life.

5He will repay the evil to my enemies;
in Your faithfulness put an end to them.

6With a freewill offering I will sacrifice to You;
I will give thanks to Your name, LORD, for it is good.

7For He has delivered me from every trouble,
and my eye has looked on my enemies.

Notes

  • The title — the men of Ziph, in the wilderness of Judah, twice betrayed David's hiding place to Saul (1 Samuel 23:19; 26:1). The Hebrew title takes two verses.

  • v5 "He will repay the evil" — the read form, yashiv; the written form yashuv, the evil will return.

speech.text: Psalms 54
God, save me by Your name, and vindicate me by Your might.
God, hear my prayer; listen to the words of my mouth.
For strangers have risen against me, and ruthless men seek my life; they have not set God before them. Selah
God is my helper; the Lord is among those who uphold my life.
He will repay the evil to my enemies; in Your faithfulness put an end to them.
With a freewill offering I will sacrifice to You; I will give thanks to Your name, LORD, for it is good.
For He has delivered me from every trouble, and my eye has looked on my enemies.

chapters.title: Oh That I Had Wings Like a Dove
chapters.html:
Psalms 55

For the director: with stringed instruments. A Maskil of David.

1Give ear to my prayer, God,
and do not hide Yourself from my plea.

2Attend to me and answer me;
I am restless in my complaint, and I moan,

3because of the voice of the enemy,
because of the pressure of the wicked;
for they bring down trouble on me,
and in anger they bear a grudge against me.

4My heart writhes within me;
the terrors of death have fallen on me.

5Fear and trembling come on me,
and horror covers me.

6I said, "Oh that I had wings like a dove!
I would fly away and be at rest;

7I would wander far away;
I would lodge in the wilderness; Selah

8I would hurry to my place of refuge
from the raging wind and the storm."

9Swallow them up, Lord; divide their tongues,
for I see violence and strife in the city.

10Day and night they go around it on its walls,
and iniquity and trouble are within it;

11ruin is within it;
oppression and deceit do not depart from its square.

12For it is not an enemy who taunts me,
or I could bear it;
it is not one who hates me who exalts himself against me,
or I could hide from him.

13But it is you, a man of my own rank,
my companion, my familiar friend.

14We used to share sweet counsel together;
we walked in the house of God with the throng.

15Let death come on them by surprise;
let them go down alive to Sheol,
for evil is in their lodging, within them.

16As for me, I call to God,
and the LORD will save me.

17Evening and morning and at noon
I complain and moan,
and He hears my voice.

18He redeems my soul in peace
from the battle against me,
for many are with me.

19God will hear and humble them,
He who sits enthroned from of old, Selah
those who have no changes
and do not fear God.

20He stretched out his hand against those at peace with him;
he broke his covenant.

21His speech was smoother than butter,
but war was in his heart;
his words were softer than oil,
but they were drawn swords.

22Cast your burden on the LORD,
and He will sustain you;
He will never let the righteous be moved.

23But You, God, will bring them down
to the pit of destruction;
men of bloodshed and deceit
will not live out half their days.
But I will trust in You.

Notes

  • vv12–14 "it is not an enemy who taunts me… but it is you" — the betrayal by a close friend, as Ahithophel betrayed David (2 Samuel 15:12, 31); compare 41:9.

  • v15 "Let death come on them by surprise" — the read form, yashi mavet; the written form joins the words, yeshimot, desolations. Go down alive to Sheol as Korah's company did (Numbers 16:30–33). Their lodging is megurim, from gur, the place where one lives as a guest.

Give ear to my prayer, God, and do not hide Yourself from my plea.

For it is not an enemy who taunts me, or I could bear it; it is not one who hates me who exalts himself against me, or I could hide from him.
But it is you, a man of my own rank, my companion, my familiar friend.
We used to share sweet counsel together; we walked in the house of God with the throng.

As for me, I call to God, and the LORD will save me.

He redeems my soul in peace from the battle against me, for many are with me.

He stretched out his hand against those at peace with him; he broke his covenant.
His speech was smoother than butter, but war was in his heart; his words were softer than oil, but they were drawn swords.

chapters.title: In God I Trust
chapters.html:
Psalms 56

For the director: on "The Silent Dove of Far Places." Of David. A Miktam, when the Philistines seized him in Gath.

1Be gracious to me, God, for man tramples on me;
all day long the fighter presses me.

2My enemies trample on me all day long,
for many fight against me proudly.

3On the day I am afraid,
I trust in You.

4In God, whose word I praise,
in God I trust; I will not be afraid.
What can flesh do to me?

5All day long they twist my words;
all their thoughts are against me for evil.

6They stir up strife; they lurk;
they watch my heels,
as they have waited for my life.

7For their iniquity, will they escape?
In anger bring down the peoples, God.

8You have counted my wanderings;
put my tears in Your flask.
Are they not in Your book?

9Then my enemies will turn back
on the day I call.
This I know, that God is for me.

10In God, whose word I praise,
in the LORD, whose word I praise,

11in God I trust; I will not be afraid.
What can man do to me?

12Your vows are on me, God;
I will pay thank offerings to You.

13For You have delivered my soul from death,
and my feet from stumbling,
so that I may walk before God
in the light of the living.

Notes

  • v9 "God is for me" — Elohim li; If God is for us, who can be against us? (Romans 8:31).

speech.text: Psalms 56
Be gracious to me, God, for man tramples on me; all day long the fighter presses me.
My enemies trample on me all day long, for many fight against me proudly.
On the day I am afraid, I trust in You.
In God, whose word I praise, in God I trust; I will not be afraid. What can flesh do to me?
All day long they twist my words; all their thoughts are against me for evil.
They stir up strife; they lurk; they watch my heels, as they have waited for my life.
For their iniquity, will they escape? In anger bring down the peoples, God.
You have counted my wanderings; put my tears in Your flask. Are they not in Your book?
Then my enemies will turn back on the day I call. This I know, that God is for me.
In God, whose word I praise, in the LORD, whose word I praise,
in God I trust; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?
Your vows are on me, God; I will pay thank offerings to You.
For You have delivered my soul from death, and my feet from stumbling, so that I may walk before God in the light of the living.

chapters.title: My Heart Is Steadfast
chapters.html:
Psalms 57

For the director: "Do Not Destroy." Of David. A Miktam, when he fled from Saul, in the cave.

1Be gracious to me, God, be gracious to me,
for in You my soul takes refuge;
in the shadow of Your wings I take refuge,
till the storms of ruin pass by.

2I call to God Most High,
to God who completes His work for me.

3He will send from heaven and save me;
He puts to shame the one who tramples on me. Selah
God will send out His loyal love and His truth.

4My soul is among lions;
I lie down among those who blaze,
the children of man, whose teeth are spears and arrows,
and their tongue a sharp sword.

5Be exalted above the heavens, God;
let Your glory be over all the earth.

6They prepared a net for my steps;
my soul was bowed down.
They dug a pit before me;
they have fallen into it themselves. Selah

7My heart is steadfast, God,
my heart is steadfast;
I will sing and make music.

8Wake up, my glory!
Wake up, harp and lyre!
I will wake the dawn.

9I will give thanks to You, Lord, among the peoples;
I will sing praises to You among the nations.

10For Your loyal love is great, reaching to the heavens,
and Your truth to the clouds.

11Be exalted above the heavens, God;
let Your glory be over all the earth.

Notes

  • vv7–11 — repeated as the first half of Psalm 108 (108:1–5).

speech.text: Psalms 57
Be gracious to me, God, be gracious to me, for in You my soul takes refuge; in the shadow of Your wings I take refuge, till the storms of ruin pass by.
I call to God Most High, to God who completes His work for me.
He will send from heaven and save me; He puts to shame the one who tramples on me. Selah God will send out His loyal love and His truth.

Be exalted above the heavens, God; let Your glory be over all the earth.
They prepared a net for my steps; my soul was bowed down. They dug a pit before me; they have fallen into it themselves. Selah
My heart is steadfast, God, my heart is steadfast; I will sing and make music.
Wake up, my glory! Wake up, harp and lyre! I will wake the dawn.
I will give thanks to You, Lord, among the peoples; I will sing praises to You among the nations.
For Your loyal love is great, reaching to the heavens, and Your truth to the clouds.
Be exalted above the heavens, God; let Your glory be over all the earth.

chapters.title: Surely There Is a God Who Judges
chapters.html:
Psalms 58

For the director: "Do Not Destroy." Of David. A Miktam.

1Do you indeed speak righteousness, you gods?
Do you judge the children of man uprightly?

2No, in your heart you work injustice;
on the earth you weigh out the violence of your hands.

3The wicked go astray from the womb;
they err from birth, speaking lies.

4They have venom like the venom of a snake,
like the deaf cobra that stops its ear,

5that does not hear the voice of the charmers
or the skilled caster of spells.

6God, break the teeth in their mouth;
tear out the fangs of the young lions, LORD.

7Let them melt away like water that runs off;
when he bends his arrows, let them be cut off.

8Let them be like the snail that dissolves as it goes,
like a woman's stillborn child, that never sees the sun.

9Before your pots feel the thorns,
whether green or burning, He will sweep them away.

10The righteous will rejoice when he sees the vengeance;
he will wash his feet in the blood of the wicked.

11Mankind will say, "Surely there is fruit for the righteous;
surely there is a God who judges on the earth."

Notes

  • v1 "you gods" — the Hebrew has elem, silence; read with other vowels as elim, gods, the rulers and judges who were to give justice in God's name (82:1, 6; Exodus 21:6). The Greek reads if indeed you speak righteousness.

speech.text: Psalms 58
Do you indeed speak righteousness, you gods? Do you judge the children of man uprightly?
No, in your heart you work injustice; on the earth you weigh out the violence of your hands.
The wicked go astray from the womb; they err from birth, speaking lies.
They have venom like the venom of a snake, like the deaf cobra that stops its ear,
that does not hear the voice of the charmers or the skilled caster of spells.
God, break the teeth in their mouth; tear out the fangs of the young lions, LORD.
Let them melt away like water that runs off; when he bends his arrows, let them be cut off.
Let them be like the snail that dissolves as it goes, like a woman's stillborn child, that never sees the sun.
Before your pots feel the thorns, whether green or burning, He will sweep them away.
The righteous will rejoice when he sees the vengeance; he will wash his feet in the blood of the wicked.
Mankind will say, "Surely there is fruit for the righteous; surely there is a God who judges on the earth."

chapters.title: God Is My Stronghold
chapters.html:
Psalms 59

For the director: "Do Not Destroy." Of David. A Miktam, when Saul sent men, and they watched the house to kill him.

1Deliver me from my enemies, my God;
set me on high, away from those who rise against me.

2Deliver me from those who do iniquity,
and save me from men of bloodshed.

3For they lie in wait for my life;
fierce men stir up strife against me,
not for my transgression or my sin, LORD.

4For no guilt of mine they run and make ready;
wake up to meet me, and see.

5You, LORD God of hosts, the God of Israel,
rouse Yourself to punish all the nations;
show no grace to any of the treacherous who do iniquity. Selah

6They return at evening;
they howl like dogs
and go around the city.

7They pour out words with their mouths;
swords are in their lips,
"for who hears?"

8But You, LORD, laugh at them;
You mock all the nations.

9My strength, I will watch for You,
for God is my stronghold.

10The God of my loyal love will come to meet me;
God will let me look on those who watch me.

11Do not kill them, or my people will forget;
make them wander by Your power and bring them down,
Lord, our shield.

12For the sin of their mouth, the word of their lips,
let them be caught in their pride,
for the cursing and the lies they tell.

13Consume them in wrath;
consume them till they are no more,
so that they may know that God rules in Jacob
to the ends of the earth. Selah

14They return at evening;
they howl like dogs
and go around the city.

15They wander about for food,
and if they are not satisfied, they stay all night.

16But I will sing of Your strength;
I will shout for joy at Your loyal love in the morning,
for You have been a stronghold for me
and a refuge in the day of my distress.

17My strength, I will sing praises to You,
for God is my stronghold,
the God of my loyal love.

Notes

  • v9 "My strength" — the Hebrew has uzzo, his strength; the Greek and some Hebrew manuscripts read uzzi, my strength, as in v17, followed here.

  • v10 "The God of my loyal love" — the read form, Elohei chasdi, as in v17, followed here; the written form has chasdo, the God of His loyal love.

Deliver me from my enemies, my God; set me on high, away from those who rise against me.
Deliver me from those who do iniquity, and save me from men of bloodshed.
For they lie in wait for my life; fierce men stir up strife against me, not for my transgression or my sin, LORD.
For no guilt of mine they run and make ready; wake up to meet me, and see.

chapters.title: With God We Will Do Valiantly
chapters.html:
Psalms 60

For the director: on "The Lily of Testimony." A Miktam of David, to teach; when he fought with Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah, and Joab returned and struck down twelve thousand of Edom in the Valley of Salt.

1God, You have rejected us; You have broken us;
You have been angry; restore us.

2You have made the land quake; You have split it open;
heal its breaches, for it totters.

3You have made Your people see hard things;
You have given us wine to drink that makes us reel.

4You have given a banner to those who fear You,
to rally to it because of the bow. Selah

5So that Your beloved ones may be rescued,
save with Your right hand, and answer me.

6God has spoken in His holiness:
"I will exult; I will divide Shechem
and measure out the Valley of Succoth.

7Gilead is Mine, and Manasseh is Mine;
Ephraim is the helmet of My head;
Judah is My scepter.

8Moab is My washbasin;
on Edom I throw My sandal;
Philistia, shout in triumph over Me!"

9Who will bring me to the fortified city?
Who will lead me to Edom?

10Have You not rejected us, God?
You do not go out, God, with our armies.

11Give us help against the foe,
for the salvation of man is worthless.

12With God we will do valiantly,
and He will trample our foes.

Notes

  • The title — David's wars against the Arameans and Edom (2 Samuel 8:3–14; 1 Chronicles 18:3–13). The Hebrew title takes two verses. To teach may mean it was to be learned by heart (Deuteronomy 31:19; 2 Samuel 1:18).

  • vv5–12 — repeated as the second half of Psalm 108 (108:6–13).

You have made the land quake; You have split it open; heal its breaches, for it totters.
You have made Your people see hard things; You have given us wine to drink that makes us reel.
You have given a banner to those who fear You, to rally to it because of the bow. Selah

chapters.title: The Rock That Is Higher Than I
chapters.html:
Psalms 61

For the director: on a stringed instrument. Of David.

1Hear my cry, God;
listen to my prayer.

2From the end of the earth I call to You
when my heart grows faint;
lead me to the rock that is higher than I,

3for You have been a refuge for me,
a strong tower against the enemy.

4Let me live as a guest in Your tent forever;
let me take refuge in the shelter of Your wings. Selah

5For You, God, have heard my vows;
You have given me the inheritance of those who fear Your name.

6Add days to the days of the king;
may his years be as generation after generation.

7May he sit enthroned forever before God;
appoint loyal love and truth to keep him.

8So I will sing praise to Your name forever,
as I pay my vows day after day.

Notes

  • v4 "Let me live as a guest in Your tent forever" — agurah, from gur, as the word table has it (15:1; 27:4–5).

speech.text: Psalms 61
Hear my cry, God; listen to my prayer.
From the end of the earth I call to You when my heart grows faint; lead me to the rock that is higher than I,
for You have been a refuge for me, a strong tower against the enemy.
Let me live as a guest in Your tent forever; let me take refuge in the shelter of Your wings. Selah
For You, God, have heard my vows; You have given me the inheritance of those who fear Your name.
Add days to the days of the king; may his years be as generation after generation.
May he sit enthroned forever before God; appoint loyal love and truth to keep him.
So I will sing praise to Your name forever, as I pay my vows day after day.

chapters.title: My Soul Waits in Silence
chapters.html:
Psalms 62

For the director: for Jeduthun. A psalm of David.

1For God alone my soul waits in silence;
from Him comes my salvation.

2He alone is my rock and my salvation,
my stronghold; I will not be greatly moved.

3How long will you rush at a man,
all of you, to batter him down,
like a leaning wall, a tottering fence?

4They only plan to push him down from his high place;
they take pleasure in lies.
They bless with their mouth,
but inwardly they curse. Selah

5For God alone, my soul, wait in silence,
for my hope is from Him.

6He alone is my rock and my salvation,
my stronghold; I will not be moved.

7On God rests my salvation and my glory;
my rock of strength, my refuge is in God.

8Trust in Him at all times, you people;
pour out your heart before Him;
God is a refuge for us. Selah

9The sons of men are only a breath;
the sons of men of rank are a lie;
in the scales they go up;
together they are lighter than a breath.

10Do not trust in oppression,
and put no empty hope in robbery;
if wealth increases, do not set your heart on it.

11God has spoken once;
twice I have heard this:
that power belongs to God,

12and loyal love belongs to You, Lord;
for You repay a man according to his work.

Notes

  • The psalm — akh, only, alone, surely, begins six of its lines (vv1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 9): God alone is to be trusted.

speech.text: Psalms 62
For God alone my soul waits in silence; from Him comes my salvation.
He alone is my rock and my salvation, my stronghold; I will not be greatly moved.
How long will you rush at a man, all of you, to batter him down, like a leaning wall, a tottering fence?
They only plan to push him down from his high place; they take pleasure in lies. They bless with their mouth, but inwardly they curse. Selah

chapters.title: My Soul Thirsts for You
chapters.html:
Psalms 63

A psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Judah.

1God, You are my God; I seek You early;
my soul thirsts for You;
my flesh longs for You,
in a dry and weary land without water.

2So I have looked on You in the sanctuary,
seeing Your power and Your glory.

3Because Your loyal love is better than life,
my lips will praise You.

4So I will bless You as long as I live;
in Your name I will lift up my hands.

5My soul will be satisfied as with fat and rich food,
and my mouth will praise You with joyful lips,

6when I remember You on my bed
and meditate on You in the watches of the night;

7for You have been my help,
and in the shadow of Your wings I sing for joy.

8My soul clings to You;
Your right hand holds me up.

9But those who seek my life to destroy it
will go down into the depths of the earth;

10they will be handed over to the power of the sword;
they will be a portion for jackals.

11But the king will rejoice in God;
all who swear by Him will boast,
for the mouths of those who speak lies will be stopped.

Notes

  • v1 "I seek You early" — ashachareka, from shachar, dawn: to seek at daybreak, and so earnestly. The Church has long sung the psalm at the morning prayer.

  • v8 "My soul clings to You" — daveqah, the word for a man holding fast to his wife (Genesis 2:24) and Israel to God (Deuteronomy 10:20).

speech.text: Psalms 63
God, You are my God; I seek You early; my soul thirsts for You; my flesh longs for You, in a dry and weary land without water.
So I have looked on You in the sanctuary, seeing Your power and Your glory.
Because Your loyal love is better than life, my lips will praise You.
So I will bless You as long as I live; in Your name I will lift up my hands.
My soul will be satisfied as with fat and rich food, and my mouth will praise You with joyful lips,
when I remember You on my bed and meditate on You in the watches of the night;
for You have been my help, and in the shadow of Your wings I sing for joy.
My soul clings to You; Your right hand holds me up.
But those who seek my life to destroy it will go down into the depths of the earth;
they will be handed over to the power of the sword; they will be a portion for jackals.
But the king will rejoice in God; all who swear by Him will boast, for the mouths of those who speak lies will be stopped.

chapters.title: God Shoots His Arrow
chapters.html:
Psalms 64

For the director. A psalm of David.

1Hear my voice, God, in my complaint;
keep my life from the dread of the enemy.

2Hide me from the secret plotting of evildoers,
from the throng of those who do iniquity,

3who sharpen their tongue like a sword
and aim bitter words like arrows,

4to shoot in hiding at the blameless,
shooting at him suddenly, without fear.

5They hold fast to their evil plan;
they talk of hiding snares;
they say, "Who will see them?"

6They search out injustices:
"We have finished a well-searched plan!"
For the inner man and the heart are deep.

7But God shoots His arrow at them;
suddenly they are wounded.

8They are made to stumble; their own tongue is against them;
all who see them shake their heads.

9Then all mankind fears;
they tell what God has done
and ponder His work.

10Let the righteous rejoice in the LORD
and take refuge in Him;
let all the upright in heart give praise.

Notes

  • vv7–8 — the reversal: God shoots His arrow at those who shot their arrows (v3), and their tongues, their weapons, bring them down (7:15–16).
