chapters.title: You Crown the Year with Your Goodness
chapters.html:
Psalms 65

For the director. A psalm of David. A song.

1To You, God, silence is praise in Zion,
and to You vows will be paid.

2You who hear prayer,
to You all flesh will come.

3Iniquities prevail against me;
our transgressions, You atone for them.

4Blessed is the one You choose and bring near
to dwell in Your courts.
We will be satisfied with the goodness of Your house,
the holiness of Your temple.

5By fearsome deeds You answer us in righteousness,
God of our salvation,
the trust of all the ends of the earth
and of the farthest seas,

6who by His strength set the mountains firm,
being girded with might,

7who stills the roaring of the seas,
the roaring of their waves,
and the tumult of the peoples,

8so that those who live at the ends of the earth are in awe of Your signs;
You make the gates of the morning and the evening shout for joy.

9You visit the earth and water it;
You greatly enrich it;
the river of God is full of water;
You provide their grain,
for so You have prepared it.

10You water its furrows abundantly,
settling its ridges;
You soften it with showers
and bless its growth.

11You crown the year with Your goodness,
and Your tracks drip with plenty.

12The pastures of the wilderness drip,
and the hills are girded with joy;

13the meadows are clothed with flocks,
and the valleys are covered with grain;
they shout for joy; they also sing.

Notes

  • v1 "To You, God, silence is praise" — lekha dumiyyah tehillah: the silent awe of the worshiper is itself praise (62:1). The Greek reads dommiyah, praise is fitting for You.

  • v3 "You atone for them" — tekhapperem, the word of the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16:30): God Himself covers the sins.

chapters.title: Come and See What God Has Done
chapters.html:
Psalms 66

For the director. A song. A psalm.

1Shout for joy to God, all the earth;

2sing the glory of His name;
make His praise glorious.

3Say to God, "How fearsome are Your deeds!
Because of the greatness of Your power, Your enemies come cringing to You.

4All the earth bows down to You
and sings praises to You;
they sing praises to Your name." Selah

5Come and see the works of God,
fearsome in His deeds toward the children of man.

6He turned the sea into dry land;
they passed through the river on foot;
there we rejoiced in Him,

7who rules by His might forever,
whose eyes keep watch over the nations;
let not the rebellious exalt themselves. Selah

8Bless our God, you peoples,
and let the sound of His praise be heard,

9who has set our soul among the living
and has not let our feet slip.

10For You, God, have tested us;
You have refined us as silver is refined.

11You brought us into the net;
You laid a heavy burden on our loins;

12You let men ride over our heads;
we went through fire and through water,
but You brought us out to abundance.

13I will enter Your house with burnt offerings;
I will pay You my vows,

14which my lips uttered
and my mouth spoke when I was in trouble.

15I will offer You burnt offerings of fat animals,
with the smoke of rams;
I will offer bulls with goats. Selah

16Come and hear, all you who fear God,
and I will tell what He has done for my soul.

17I cried to Him with my mouth,
and high praise was under my tongue.

18If I had regarded iniquity in my heart,
the Lord would not have heard.

19But truly God has heard;
He has attended to the voice of my prayer.

20Blessed be God,
who has not turned away my prayer
or His loyal love from me.

Notes

  • v6 "He turned the sea into dry land; they passed through the river on foot" — the crossing of the Red Sea and of the Jordan, the two great waters of the Exodus (Exodus 14:21–22; Joshua 3:14–17; 114:3).

chapters.title: Let the Peoples Praise You
chapters.html:
Psalms 67

For the director: with stringed instruments. A psalm. A song.

1May God be gracious to us and bless us
and make His face shine on us, Selah

2so that Your way may be known on the earth,
Your salvation among all nations.

3Let the peoples praise You, God;
let all the peoples praise You.

4Let the nations be glad and sing for joy,
for You judge the peoples with equity
and guide the nations on the earth. Selah

5Let the peoples praise You, God;
let all the peoples praise You.

6The earth has given its produce;
God, our God, blesses us.

7God blesses us;
let all the ends of the earth fear Him.

Notes

  • v1 "May God be gracious to us and bless us and make His face shine on us" — the priestly blessing of Numbers 6:24–26, The LORD bless you… make His face shine on you and be gracious to you, turned into the people's prayer.

  • v2 "so that Your way may be known on the earth" — Israel is blessed so that the nations may know God: the promise to Abraham, in you all the families of the earth shall be blessed (Genesis 12:2–3).

so that Your way may be known on the earth, Your salvation among all nations.
Let the peoples praise You, God; let all the peoples praise You.
Let the nations be glad and sing for joy, for You judge the peoples with equity and guide the nations on the earth. Selah

chapters.title: Let God Arise
chapters.html:
Psalms 68

For the director. Of David. A psalm. A song.

1Let God arise, let His enemies be scattered,
and let those who hate Him flee before Him.

2As smoke is driven away, drive them away;
as wax melts before fire,
let the wicked perish before God.

3But let the righteous be glad;
let them exult before God
and rejoice with gladness.

4Sing to God, sing praises to His name;
build up a highway for Him who rides through the deserts.
Yah is His name; exult before Him.

5A father of the fatherless and a defender of widows
is God in His holy dwelling.

6God gives the lonely a home to live in;
He leads prisoners out into prosperity,
but the rebellious live in a parched land.

7God, when You went out before Your people,
when You marched through the wasteland, Selah

8the earth shook, the heavens poured
before God, the One of Sinai,
before God, the God of Israel.

9You sent down a generous rain, God;
when Your inheritance was weary, You restored it.

10Your flock settled in it;
in Your goodness You provided for the poor, God.

11The Lord gives the word;
the women who bring the good news are a great army:

12"Kings of armies flee, they flee!"
while she who stays at home divides the spoil.

13Though you lie down among the sheepfolds —
the wings of a dove covered with silver,
its feathers with shimmering gold.

14When the Almighty scattered kings there,
it snowed on Zalmon.

15A mountain of God is Mount Bashan;
a mountain of many peaks is Mount Bashan.

16Why do you look with envy, mountains of many peaks,
at the mountain God has desired for His dwelling?
The LORD will dwell there forever.

17The chariots of God are twice ten thousand,
thousands upon thousands;
the Lord is among them, Sinai in the holy place.

18You went up on high;
You led captives away;
You received gifts among people,
even among the rebellious,
so that Yah God might dwell there.

19Blessed be the Lord;
day after day He bears our load,
God our salvation. Selah

20Our God is a God who saves,
and to GOD the Lord belong the ways out of death.

21Surely God will crush the head of His enemies,
the hairy crown of the one who goes on in his guilt.

22The Lord said, "I will bring them back from Bashan;
I will bring them back from the depths of the sea,

23so that you may plunge your foot in blood,
and the tongues of your dogs have their share of the enemies."

24Your processions are seen, God,
the processions of my God, my King, into the holy place.

25The singers go in front, the musicians last,
between them young women playing tambourines.

26Bless God in the great congregation;
bless the LORD, you who come from the fountain of Israel.

27There is Benjamin, the youngest, leading them,
the princes of Judah in their throng,
the princes of Zebulun, the princes of Naphtali.

28Your God has commanded your strength;
show Your strength, God, You who have acted for us.

29Because of Your temple at Jerusalem
kings will bring You gifts.

30Rebuke the beast among the reeds,
the herd of bulls with the calves of the peoples,
trampling on pieces of silver;
He has scattered the peoples who delight in war.

31Envoys will come from Egypt;
Cush will run to stretch out its hands to God.

32Kingdoms of the earth, sing to God;
sing praises to the Lord, Selah

33to Him who rides in the heavens, the ancient heavens;
listen: He sends out His voice, a mighty voice.

34Ascribe strength to God,
whose majesty is over Israel
and whose strength is in the skies.

35God is awesome from Your sanctuaries;
the God of Israel gives strength and power to the people.
Blessed be God.

Notes

  • v1 "Let God arise, let His enemies be scattered" — the words Moses spoke whenever the ark set out (Numbers 10:35). The psalm follows God's march from Sinai through the wilderness to His dwelling in Zion.

  • vv11–13 — some of the hardest lines in the Psalms. The women who announce the victory (v11) are like Miriam (Exodus 15:20–21); v13 may be a rebuke to tribes who stayed among the sheepfolds (Judges 5:16) or a picture of the spoil. The Hebrew is followed line by line.

  • v17 "Sinai in the holy place" — the Hebrew is followed. Many read ba mi-Sinai, "the Lord came from Sinai into the holy place," by dividing the letters differently (compare Deuteronomy 33:2).

  • v18 "You went up on high… You received gifts among people" — Ephesians 4:8 quotes this of Christ as "He gave gifts to people." The Aramaic Targum also reads "gave," and Paul follows that reading.

chapters.title: Save Me, God
chapters.html:
Psalms 69

For the director: on "Lilies." Of David.

1Save me, God,
for the waters have come up to my neck.

2I sink in deep mire
where there is no foothold;
I have come into deep waters,
and the flood sweeps over me.

3I am weary with my crying;
my throat is parched;
my eyes fail
while I wait for my God.

4More than the hairs of my head
are those who hate me without cause;
mighty are those who would destroy me,
my enemies for no reason.
What I did not steal —
must I now give it back?

5God, You know my folly,
and my guilt is not hidden from You.

6Let those who hope in You not be put to shame because of me,
Lord GOD of hosts;
let those who seek You not be disgraced because of me,
God of Israel.

7For it is for Your sake that I have borne reproach,
that disgrace has covered my face.

8I have become a stranger to my brothers,
a foreigner to my mother's sons.

9For zeal for Your house has consumed me,
and the reproaches of those who reproach You have fallen on me.

10When I wept and humbled my soul with fasting,
it became a reproach to me.

11When I made sackcloth my clothing,
I became a byword to them.

12Those who sit in the gate talk about me,
and the drinkers of strong drink make songs about me.

13But as for me, my prayer is to You, LORD,
at a time of favor;
God, in the abundance of Your loyal love,
answer me with Your faithful salvation.

14Rescue me from the mire,
and do not let me sink;
let me be rescued from those who hate me
and from the deep waters.

15Do not let the flood of waters sweep over me,
or the deep swallow me up,
or the pit close its mouth over me.

16Answer me, LORD, for Your loyal love is good;
in Your great compassion turn to me.

17Do not hide Your face from Your servant,
for I am in distress;
answer me quickly.

18Draw near to my soul and redeem it;
ransom me because of my enemies.

19You know my reproach,
my shame and my disgrace;
all my foes are before You.

20Reproach has broken my heart,
and I am sick.
I looked for sympathy, but there was none,
and for comforters, but I found none.

21They put poison in my food,
and for my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.

22Let their table before them become a snare,
and a trap for those at ease.

23Let their eyes be darkened so that they cannot see,
and make their loins shake continually.

24Pour out Your indignation on them,
and let Your burning anger overtake them.

25Let their camp be desolate;
let no one live in their tents.

26For they persecute the one You have struck,
and they tell of the pain of those You have wounded.

27Add guilt to their guilt;
let them not come into Your righteousness.

28Let them be blotted out of the book of the living
and not be written down with the righteous.

29But I am afflicted and in pain;
let Your salvation, God, set me on high.

30I will praise the name of God with a song
and magnify Him with thanksgiving.

31This will please the LORD more than an ox,
a bull with horns and hoofs.

32The humble will see it and be glad;
you who seek God, let your heart live.

33For the LORD listens to the needy
and does not despise His own who are prisoners.

34Let heaven and earth praise Him,
the seas and everything that moves in them.

35For God will save Zion
and build the cities of Judah;
they will live there and possess it.

36The offspring of His servants will inherit it,
and those who love His name will dwell in it.

Notes

  • v4 "those who hate me without cause" — Jesus applies this to Himself: They hated Me without a cause (John 15:25; also Psalm 35:19). The speaker stays lowercase here, as in the other psalms the New Testament reads of Christ.

  • v9 "zeal for Your house has consumed me" — the disciples remembered this when Jesus cleared the temple (John 2:17); the second line is quoted in Romans 15:3.

  • v21 "poison… vinegar" — rosh is a bitter, poisonous plant (Deuteronomy 29:18). At the cross Jesus was offered wine mixed with gall and then sour wine (Matthew 27:34, 48; John 19:28–30).

  • v25 "Let their camp be desolate" — Peter applies this to Judas (Acts 1:20), with "his" for "their."

chapters.title: Hurry to Help Me
chapters.html:
Psalms 70

For the director. Of David, to bring to remembrance.

1God, rescue me;
LORD, hurry to help me.

2Let them be put to shame and confounded
who seek my life;
let them be turned back and disgraced
who delight in my harm.

3Let them turn back because of their shame
who say, "Aha, aha!"

4But let all who seek You
rejoice and be glad in You;
let those who love Your salvation
say always, "Great is God!"

5As for me, I am poor and needy;
God, hurry to me.
You are my help and my deliverer;
LORD, do not delay.

Notes

  • The whole psalm — nearly the same as 40:13–17, and the English there is followed. Where the Hebrew differs, so does the English: v1 has "God" and no "Be pleased"; v2 drops "together" and "to sweep it away"; v3 has "turn back" for "be appalled" and no "to me"; v4 has "God" for "the LORD"; v5 has "God, hurry to me" for "the Lord thinks of me," and "LORD" for "my God."

speech.text: Psalms 70
God, rescue me; LORD, hurry to help me.
Let them be put to shame and confounded who seek my life; let them be turned back and disgraced who delight in my harm.
Let them turn back because of their shame who say, "Aha, aha!"
But let all who seek You rejoice and be glad in You; let those who love Your salvation say always, "Great is God!"
As for me, I am poor and needy; God, hurry to me. You are my help and my deliverer; LORD, do not delay.

chapters.title: Do Not Cast Me Off in Old Age
chapters.html:
Psalms 71

1In You, LORD, I take refuge;
let me never be put to shame.

2In Your righteousness rescue me and deliver me;
incline Your ear to me and save me.

3Be a rock of refuge for me, where I can always come;
You have given the command to save me,
for You are my rock and my fortress.

4My God, deliver me from the hand of the wicked,
from the grasp of the unjust and cruel.

5For You are my hope, Lord GOD,
my trust from my youth.

6I have leaned on You from birth;
You are the one who took me from my mother's womb.
My praise is always of You.

7I have been a portent to many,
but You are my strong refuge.

8My mouth is filled with Your praise,
with Your glory all day long.

9Do not cast me off in the time of old age;
when my strength fails, do not forsake me.

10For my enemies speak against me,
and those who watch for my life consult together,

11saying, "God has forsaken him;
pursue and seize him,
for there is no one to rescue him."

12God, do not be far from me;
my God, hurry to help me.

13Let my accusers be put to shame and consumed;
let those who seek my harm
be covered with reproach and disgrace.

14But I will hope continually
and will praise You yet more and more.

15My mouth will tell of Your righteousness,
of Your salvation all day long,
though I do not know their number.

16I will come with the mighty deeds of the Lord GOD;
I will make mention of Your righteousness, Yours alone.

17God, You have taught me from my youth,
and to this day I declare Your wonders.

18So even to old age and gray hair,
God, do not forsake me,
until I declare Your arm to this generation,
Your might to all who are to come.

19Your righteousness, God, reaches the heights,
You who have done great things.
God, who is like You?

20You who have shown me many troubles and distresses
will revive me again;
from the depths of the earth
You will bring me up again.

21You will increase my greatness
and turn and comfort me.

22I will also praise You with the harp
for Your faithfulness, my God;
I will sing praises to You with the lyre,
Holy One of Israel.

23My lips will shout for joy when I sing praises to You,
and my soul, which You have redeemed.

24My tongue also will talk of Your righteousness all day long,
for they have been put to shame, for they have been disgraced,
who seek my harm.

Notes

  • vv1–3 — the opening of Psalm 31, and the English there is followed. Where the Hebrew differs, so does the English: here "in Your righteousness" opens v2, and v3 has ma'on, "a dwelling," with "where I can always come," for 31:2's "a strong fortress."

  • v20 "You who have shown me… will revive me… bring me up" — the written forms say "us" twice ("shown us," "revive us"); the read forms, "me," are followed.

chapters.title: Give the King Your Judgments
chapters.html:
Psalms 72

Of Solomon.

1God, give the king Your judgments,
and Your righteousness to the king's son.

2May he judge Your people with righteousness,
and Your poor with justice.

3May the mountains bring peace to the people,
and the hills, in righteousness.

4May he defend the poor of the people,
save the children of the needy,
and crush the oppressor.

5May they fear You while the sun endures,
and as long as the moon, through all generations.

6May he come down like rain on the mown grass,
like showers that water the earth.

7In his days may the righteous flourish,
and peace abound till the moon is no more.

8May he rule from sea to sea,
and from the River to the ends of the earth.

9May the desert tribes bow down before him,
and his enemies lick the dust.

10May the kings of Tarshish and of the coastlands bring tribute;
may the kings of Sheba and Seba offer gifts.

11May all kings bow down to him,
all nations serve him.

12For he rescues the needy who cry for help,
the poor and the one who has no helper.

13He has pity on the weak and the needy
and saves the lives of the needy.

14From oppression and violence he redeems their life,
and their blood is precious in his sight.

15Long may he live;
may gold of Sheba be given to him;
may prayer be made for him continually,
and blessings called down on him all day long.

16May there be abundance of grain in the land,
on the tops of the mountains;
may its fruit rustle like Lebanon,
and may people flourish in the cities
like the grass of the earth.

17May his name endure forever,
his name continue as long as the sun;
may people be blessed in him;
may all nations call him blessed.

18Blessed be the LORD God, the God of Israel,
who alone does wonders.

19Blessed be His glorious name forever;
may the whole earth be filled with His glory.
Amen and Amen.

20The prayers of David son of Jesse are ended.

Notes

  • v1 "the king… the king's son" — Jewish and Christian readers alike took the psalm of the Messiah, whose rule has no end (Isaiah 11:1–5).

  • v17 "may people be blessed in him" — the promise to Abraham (Genesis 12:3; 22:18) fulfilled in the king.

  • vv18–19 — the blessing that closes the second book of the Psalms, as 41:13 closed the first.

chapters.title: Surely God Is Good
chapters.html:
Psalms 73

A psalm of Asaph.

1Surely God is good to Israel,
to those who are pure in heart.

2But as for me, my feet had almost stumbled;
my steps had nearly slipped.

3For I envied the boastful
when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.

4For they have no pangs until their death;
their body is fat and sleek.

5They are not in trouble as others are;
they are not struck like other people.

6So pride is their necklace;
violence covers them like a garment.

7Their eyes bulge out from fatness;
the imaginations of their heart overflow.

8They mock and speak with malice;
from on high they threaten oppression.

9They set their mouth against the heavens,
and their tongue struts through the earth.

10So his people turn back to them,
and they drink up waters in abundance.

11They say, "How does God know?
Is there knowledge in the Most High?"

12Such are the wicked:
always at ease, they increase in wealth.

13Surely in vain I have kept my heart clean
and washed my hands in innocence.

14For all day long I have been stricken,
and rebuked every morning.

15If I had said, "I will speak like that,"
I would have betrayed the generation of Your children.

16But when I thought how to understand this,
it seemed a wearisome task to me,

17until I went into the sanctuary of God;
then I understood their end.

18Surely You set them in slippery places;
You make them fall to ruin.

19How they are made a desolation in a moment,
swept away, utterly consumed by terrors!

20Like a dream when one wakes, Lord,
when You rouse Yourself, You will despise their image.

21When my heart was embittered
and I was pierced within,

22I was brutish and did not understand;
I was like a beast before You.

23Yet I am always with You;
You hold my right hand.

24You guide me with Your counsel,
and afterward You will take me to glory.

25Whom have I in heaven but You?
Besides You I desire nothing on earth.

26My flesh and my heart may fail,
but God is the rock of my heart and my portion forever.

27For those who are far from You will perish;
You destroy all who are unfaithful to You.

28But for me it is good to be near God;
I have made the Lord GOD my refuge,
to tell of all Your works.

Notes

  • The title, "A psalm of Asaph" — the third book of the Psalms begins here and opens with eleven psalms of Asaph (73–83); Psalm 50 is the only other. Asaph led David's singers (1 Chronicles 16:5).

  • v10 "So his people turn back to them" — the read form; the written form has "he brings his people back." The verse is obscure, perhaps of people flocking to the wicked and drinking in their words.

  • v24 "afterward You will take me to glory" — laqach, the verb used of Enoch (Genesis 5:24) and Elijah (2 Kings 2:3) and in 49:15; "receive me with honor" is another reading.

For I envied the boastful when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.

chapters.title: Remember Your Congregation
chapters.html:
Psalms 74

A Maskil of Asaph.

1Why, God, have You rejected us forever?
Why does Your anger smoke against the sheep of Your pasture?

2Remember Your congregation, which You acquired long ago,
the tribe of Your inheritance, which You redeemed —
Mount Zion, where You have dwelt.

3Lift up Your steps to the everlasting ruins;
the enemy has destroyed everything in the sanctuary.

4Your foes have roared inside Your meeting place;
they set up their own signs for signs.

5They were like those who swing axes up high
in a thicket of trees.

6Now all its carved work
they smash with hatchet and hammers.

7They set Your sanctuary on fire;
they defiled the dwelling place of Your name, bringing it to the ground.

8They said in their hearts, "We will crush them altogether";
they burned all the meeting places of God in the land.

9We do not see our signs;
there is no longer any prophet,
and none among us knows how long.

10How long, God, will the foe scoff?
Will the enemy revile Your name forever?

11Why do You hold back Your hand, Your right hand?
Take it from Your bosom and destroy them.

12Yet God is my King from of old,
working salvation on the earth.

13You divided the sea by Your strength;
You broke the heads of the sea monsters on the waters.

14You crushed the heads of Leviathan;
You gave him as food to the creatures of the desert.

15You split open spring and torrent;
You dried up ever-flowing rivers.

16Yours is the day, Yours also the night;
You established the light and the sun.

17You have fixed all the boundaries of the earth;
summer and winter — You made them.

18Remember this: the enemy scoffs, LORD,
and a foolish people reviles Your name.

19Do not hand over the life of Your dove to the wild beast;
do not forget the life of Your poor forever.

20Look to the covenant,
for the dark places of the land are full of the haunts of violence.

21Do not let the oppressed turn back in shame;
let the poor and needy praise Your name.

22Arise, God, plead Your own cause;
remember how the fool scoffs at You all day long.

23Do not forget the clamor of Your foes,
the uproar of those who rise against You, which goes up continually.

Notes

  • The setting — the temple burned and its carving smashed (vv3–8) fits the Babylonian destruction of 587 BC (2 Kings 25:9); the psalm is a lament over it.

  • v11 "from Your bosom" — the read form cheqekha; the written form has chuqqekha, "Your statute."

  • vv13–14 "the sea monsters… Leviathan" — God's victory over the sea at creation and at the Exodus, told in the pictures of the old sea dragon (Job 26:12–13; Isaiah 27:1; 51:9–10).

Why, God, have You rejected us forever? Why does Your anger smoke against the sheep of Your pasture?
Remember Your congregation, which You acquired long ago, the tribe of Your inheritance, which You redeemed — Mount Zion, where You have dwelt.
Lift up Your steps to the everlasting ruins; the enemy has destroyed everything in the sanctuary.
Your foes have roared inside Your meeting place; they set up their own signs for signs.
They were like those who swing axes up high in a thicket of trees.

Look to the covenant, for the dark places of the land are full of the haunts of violence.
Do not let the oppressed turn back in shame; let the poor and needy praise Your name.
Arise, God, plead Your own cause; remember how the fool scoffs at You all day long.
Do not forget the clamor of Your foes, the uproar of those who rise against You, which goes up continually.

chapters.title: I Will Judge with Equity
chapters.html:
Psalms 75

For the director: "Do Not Destroy." A psalm of Asaph. A song.

1We give thanks to You, God;
we give thanks, for Your name is near;
they tell of Your wonders.

2"When I choose the appointed time,
I will judge with equity.

3When the earth and all its inhabitants melt,
it is I who keep its pillars steady. Selah

4I said to the boastful, 'Do not boast,'
and to the wicked, 'Do not lift up your horn;

5do not lift up your horn on high,
or speak with an arrogant neck.'"

6For not from the east or from the west,
and not from the wilderness, comes lifting up.

7But it is God who judges,
putting down one and lifting up another.

8For in the hand of the LORD there is a cup
with foaming wine, well mixed;
He pours from it,
and all the wicked of the earth
will drain it down to the dregs.

9But I will declare it forever;
I will sing praises to the God of Jacob.

10"All the horns of the wicked I will cut off,
but the horns of the righteous will be lifted up."

Notes

  • v8 "a cup" — the cup of God's wrath (Isaiah 51:17; Jeremiah 25:15; Revelation 14:10).

speech.text: Psalms 75
We give thanks to You, God; we give thanks, for Your name is near; they tell of Your wonders.
"When I choose the appointed time, I will judge with equity.
When the earth and all its inhabitants melt, it is I who keep its pillars steady. Selah
I said to the boastful, 'Do not boast,' and to the wicked, 'Do not lift up your horn;
do not lift up your horn on high, or speak with an arrogant neck.'"
For not from the east or from the west, and not from the wilderness, comes lifting up.
But it is God who judges, putting down one and lifting up another.
For in the hand of the LORD there is a cup with foaming wine, well mixed; He pours from it, and all the wicked of the earth will drain it down to the dregs.
But I will declare it forever; I will sing praises to the God of Jacob.
"All the horns of the wicked I will cut off, but the horns of the righteous will be lifted up."

chapters.title: God Is Known in Judah
chapters.html:
Psalms 76

For the director: with stringed instruments. A psalm of Asaph. A song.

1God is known in Judah;
His name is great in Israel.

2His tent is in Salem,
His dwelling place in Zion.

3There He broke the flaming arrows of the bow,
the shield, the sword, and the weapons of war. Selah

4You are radiant,
more majestic than the mountains of prey.

5The stouthearted have been stripped;
they have sunk into their sleep;
none of the men of war could lift their hands.

6At Your rebuke, God of Jacob,
both chariot and horse lay stunned.

7You — You are to be feared;
who can stand before You once Your anger is roused?

8From heaven You made Your judgment heard;
the earth feared and was still

9when God rose up to judge,
to save all the humble of the earth. Selah

10Surely human wrath will praise You;
the remnant of wrath You will put on like a belt.

11Make vows to the LORD your God and keep them;
let all around Him bring gifts to the One who is to be feared.

12He cuts off the spirit of princes;
He is feared by the kings of the earth.

Notes

  • The setting — an army broken outside Jerusalem without a battle (vv3–6) fits the night the LORD struck down Sennacherib's camp (2 Kings 19:35); the Greek title adds "concerning the Assyrian."

  • v2 "Salem" — Jerusalem, the city of Melchizedek (Genesis 14:18; Hebrews 7:1–2). "His tent" (sukko) is also a lion's lair (Jeremiah 25:38), fitting "the mountains of prey" in v4.

chapters.title: I Will Remember the Deeds of Yah
chapters.html:
Psalms 77

For the director: for Jeduthun. Of Asaph. A psalm.

1My voice goes up to God, and I cry out;
my voice goes up to God, and He will hear me.

2In the day of my trouble I sought the Lord;
in the night my hand was stretched out without tiring;
my soul refused to be comforted.

3I remember God, and I moan;
I meditate, and my spirit grows faint. Selah

4You hold my eyelids open;
I am so troubled that I cannot speak.

5I consider the days of old,
the years long past.

6I remember my song in the night;
I meditate in my heart,
and my spirit searches:

7"Will the Lord reject forever
and never again show favor?

8Has His loyal love come to an end forever?
Is His promise at an end for all generations?

9Has God forgotten to be gracious?
Has He in anger shut up His compassion?" Selah

10Then I said, "This is my grief:
that the right hand of the Most High has changed."

11I will remember the deeds of Yah;
yes, I will remember Your wonders of old.

12I will ponder all Your work
and meditate on Your mighty deeds.

13God, Your way is holy.
What god is great like God?

14You are the God who does wonders;
You have made known Your strength among the peoples.

15With Your arm You redeemed Your people,
the children of Jacob and Joseph. Selah

16The waters saw You, God;
the waters saw You and writhed;
the deeps also trembled.

17The clouds poured out water;
the skies gave out a voice;
Your arrows flashed back and forth.

18The sound of Your thunder was in the whirlwind;
lightning lit up the world;
the earth trembled and shook.

19Your way was through the sea,
Your path through the great waters,
yet Your footprints were not seen.

20You led Your people like a flock
by the hand of Moses and Aaron.

Notes

  • vv16–19 — the crossing of the Red Sea (Exodus 14–15) told as a storm theophany, with thunder and lightning as at Sinai (Exodus 19:16).

  • v19 "yet Your footprints were not seen" — God led them through, but the water closed behind Him; His presence is sure even where His steps cannot be traced.

chapters.title: Tell the Next Generation
chapters.html:
Psalms 78

A Maskil of Asaph.

1Give ear, my people, to my teaching;
incline your ears to the words of my mouth.

2I will open my mouth in a parable;
I will pour out riddles from of old,

3things that we have heard and known,
that our fathers have told us.

4We will not hide them from their children;
we will tell the next generation
the praises of the LORD and His might,
and the wonders He has done.

5He set up a testimony in Jacob
and placed a law in Israel,
which He commanded our fathers
to make known to their children,

6so that the next generation might know them,
children yet to be born,
and they would rise and tell them to their children,

7so that they would set their hope in God
and not forget the works of God,
but keep His commandments,

8and not be like their fathers,
a stubborn and rebellious generation,
a generation whose heart was not steadfast,
whose spirit was not faithful to God.

9The sons of Ephraim, armed archers,
turned back on the day of battle.

10They did not keep the covenant of God
and refused to walk in His law.

11They forgot His deeds
and the wonders He had shown them.

12In the sight of their fathers He did wonders
in the land of Egypt, in the field of Zoan.

13He split the sea and let them pass through;
He made the waters stand up like a heap.

14He led them with the cloud by day
and all night with a light of fire.

15He split rocks in the wilderness
and gave them drink as from the great deep.

16He brought streams out of the rock
and made water flow down like rivers.

17Yet they went on sinning against Him,
rebelling against the Most High in the desert.

18They tested God in their heart
by demanding the food they craved.

19They spoke against God; they said,
"Can God spread a table in the wilderness?

20He struck the rock so that water gushed out
and streams overflowed;
can He also give bread
or provide meat for His people?"

21So when the LORD heard, He was furious;
a fire was kindled against Jacob,
and anger also went up against Israel,

22because they did not believe in God
or trust in His salvation.

23Yet He commanded the skies above
and opened the doors of heaven;

24He rained down manna on them to eat
and gave them the grain of heaven.

25Each one ate the bread of the mighty;
He sent them food in abundance.

26He let loose the east wind in the heavens,
and by His power He drove the south wind;

27He rained meat on them like dust,
winged birds like the sand of the seas;

28He let them fall inside their camp,
all around their dwellings.

29They ate and were well filled,
for He gave them what they craved.

30But before they had turned from their craving,
while the food was still in their mouths,

31the anger of God went up against them;
He killed the strongest of them
and struck down the young men of Israel.

32In spite of all this they still sinned
and did not believe in His wonders.

33So He made their days vanish like a breath,
and their years in sudden terror.

34When He killed them, they sought Him;
they turned and searched eagerly for God.

35They remembered that God was their rock,
the Most High God their redeemer.

36But they flattered Him with their mouths
and lied to Him with their tongues.

37Their heart was not steadfast toward Him;
they were not faithful to His covenant.

38Yet He, being compassionate, atoned for their guilt
and did not destroy them;
many times He turned back His anger
and did not stir up all His wrath.

39He remembered that they were flesh,
a wind that passes and does not return.

40How often they rebelled against Him in the wilderness
and grieved Him in the desert!

41Again and again they tested God
and pained the Holy One of Israel.

42They did not remember His hand,
the day He redeemed them from the foe,

43when He set His signs in Egypt
and His wonders in the field of Zoan.

44He turned their rivers into blood,
so that they could not drink from their streams.

45He sent swarms of flies among them, which devoured them,
and frogs, which destroyed them.

46He gave their crops to the grasshopper
and their labor to the locust.

47He killed their vines with hail
and their sycamore figs with frost.

48He gave over their cattle to the hail
and their livestock to bolts of fire.

49He sent on them His burning anger,
fury, indignation, and distress,
a company of messengers of harm.

50He made a path for His anger;
He did not spare them from death
but gave their lives over to the plague.

51He struck all the firstborn in Egypt,
the first fruits of their strength in the tents of Ham.

52Then He led out His people like sheep
and guided them like a flock in the wilderness.

53He led them in safety, so that they were not afraid,
but the sea covered their enemies.

54He brought them to His holy territory,
to this mountain His right hand had acquired.

55He drove out nations before them;
He apportioned them an inheritance by measuring line
and settled the tribes of Israel in their tents.

56Yet they tested and rebelled against the Most High God
and did not keep His testimonies.

57They turned away and were faithless like their fathers;
they twisted like a deceitful bow.

58They provoked Him to anger with their high places
and moved Him to jealousy with their carved images.

59When God heard, He was furious
and utterly rejected Israel.

60He abandoned the dwelling at Shiloh,
the tent where He had dwelt among people.

61He gave His strength into captivity,
His glory into the hand of the foe.

62He gave His people over to the sword
and was furious with His inheritance.

63Fire devoured their young men,
and their young women had no wedding songs.

64Their priests fell by the sword,
and their widows could not weep.

65Then the Lord awoke as from sleep,
like a warrior shouting because of wine.

66He struck His foes from behind;
He put them to everlasting reproach.

67He rejected the tent of Joseph
and did not choose the tribe of Ephraim,

68but He chose the tribe of Judah,
Mount Zion, which He loves.

69He built His sanctuary like the heights,
like the earth, which He founded forever.

70He chose David His servant
and took him from the sheepfolds;

71from following the nursing ewes He brought him
to shepherd Jacob His people,
Israel His inheritance.

72He shepherded them with integrity of heart
and guided them with skillful hands.

Notes

  • v2 "I will open my mouth in a parable" — mashal, a saying with a lesson hidden in it; chidot, riddles. Matthew 13:35 quotes the line of Jesus' teaching in parables. The riddle here is Israel's own history.

  • v25 "the bread of the mighty" — abbirim; the Greek reads "the bread of angels," and Wisdom 16:20 follows it. John 6:31 quotes v24, "He gave them bread from heaven to eat."

  • vv70–72 "He chose David His servant and took him from the sheepfolds" — 1 Samuel 16:11; 2 Samuel 7:8. The history ends with the shepherd king, the answer to the people's straying.

chapters.title: The Nations Have Come into Your Inheritance
chapters.html:
Psalms 79

A psalm of Asaph.

1God, the nations have entered Your inheritance;
they have defiled Your holy temple;
they have laid Jerusalem in heaps of ruins.

2They have given the bodies of Your servants
as food to the birds of the heavens,
the flesh of Your faithful ones to the beasts of the earth.

3They have poured out their blood like water
all around Jerusalem,
and there is no one to bury them.

4We have become a reproach to our neighbors,
mocked and derided by those around us.

5How long, LORD? Will You be angry forever?
Will Your jealousy burn like fire?

6Pour out Your wrath on the nations that do not know You,
and on the kingdoms that do not call on Your name,

7for they have devoured Jacob
and laid waste his homeland.

8Do not remember against us the guilt of former generations;
let Your compassion come quickly to meet us,
for we are brought very low.

9Help us, God of our salvation,
for the glory of Your name;
deliver us and atone for our sins
for Your name's sake.

10Why should the nations say,
"Where is their God?"
Let the avenging of the poured-out blood of Your servants
be known among the nations before our eyes.

11Let the groaning of the prisoner come before You;
by the greatness of Your arm
preserve those doomed to die.

12Return sevenfold into the lap of our neighbors
the reproach with which they have reproached You, Lord.

13Then we, Your people, the sheep of Your pasture,
will give thanks to You forever;
from generation to generation we will tell of Your praise.

Notes

  • The setting — like Psalm 74, a lament over the fall of Jerusalem to Babylon (2 Kings 25); 1 Maccabees 7:16–17 quotes vv2–3 of the killing of the faithful in its own day.

  • vv6–7 — nearly the same as Jeremiah 10:25, which reads "on the families that do not call on Your name."

chapters.title: Restore Us, God
chapters.html:
Psalms 80

For the director: on "Lilies of Testimony." Of Asaph. A psalm.

1Shepherd of Israel, give ear,
You who lead Joseph like a flock;
You who are enthroned on the cherubim, shine forth.

2Before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh,
stir up Your might
and come to save us.

3God, restore us;
make Your face shine, so that we may be saved.

4LORD God of hosts,
how long will Your anger smoke against the prayers of Your people?

5You have fed them with the bread of tears
and given them tears to drink by the measure.

6You make us a cause of strife to our neighbors,
and our enemies laugh among themselves.

7God of hosts, restore us;
make Your face shine, so that we may be saved.

8You brought a vine out of Egypt;
You drove out the nations and planted it.

9You cleared the ground for it;
it took deep root and filled the land.

10The mountains were covered with its shade,
the mighty cedars with its branches.

11It sent out its branches to the sea
and its shoots to the River.

12Why then have You broken down its walls,
so that all who pass along the road pluck its fruit?

13The boar from the forest ravages it,
and whatever moves in the field feeds on it.

14God of hosts, turn again;
look down from heaven and see;
take care of this vine,

15the stock that Your right hand planted,
and the son You made strong for Yourself.

16It is burned with fire; it is cut down;
they perish at the rebuke of Your face.

17Let Your hand be on the man of Your right hand,
on the son of man You made strong for Yourself.

18Then we will not turn back from You;
give us life, and we will call on Your name.

19LORD God of hosts, restore us;
make Your face shine, so that we may be saved.

Notes

  • vv8–16 "a vine out of Egypt" — Israel as God's vine, as in Isaiah 5:1–7 and Jeremiah 2:21; Jesus takes up the picture: I am the true vine (John 15:1).

  • vv15, 17 "the son… the man of Your right hand… the son of man" — the king, or Israel itself (Exodus 4:22), whom God raised up; "man of Your right hand" may play on Benjamin, "son of the right hand." These stay lowercase.

chapters.title: Open Your Mouth Wide
chapters.html:
Psalms 81

For the director: on the Gittith. Of Asaph.

1Sing for joy to God our strength;
shout aloud to the God of Jacob.

2Raise a song and sound the tambourine,
the sweet lyre with the harp.

3Blow the ram's horn at the new moon,
at the full moon, on our feast day.

4For it is a statute for Israel,
a rule of the God of Jacob.

5He made it a testimony in Joseph
when He went out over the land of Egypt.
I heard a language I did not know:

6"I removed the burden from his shoulder;
his hands were freed from the basket.

7In distress you called, and I rescued you;
I answered you in the hiding place of thunder;
I tested you at the waters of Meribah. Selah

8Hear, My people, and I will warn you —
Israel, if you would only listen to Me!

9There shall be no strange god among you;
you shall not bow down to a foreign god.

10I am the LORD your God,
who brought you up out of the land of Egypt.
Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it.

11But My people did not listen to My voice;
Israel would have none of Me.

12So I gave them over to the stubbornness of their heart,
to follow their own counsels.

13If only My people would listen to Me,
if Israel would walk in My ways!

14I would soon subdue their enemies
and turn My hand against their foes.

15Those who hate the LORD would cringe before Him,
and their time of doom would last forever.

16He would feed them with the finest of the wheat,
and with honey from the rock I would satisfy you."

Notes

  • vv9–10 — the opening of the Ten Commandments (Exodus 20:2–3), with "brought you up" (hamma'alkha) for "brought you out."

chapters.title: God Stands in the Divine Council
chapters.html:
Psalms 82

A psalm of Asaph.

1God stands in the divine council;
among the gods He passes judgment:

2"How long will you judge unjustly
and show favor to the wicked? Selah

3Give justice to the weak and the fatherless;
uphold the right of the afflicted and the destitute.

4Rescue the weak and the needy;
deliver them from the hand of the wicked."

5They do not know, they do not understand;
they walk about in darkness;
all the foundations of the earth are shaken.

6I said, "You are gods,
sons of the Most High, all of you;

7nevertheless, you will die like mortals
and fall like any of the princes."

8Arise, God, judge the earth,
for You will inherit all the nations.

Notes

  • v1 "in the divine council" — ba'adat El, "in the assembly of God." Who the "gods" are has been read two ways: heavenly powers set over the nations (Deuteronomy 32:8; Daniel 10:13, 20), or human judges who rule in God's name (Exodus 22:8–9, where elohim may mean judges). The psalm itself holds them to account for injustice on earth.

  • v6 "You are gods" — Jesus quotes this in John 10:34–35: If He called them gods to whom the word of God came… do you say of Him whom the Father sanctified, 'You are blaspheming'?

speech.text: Psalms 82
God stands in the divine council; among the gods He passes judgment:
"How long will you judge unjustly and show favor to the wicked? Selah
Give justice to the weak and the fatherless; uphold the right of the afflicted and the destitute.
Rescue the weak and the needy; deliver them from the hand of the wicked."
They do not know, they do not understand; they walk about in darkness; all the foundations of the earth are shaken.
I said, "You are gods, sons of the Most High, all of you;
nevertheless, you will die like mortals and fall like any of the princes."
Arise, God, judge the earth, for You will inherit all the nations.

chapters.title: Do Not Keep Silent
chapters.html:
Psalms 83

A song. A psalm of Asaph.

1God, do not keep silent;
do not hold Your peace or be still, God.

2For listen: Your enemies are in an uproar;
those who hate You have raised their heads.

3They lay crafty plans against Your people;
they consult together against Your treasured ones.

4They say, "Come, let us wipe them out as a nation,
so that the name of Israel is remembered no more."

5For they plot together with one heart;
against You they make a covenant —

6the tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites,
Moab and the Hagrites,

7Gebal and Ammon and Amalek,
Philistia with the inhabitants of Tyre;

8Assyria also has joined them;
they have become the strong arm of the children of Lot. Selah

9Do to them as You did to Midian,
as to Sisera and Jabin at the brook Kishon,

10who were destroyed at En-dor,
who became dung for the ground.

11Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb,
all their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna,

12who said, "Let us take for ourselves
the pastures of God."

13My God, make them like whirling dust,
like chaff before the wind.

14As fire burns a forest,
as a flame sets the mountains ablaze,

15so pursue them with Your tempest
and terrify them with Your storm.

16Fill their faces with shame,
so that they may seek Your name, LORD.

17Let them be put to shame and terrified forever;
let them be disgraced and perish,

18so that they may know that You alone,
whose name is the LORD,
are the Most High over all the earth.

Notes

  • vv9–12 — the victories of Deborah and Barak over Sisera and Jabin (Judges 4–5) and of Gideon over Midian, with its princes Oreb and Zeeb and kings Zebah and Zalmunna (Judges 7:25; 8:21).

chapters.title: How Lovely Is Your Dwelling Place
chapters.html:
Psalms 84

For the director: on the Gittith. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.

1How lovely is Your dwelling place,
LORD of hosts!

2My soul longs, yes, faints
for the courts of the LORD;
my heart and my flesh sing for joy
to the living God.

3Even the sparrow has found a home,
and the swallow a nest for herself,
where she may lay her young —
at Your altars, LORD of hosts,
my King and my God.

4Blessed are those who dwell in Your house;
they are always praising You. Selah

5Blessed is the one whose strength is in You,
in whose heart are the highways.

6As they pass through the Valley of Baca,
they make it a place of springs;
the early rain also covers it with blessings.

7They go from strength to strength;
each one appears before God in Zion.

8LORD God of hosts, hear my prayer;
give ear, God of Jacob. Selah

9See our shield, God;
look on the face of Your anointed.

10For a day in Your courts
is better than a thousand elsewhere;
I would rather stand at the threshold of the house of my God
than live in the tents of wickedness.

11For the LORD God is a sun and a shield;
the LORD gives grace and glory;
no good thing does He hold back
from those who walk blamelessly.

12LORD of hosts,
blessed is the one who trusts in You.

Notes

  • v11 "a sun and a shield" — the only place in the Psalms where God is called a sun.

chapters.title: Righteousness and Peace Have Kissed
chapters.html:
Psalms 85

For the director. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.

1LORD, You showed favor to Your land;
You restored the fortunes of Jacob.

2You forgave the guilt of Your people;
You covered all their sin. Selah

3You withdrew all Your fury;
You turned from the heat of Your anger.

4Restore us, God of our salvation,
and put away Your displeasure toward us.

5Will You be angry with us forever?
Will You draw out Your anger to all generations?

6Will You not give us life again,
so that Your people may rejoice in You?

7Show us Your loyal love, LORD,
and grant us Your salvation.

8Let me hear what God the LORD will speak,
for He will speak peace to His people, to His faithful ones;
but let them not turn back to folly.

9Surely His salvation is near to those who fear Him,
so that glory may dwell in our land.

10Loyal love and truth have met together;
righteousness and peace have kissed.

11Truth springs up from the earth,
and righteousness looks down from heaven.

12The LORD will indeed give what is good,
and our land will yield its harvest.

13Righteousness will go before Him
and make His footsteps a way.

Notes

  • v10 "Loyal love and truth have met together; righteousness and peace have kissed" — God's gifts pictured as people meeting on the road; the Exodus pair chesed and emet (Exodus 34:6) with tsedeq and shalom.

Show us Your loyal love, LORD, and grant us Your salvation.

chapters.title: Unite My Heart to Fear Your Name
chapters.html:
Psalms 86

A prayer of David.

1Incline Your ear, LORD, and answer me,
for I am poor and needy.

2Guard my life, for I am faithful;
save Your servant who trusts in You —
You are my God.

3Be gracious to me, Lord,
for I call to You all day long.

4Gladden the soul of Your servant,
for to You, Lord, I lift up my soul.

5For You, Lord, are good and forgiving,
abounding in loyal love to all who call on You.

6Give ear, LORD, to my prayer;
listen to my plea for grace.

7In the day of my trouble I call on You,
for You answer me.

8There is none like You among the gods, Lord,
and there are no works like Yours.

9All the nations You have made
will come and bow down before You, Lord,
and glorify Your name.

10For You are great and do wonders;
You alone are God.

11Teach me Your way, LORD,
so that I may walk in Your truth;
unite my heart to fear Your name.

12I will give thanks to You, Lord my God, with all my heart,
and I will glorify Your name forever.

13For great is Your loyal love toward me;
You have delivered my soul from the depths of Sheol.

14God, the arrogant have risen against me,
and a band of ruthless men seeks my life;
they have not set You before them.

15But You, Lord, are God merciful and gracious,
slow to anger, and abundant in loyal love and truth.

16Turn to me and be gracious to me;
give Your strength to Your servant,
and save the son of Your maidservant.

17Show me a sign of Your goodness,
so that those who hate me may see it and be put to shame,
because You, LORD, have helped me and comforted me.

Notes

  • v9 "All the nations You have made will come and bow down before You" — quoted in the song of the Lamb (Revelation 15:4).

  • v15 "God merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abundant in loyal love and truth" — the LORD's words about Himself at Sinai (Exodus 34:6), and the English there is followed.

chapters.title: Glorious Things Are Spoken of You
chapters.html:
Psalms 87

Of the sons of Korah. A psalm. A song.

1His foundation is on the holy mountains.

2The LORD loves the gates of Zion
more than all the dwellings of Jacob.

3Glorious things are spoken of you,
city of God. Selah

4"I will count Rahab and Babylon
among those who know Me;
Philistia and Tyre, with Cush —
'This one was born there.'"

5Of Zion it will be said,
"Each one was born in her,"
and the Most High Himself will establish her.

6The LORD will write when He registers the peoples,
"This one was born there." Selah

7Singers and dancers alike will say,
"All my springs are in you."

Notes

  • v4 "Rahab and Babylon" — Rahab, the sea monster, is a name for Egypt (Isaiah 30:7; 51:9). Egypt and Babylon, the great oppressors, with Philistia, Tyre and Cush, are counted as natives of Zion.

His foundation is on the holy mountains.
The LORD loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.
Glorious things are spoken of you, city of God. Selah

chapters.title: Darkness Is My Companion
chapters.html:
Psalms 88

A song. A psalm of the sons of Korah. For the director: on Mahalath Leannoth. A Maskil of Heman the Ezrahite.

1LORD, God of my salvation,
by day I cry out, and by night, before You.

2Let my prayer come before You;
incline Your ear to my cry.

3For my soul is full of troubles,
and my life draws near to Sheol.

4I am counted among those who go down to the pit;
I have become like a man without strength,

5set loose among the dead,
like the slain who lie in the grave,
whom You remember no more,
for they are cut off from Your hand.

6You have put me in the lowest pit,
in dark places, in the depths.

7Your wrath lies heavy on me,
and You have afflicted me with all Your waves. Selah

8You have put my companions far from me;
You have made me detestable to them;
I am shut in and cannot get out.

9My eye grows dim through affliction;
I call on You, LORD, every day;
I spread out my hands to You.

10Do You work wonders for the dead?
Do the shades rise up to praise You? Selah

11Is Your loyal love told in the grave,
Your faithfulness in Abaddon?

12Are Your wonders known in the darkness,
or Your righteousness in the land of forgetfulness?

13But I cry to You, LORD, for help;
in the morning my prayer comes before You.

14LORD, why do You reject my soul?
Why do You hide Your face from me?

15I have been afflicted and close to death from my youth;
I bear Your terrors; I am in despair.

16Your burning anger has swept over me;
Your terrors have destroyed me.

17They surround me like water all day long;
they close in on me together.

18You have put loved one and friend far from me;
my companions are darkness.

Notes

  • The whole psalm — the only lament in the Psalms that ends with no turn to hope; its last word is "darkness." Yet it is prayer from first to last, addressed to the "God of my salvation" (v1).

chapters.title: I Will Sing of the LORD's Loyal Love Forever
chapters.html:
Psalms 89

A Maskil of Ethan the Ezrahite.

1I will sing of the loyal love of the LORD forever;
with my mouth I will make known Your faithfulness to all generations.

2For I said, "Loyal love will be built up forever;
in the heavens You will establish Your faithfulness."

3"I have made a covenant with My chosen one;
I have sworn to David My servant:

4'I will establish your offspring forever
and build up your throne for all generations.'" Selah

5Let the heavens praise Your wonders, LORD,
Your faithfulness also in the assembly of the holy ones.

6For who in the skies can compare with the LORD?
Who among the sons of God is like the LORD,

7a God greatly feared in the council of the holy ones,
and awesome above all who are around Him?

8LORD God of hosts,
who is mighty like You, Yah?
Your faithfulness surrounds You.

9You rule the raging of the sea;
when its waves rise, You still them.

10You crushed Rahab like one who is slain;
You scattered Your enemies with Your mighty arm.

11The heavens are Yours; the earth also is Yours;
the world and all that fills it — You founded them.

12The north and the south — You created them;
Tabor and Hermon sing for joy at Your name.

13You have a mighty arm;
strong is Your hand, high is Your right hand.

14Righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne;
loyal love and truth go before You.

15Blessed are the people who know the festal shout,
who walk, LORD, in the light of Your face.

16They rejoice in Your name all day long,
and in Your righteousness they are lifted up.

17For You are the glory of their strength,
and by Your favor our horn is lifted high.

18For our shield belongs to the LORD,
our king to the Holy One of Israel.

19Once You spoke in a vision to Your faithful ones and said:
"I have given help to a mighty one;
I have raised up one chosen from the people.

20I have found David My servant;
with My holy oil I have anointed him,

21so that My hand will stay with him;
My arm also will strengthen him.

22The enemy will not get the better of him;
the wicked will not afflict him.

23I will crush his foes before him
and strike down those who hate him.

24My faithfulness and My loyal love will be with him,
and in My name his horn will be lifted high.

25I will set his hand on the sea
and his right hand on the rivers.

26He will call to Me, 'You are my Father,
my God, and the rock of my salvation.'

27I will also make him the firstborn,
the highest of the kings of the earth.

28I will keep My loyal love for him forever,
and My covenant will stand firm for him.

29I will establish his offspring forever
and his throne as the days of heaven.

30If his sons forsake My law
and do not walk in My judgments,

31if they profane My statutes
and do not keep My commandments,

32then I will punish their transgression with the rod
and their guilt with blows,

33but I will not take My loyal love from him
or be false to My faithfulness.

34I will not profane My covenant
or change what has gone out from My lips.

35Once for all I have sworn by My holiness;
I will not lie to David.

36His offspring will endure forever,
and his throne like the sun before Me.

37Like the moon it will be established forever,
a faithful witness in the skies." Selah

38But You have rejected and spurned;
You are furious with Your anointed.

39You have renounced the covenant with Your servant;
You have profaned his crown in the dust.

40You have broken down all his walls;
You have laid his strongholds in ruins.

41All who pass along the road plunder him;
he has become a reproach to his neighbors.

42You have raised the right hand of his foes;
You have made all his enemies rejoice.

43You have turned back the edge of his sword
and have not made him stand in battle.

44You have ended his splendor
and hurled his throne to the ground.

45You have cut short the days of his youth;
You have covered him with shame. Selah

46How long, LORD? Will You hide Yourself forever?
Will Your wrath burn like fire?

47Remember how short my life is!
For what futility You have created all the children of man!

48What man can live and not see death?
Who can deliver his soul from the hand of Sheol? Selah

49Lord, where are Your loyal loves of old,
which You swore to David in Your faithfulness?

50Remember, Lord, the reproach of Your servants,
how I carry in my bosom the insults of all the many peoples,

51with which Your enemies have reproached, LORD,
with which they have reproached the footsteps of Your anointed.

52Blessed be the LORD forever.
Amen and Amen.

Notes

  • vv3–4, 19–37 — God's covenant with David from 2 Samuel 7:8–16, retold in poetry; v4 and v29 echo I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever (2 Samuel 7:13). The king's pronouns stay lowercase; the New Testament sees the covenant kept in Christ, the Son of David (Luke 1:32–33; Acts 13:22–23).

  • v52 — the blessing that closes the third book of the Psalms, as 41:13 and 72:18–19 closed the first two.

chapters.title: Teach Us to Number Our Days
chapters.html:
Psalms 90

A prayer of Moses, the man of God.

1Lord, You have been our dwelling place
in all generations.

2Before the mountains were born,
or You brought forth the earth and the world,
from everlasting to everlasting You are God.

3You turn mortals back to dust
and say, "Return, children of man."

4For a thousand years in Your sight
are like yesterday when it is past,
or like a watch in the night.

5You sweep them away; they are like a sleep,
like grass that springs up in the morning:

6in the morning it flourishes and springs up;
by evening it withers and dries.

7For we are consumed by Your anger;
by Your wrath we are terrified.

8You have set our iniquities before You,
our secret sins in the light of Your face.

9For all our days pass away under Your wrath;
we bring our years to an end like a sigh.

10The days of our years are seventy years,
or if by strength, eighty years;
yet their pride is only trouble and sorrow,
for it is soon gone, and we fly away.

11Who knows the power of Your anger,
and Your wrath as the fear of You deserves?

12So teach us to number our days,
so that we may gain a heart of wisdom.

13Return, LORD — how long?
Have compassion on Your servants.

14Satisfy us in the morning with Your loyal love,
so that we may sing for joy and be glad all our days.

15Make us glad for as many days as You have afflicted us,
for as many years as we have seen trouble.

16Let Your work be seen by Your servants,
and Your splendor by their children.

17Let the favor of the Lord our God be on us,
and establish the work of our hands for us —
yes, establish the work of our hands.

Notes

  • The title, "A prayer of Moses, the man of God" — the only psalm credited to Moses, and the first of the fourth book of the Psalms. "The man of God" is Moses' title in Deuteronomy 33:1.

  • v4 "a thousand years in Your sight are like yesterday" — 2 Peter 3:8 draws on this: with the Lord one day is as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.

speech.text: Psalms 90
Lord, You have been our dwelling place in all generations.
Before the mountains were born, or You brought forth the earth and the world, from everlasting to everlasting You are God.
You turn mortals back to dust and say, "Return, children of man."
For a thousand years in Your sight are like yesterday when it is past, or like a watch in the night.
You sweep them away; they are like a sleep, like grass that springs up in the morning:
in the morning it flourishes and springs up; by evening it withers and dries.
For we are consumed by Your anger; by Your wrath we are terrified.
You have set our iniquities before You, our secret sins in the light of Your face.
For all our days pass away under Your wrath; we bring our years to an end like a sigh.
The days of our years are seventy years, or if by strength, eighty years; yet their pride is only trouble and sorrow, for it is soon gone, and we fly away.
Who knows the power of Your anger, and Your wrath as the fear of You deserves?
So teach us to number our days, so that we may gain a heart of wisdom.
Return, LORD — how long? Have compassion on Your servants.
Satisfy us in the morning with Your loyal love, so that we may sing for joy and be glad all our days.
Make us glad for as many days as You have afflicted us, for as many years as we have seen trouble.
Let Your work be seen by Your servants, and Your splendor by their children.
Let the favor of the Lord our God be on us, and establish the work of our hands for us — yes, establish the work of our hands.

chapters.title: Under the Shadow of the Almighty
chapters.html:
Psalms 91

1The one who dwells in the shelter of the Most High
will rest in the shadow of the Almighty.

2I will say to the LORD, "My refuge and my fortress,
my God, in whom I trust."

3For He will deliver you from the snare of the fowler
and from the deadly plague.

4He will cover you with His feathers,
and under His wings you will find refuge;
His faithfulness is a shield and a wall.

5You will not fear the terror of the night,
or the arrow that flies by day,

6or the plague that stalks in darkness,
or the destruction that lays waste at noon.

7A thousand may fall at your side,
ten thousand at your right hand,
but it will not come near you.

8You will only look with your eyes
and see the recompense of the wicked.

9For You, LORD, are my refuge!
You have made the Most High your dwelling place;

10no evil will befall you,
no plague come near your tent.

11For He will command His messengers concerning you
to guard you in all your ways.

12On their hands they will bear you up,
so that you do not strike your foot against a stone.

13You will tread on the lion and the cobra;
you will trample the young lion and the serpent.

14"Because he holds fast to Me in love, I will deliver him;
I will set him on high, because he knows My name.

15He will call on Me, and I will answer him;
I will be with him in trouble;
I will rescue him and honor him.

16With long life I will satisfy him
and show him My salvation."

Notes

  • vv11–12 "He will command His messengers concerning you" — mal'akhim, messengers, as everywhere in this rendering; in the temptation the devil quotes these lines to Jesus, and the Gospel has "angels" (Matthew 4:6; Luke 4:10–11). Jesus answers from Deuteronomy 6:16.

  • v13 "the lion and the cobra… the serpent" — compare Luke 10:19, I have given you authority to tread on serpents and scorpions.

or the plague that stalks in darkness, or the destruction that lays waste at noon.

For He will command His messengers concerning you to guard you in all your ways.

chapters.title: A Song for the Sabbath
chapters.html:
Psalms 92

A psalm. A song for the Sabbath day.

1It is good to give thanks to the LORD,
to sing praises to Your name, Most High,

2to declare Your loyal love in the morning
and Your faithfulness by night,

3on the ten-stringed instrument and the harp,
with the music of the lyre.

4For You have made me glad, LORD, by what You have done;
I sing for joy at the works of Your hands.

5How great are Your works, LORD!
Your thoughts are very deep.

6The senseless man does not know;
the fool does not understand this:

7that though the wicked sprout like grass
and all evildoers flourish,
they are doomed to destruction forever.

8But You, LORD, are on high forever.

9For indeed Your enemies, LORD,
for indeed Your enemies will perish;
all evildoers will be scattered.

10But You have lifted up my horn like that of the wild ox;
I am anointed with fresh oil.

11My eyes have looked on those who lie in wait for me;
my ears have heard of the evildoers who rise against me.

12The righteous will flourish like the palm tree
and grow like a cedar in Lebanon.

13Planted in the house of the LORD,
they will flourish in the courts of our God.

14They will still bear fruit in old age;
they will be full of sap and green,

15to declare that the LORD is upright;
He is my rock, and there is no unrighteousness in Him.

Notes

  • The title, "A song for the Sabbath day" — the only psalm the Hebrew titles assign to a day; it was sung in the temple on the Sabbath (Mishnah Tamid 7:4).
