chapters.title: The LORD Reigns
chapters.html:
Psalms 93

1The LORD reigns; He is clothed with majesty;
the LORD is clothed; He has put on strength like a belt.
The world is firmly established; it cannot be moved.

2Your throne is established from of old;
You are from everlasting.

3The floods have lifted up, LORD,
the floods have lifted up their voice;
the floods lift up their roaring.

4Mightier than the sounds of many waters,
mightier than the breakers of the sea,
the LORD on high is mighty.

5Your testimonies are very sure;
holiness befits Your house, LORD,
for length of days.

Notes

  • v1 "The LORD reigns" — YHWH malakh, the cry that opens the psalms of the LORD's kingship (93; 96–99). The Greek adds a title, "For the day before the Sabbath, when the earth was inhabited."

speech.text: Psalms 93
The LORD reigns; He is clothed with majesty; the LORD is clothed; He has put on strength like a belt. The world is firmly established; it cannot be moved.
Your throne is established from of old; You are from everlasting.
The floods have lifted up, LORD, the floods have lifted up their voice; the floods lift up their roaring.
Mightier than the sounds of many waters, mightier than the breakers of the sea, the LORD on high is mighty.
Your testimonies are very sure; holiness befits Your house, LORD, for length of days.

chapters.title: God of Vengeance, Shine Forth
chapters.html:
Psalms 94

1God of vengeance, LORD,
God of vengeance, shine forth!

2Rise up, Judge of the earth;
repay the proud what they deserve.

3How long shall the wicked, LORD,
how long shall the wicked exult?

4They pour out arrogant words;
all evildoers boast.

5They crush Your people, LORD,
and afflict Your inheritance.

6They kill the widow and the guest
and murder the fatherless.

7They say, "Yah does not see;
the God of Jacob does not notice."

8Understand, you senseless among the people!
Fools, when will you be wise?

9He who planted the ear, does He not hear?
He who formed the eye, does He not see?

10He who disciplines the nations, does He not rebuke —
He who teaches mankind knowledge?

11The LORD knows the thoughts of man,
that they are a breath.

12Blessed is the man whom You discipline, Yah,
and whom You teach from Your law,

13to give him rest from days of trouble,
until a pit is dug for the wicked.

14For the LORD will not forsake His people;
He will not abandon His inheritance.

15For justice will return to righteousness,
and all the upright in heart will follow it.

16Who will rise up for me against the evildoers?
Who will stand up for me against those who do wrong?

17If the LORD had not been my help,
my soul would soon have dwelt in silence.

18When I said, "My foot slips,"
Your loyal love, LORD, held me up.

19When my anxious thoughts are many within me,
Your comforts delight my soul.

20Can a throne of destruction be allied with You,
one that frames trouble by statute?

21They band together against the life of the righteous
and condemn innocent blood.

22But the LORD has become my stronghold,
and my God the rock of my refuge.

23He will bring back on them their own iniquity
and destroy them for their evil;
the LORD our God will destroy them.

Notes

  • v11 "that they are a breath" — hevel, as in Ecclesiastes; Paul quotes the verse as The Lord knows the thoughts of the wise, that they are futile (1 Corinthians 3:20).

speech.text: Psalms 94
God of vengeance, LORD, God of vengeance, shine forth!
Rise up, Judge of the earth; repay the proud what they deserve.
How long shall the wicked, LORD, how long shall the wicked exult?
They pour out arrogant words; all evildoers boast.
They crush Your people, LORD, and afflict Your inheritance.
They kill the widow and the guest and murder the fatherless.
They say, "Yah does not see; the God of Jacob does not notice."
Understand, you senseless among the people! Fools, when will you be wise?
He who planted the ear, does He not hear? He who formed the eye, does He not see?
He who disciplines the nations, does He not rebuke — He who teaches mankind knowledge?
The LORD knows the thoughts of man, that they are a breath.
Blessed is the man whom You discipline, Yah, and whom You teach from Your law,
to give him rest from days of trouble, until a pit is dug for the wicked.
For the LORD will not forsake His people; He will not abandon His inheritance.
For justice will return to righteousness, and all the upright in heart will follow it.
Who will rise up for me against the evildoers? Who will stand up for me against those who do wrong?
If the LORD had not been my help, my soul would soon have dwelt in silence.
When I said, "My foot slips," Your loyal love, LORD, held me up.
When my anxious thoughts are many within me, Your comforts delight my soul.
Can a throne of destruction be allied with You, one that frames trouble by statute?
They band together against the life of the righteous and condemn innocent blood.
But the LORD has become my stronghold, and my God the rock of my refuge.
He will bring back on them their own iniquity and destroy them for their evil; the LORD our God will destroy them.

chapters.title: Today, If You Will Hear His Voice
chapters.html:
Psalms 95

1Come, let us sing for joy to the LORD;
let us shout aloud to the rock of our salvation.

2Let us come before His face with thanksgiving;
let us shout to Him with songs of praise.

3For the LORD is a great God,
and a great King above all gods.

4In His hand are the depths of the earth,
and the heights of the mountains are His.

5The sea is His, for He made it,
and His hands formed the dry land.

6Come, let us worship and bow down;
let us kneel before the LORD our Maker.

7For He is our God,
and we are the people of His pasture
and the sheep of His hand.
Today, if you will hear His voice,

8do not harden your hearts as at Meribah,
as on the day of Massah in the wilderness,

9when your fathers tested Me;
they tried Me, though they had seen My work.

10For forty years I was disgusted with that generation,
and I said, "They are a people whose hearts go astray,
and they do not know My ways."

11So I swore in My anger,
"They shall not enter My rest."

Notes

  • v7 "Today, if you will hear His voice" — the turn from praise to warning; God Himself speaks in vv8–11.

  • v11 "They shall not enter My rest" — the oath of Numbers 14:21–23; "My rest" is the land, and Deuteronomy 12:9 calls it the rest. Hebrews 3:7–4:11 quotes vv7–11 from the Greek and reads "today" and "rest" as still open to God's people.

speech.text: Psalms 95
Come, let us sing for joy to the LORD; let us shout aloud to the rock of our salvation.
Let us come before His face with thanksgiving; let us shout to Him with songs of praise.
For the LORD is a great God, and a great King above all gods.
In His hand are the depths of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are His.
The sea is His, for He made it, and His hands formed the dry land.
Come, let us worship and bow down; let us kneel before the LORD our Maker.
For He is our God, and we are the people of His pasture and the sheep of His hand. Today, if you will hear His voice,
do not harden your hearts as at Meribah, as on the day of Massah in the wilderness,
when your fathers tested Me; they tried Me, though they had seen My work.
For forty years I was disgusted with that generation, and I said, "They are a people whose hearts go astray, and they do not know My ways."
So I swore in My anger, "They shall not enter My rest."

chapters.title: Sing to the LORD a New Song
chapters.html:
Psalms 96

1Sing to the LORD a new song;
sing to the LORD, all the earth.

2Sing to the LORD, bless His name;
proclaim His salvation from day to day.

3Declare His glory among the nations,
His wonders among all the peoples.

4For great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised;
He is to be feared above all gods.

5For all the gods of the peoples are idols,
but the LORD made the heavens.

6Splendor and majesty are before Him;
strength and beauty are in His sanctuary.

7Ascribe to the LORD, families of the peoples,
ascribe to the LORD glory and strength.

8Ascribe to the LORD the glory of His name;
bring an offering and enter His courts.

9Worship the LORD in the splendor of holiness;
tremble before Him, all the earth.

10Say among the nations, "The LORD reigns!"
The world is established; it shall not be moved;
He will judge the peoples with equity.

11Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth rejoice;
let the sea roar, and all that fills it;

12let the field exult, and all that is in it.
Then all the trees of the forest will sing for joy

13before the LORD, for He comes,
for He comes to judge the earth.
He will judge the world in righteousness,
and the peoples in His faithfulness.

Notes

  • The whole psalm — nearly the same as the song David appointed when the ark came to Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 16:23–33), and the English there is followed. Where the Hebrew differs, so does the English: v1 adds "a new song" and v2 "bless His name"; v6 has "beauty… in His sanctuary" for "joy… in His place"; v8 has "into His courts" for "before Him"; v10 adds "He will judge the peoples with equity"; v13 adds the last two lines. "O" is dropped from v7, as everywhere in this rendering of the Psalms.

speech.text: Psalms 96
Sing to the LORD a new song; sing to the LORD, all the earth.
Sing to the LORD, bless His name; proclaim His salvation from day to day.
Declare His glory among the nations, His wonders among all the peoples.
For great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised; He is to be feared above all gods.
For all the gods of the peoples are idols, but the LORD made the heavens.
Splendor and majesty are before Him; strength and beauty are in His sanctuary.
Ascribe to the LORD, families of the peoples, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength.
Ascribe to the LORD the glory of His name; bring an offering and enter His courts.
Worship the LORD in the splendor of holiness; tremble before Him, all the earth.
Say among the nations, "The LORD reigns!" The world is established; it shall not be moved; He will judge the peoples with equity.
Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth rejoice; let the sea roar, and all that fills it;
let the field exult, and all that is in it. Then all the trees of the forest will sing for joy
before the LORD, for He comes, for He comes to judge the earth. He will judge the world in righteousness, and the peoples in His faithfulness.

chapters.title: Clouds and Thick Darkness Surround Him
chapters.html:
Psalms 97

1The LORD reigns; let the earth rejoice;
let the many coastlands be glad.

2Clouds and thick darkness surround Him;
righteousness and justice are the foundation of His throne.

3Fire goes before Him
and burns up His foes all around.

4His lightnings light up the world;
the earth sees and trembles.

5The mountains melt like wax before the LORD,
before the Lord of all the earth.

6The heavens declare His righteousness,
and all the peoples see His glory.

7Let all who serve carved images be put to shame,
who boast in idols;
bow down to Him, all gods.

8Zion hears and is glad,
and the daughters of Judah rejoice
because of Your judgments, LORD.

9For You, LORD, are Most High over all the earth;
You are exalted far above all gods.

10You who love the LORD, hate evil!
He guards the lives of His faithful ones;
He delivers them from the hand of the wicked.

11Light is sown for the righteous,
and joy for the upright in heart.

12Rejoice in the LORD, you righteous,
and give thanks to His holy name.

Notes

  • v7 "bow down to Him, all gods" — the Greek reads "all His angels," and Hebrews 1:6 quotes a line like it of the Son (compare the Greek of Deuteronomy 32:43).

speech.text: Psalms 97
The LORD reigns; let the earth rejoice; let the many coastlands be glad.
Clouds and thick darkness surround Him; righteousness and justice are the foundation of His throne.
Fire goes before Him and burns up His foes all around.
His lightnings light up the world; the earth sees and trembles.
The mountains melt like wax before the LORD, before the Lord of all the earth.
The heavens declare His righteousness, and all the peoples see His glory.
Let all who serve carved images be put to shame, who boast in idols; bow down to Him, all gods.
Zion hears and is glad, and the daughters of Judah rejoice because of Your judgments, LORD.
For You, LORD, are Most High over all the earth; You are exalted far above all gods.
You who love the LORD, hate evil! He guards the lives of His faithful ones; He delivers them from the hand of the wicked.
Light is sown for the righteous, and joy for the upright in heart.
Rejoice in the LORD, you righteous, and give thanks to His holy name.

chapters.title: He Comes to Judge the Earth
chapters.html:
Psalms 98

A psalm.

1Sing to the LORD a new song,
for He has done wonders;
His right hand and His holy arm
have won Him the victory.

2The LORD has made known His salvation;
He has revealed His righteousness in the sight of the nations.

3He has remembered His loyal love and His faithfulness
to the house of Israel;
all the ends of the earth have seen
the salvation of our God.

4Shout to the LORD, all the earth;
break out in joyful song and sing praises.

5Sing praises to the LORD with the lyre,
with the lyre and the sound of song.

6With trumpets and the sound of the ram's horn
shout before the King, the LORD.

7Let the sea roar, and all that fills it,
the world and those who live in it.

8Let the rivers clap their hands;
let the mountains sing for joy together

9before the LORD, for He comes to judge the earth.
He will judge the world in righteousness,
and the peoples with equity.

Notes

  • v3 "He has remembered His loyal love and His faithfulness to the house of Israel" — Mary's song takes this up: He has helped His servant Israel, in remembrance of His mercy (Luke 1:54).

speech.text: Psalms 98
Sing to the LORD a new song, for He has done wonders; His right hand and His holy arm have won Him the victory.
The LORD has made known His salvation; He has revealed His righteousness in the sight of the nations.
He has remembered His loyal love and His faithfulness to the house of Israel; all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.
Shout to the LORD, all the earth; break out in joyful song and sing praises.
Sing praises to the LORD with the lyre, with the lyre and the sound of song.
With trumpets and the sound of the ram's horn shout before the King, the LORD.
Let the sea roar, and all that fills it, the world and those who live in it.
Let the rivers clap their hands; let the mountains sing for joy together
before the LORD, for He comes to judge the earth. He will judge the world in righteousness, and the peoples with equity.

chapters.title: Holy Is He
chapters.html:
Psalms 99

1The LORD reigns; let the peoples tremble.
He is enthroned on the cherubim; let the earth quake.

2The LORD is great in Zion;
He is exalted over all the peoples.

3Let them praise Your name, great and awesome.
Holy is He!

4The strength of the King loves justice;
You have established equity;
You have done justice and righteousness in Jacob.

5Exalt the LORD our God,
and worship at His footstool.
Holy is He!

6Moses and Aaron were among His priests,
Samuel among those who called on His name;
they called to the LORD, and He answered them.

7He spoke to them in the pillar of cloud;
they kept His testimonies
and the statute He gave them.

8LORD our God, You answered them;
You were a forgiving God to them,
yet an avenger of their misdeeds.

9Exalt the LORD our God,
and worship at His holy mountain,
for the LORD our God is holy.

Notes

  • vv3, 5, 9 "Holy is He" — three times, ending each part of the psalm, like the threefold "Holy" of the seraphim (Isaiah 6:3).

speech.text: Psalms 99
The LORD reigns; let the peoples tremble. He is enthroned on the cherubim; let the earth quake.
The LORD is great in Zion; He is exalted over all the peoples.
Let them praise Your name, great and awesome. Holy is He!
The strength of the King loves justice; You have established equity; You have done justice and righteousness in Jacob.
Exalt the LORD our God, and worship at His footstool. Holy is He!
Moses and Aaron were among His priests, Samuel among those who called on His name; they called to the LORD, and He answered them.
He spoke to them in the pillar of cloud; they kept His testimonies and the statute He gave them.
LORD our God, You answered them; You were a forgiving God to them, yet an avenger of their misdeeds.
Exalt the LORD our God, and worship at His holy mountain, for the LORD our God is holy.

chapters.title: Enter His Gates with Thanksgiving
chapters.html:
Psalms 100

A psalm of thanksgiving.

1Shout to the LORD, all the earth.

2Serve the LORD with gladness;
come before Him with joyful singing.

3Know that the LORD, He is God.
It is He who made us, and we are His;
we are His people and the sheep of His pasture.

4Enter His gates with thanksgiving,
His courts with praise;
give thanks to Him, bless His name.

5For the LORD is good;
His loyal love endures forever,
and His faithfulness to all generations.

Notes

  • v3 "and we are His" — the read form, lo with vav; the written form, lo with aleph, gives "and not we ourselves," which the Greek follows.

speech.text: Psalms 100
Shout to the LORD, all the earth.
Serve the LORD with gladness; come before Him with joyful singing.
Know that the LORD, He is God. It is He who made us, and we are His; we are His people and the sheep of His pasture.
Enter His gates with thanksgiving, His courts with praise; give thanks to Him, bless His name.
For the LORD is good; His loyal love endures forever, and His faithfulness to all generations.

chapters.title: I Will Walk with a Blameless Heart
chapters.html:
Psalms 101

Of David. A psalm.

1I will sing of loyal love and justice;
to You, LORD, I will sing praises.

2I will give heed to the blameless way —
when will You come to me?
I will walk with a blameless heart
within my house.

3I will not set before my eyes
anything worthless.
I hate the work of those who fall away;
it will not cling to me.

4A perverse heart will be far from me;
I will have nothing to do with evil.

5Whoever slanders his neighbor in secret
I will destroy;
whoever has haughty eyes and a proud heart
I will not endure.

6My eyes will be on the faithful of the land,
so that they may live with me;
whoever walks in the blameless way
will serve me.

7No one who practices deceit
will live within my house;
no one who speaks lies
will stand before my eyes.

8Morning by morning I will destroy
all the wicked of the land,
cutting off all evildoers
from the city of the LORD.

Notes

  • The whole psalm — a king's vow, for his own life (vv2–4) and for his court and city (vv5–8). The pronouns for the king stay lowercase.

speech.text: Psalms 101
I will sing of loyal love and justice; to You, LORD, I will sing praises.
I will give heed to the blameless way — when will You come to me? I will walk with a blameless heart within my house.
I will not set before my eyes anything worthless. I hate the work of those who fall away; it will not cling to me.
A perverse heart will be far from me; I will have nothing to do with evil.
Whoever slanders his neighbor in secret I will destroy; whoever has haughty eyes and a proud heart I will not endure.
My eyes will be on the faithful of the land, so that they may live with me; whoever walks in the blameless way will serve me.
No one who practices deceit will live within my house; no one who speaks lies will stand before my eyes.
Morning by morning I will destroy all the wicked of the land, cutting off all evildoers from the city of the LORD.

chapters.title: You Remain
chapters.html:
Psalms 102

A prayer of one afflicted, when he is faint and pours out his complaint before the LORD.

1LORD, hear my prayer;
let my cry come to You.

2Do not hide Your face from me
in the day of my distress;
incline Your ear to me;
in the day I call, answer me quickly.

3For my days vanish like smoke,
and my bones burn like a furnace.

4My heart is struck down like grass and withered,
for I forget to eat my bread.

5Because of the sound of my groaning
my bones cling to my flesh.

6I am like a desert owl,
like an owl among the ruins.

7I lie awake;
I am like a lonely bird on a housetop.

8All day long my enemies taunt me;
those who mock me use my name as a curse.

9For I eat ashes like bread
and mix my drink with tears,

10because of Your indignation and Your wrath,
for You have lifted me up and thrown me aside.

11My days are like a lengthening shadow,
and I wither like grass.

12But You, LORD, are enthroned forever,
and Your renown is to all generations.

13You will arise and have compassion on Zion,
for it is time to be gracious to her;
the appointed time has come.

14For Your servants delight in her stones
and pity her dust.

15The nations will fear the name of the LORD,
and all the kings of the earth Your glory.

16For the LORD has built up Zion;
He has appeared in His glory.

17He has turned to the prayer of the destitute
and has not despised their prayer.

18Let this be written for a generation to come,
so that a people yet to be created may praise Yah.

19For He looked down from His holy height;
from heaven the LORD looked at the earth,

20to hear the groaning of the prisoner,
to set free those doomed to die,

21so that the name of the LORD may be declared in Zion,
and His praise in Jerusalem,

22when peoples gather together,
and kingdoms, to serve the LORD.

23He has broken my strength on the way;
He has cut short my days.

24I say, "My God, do not take me away
in the middle of my days —
You whose years go on through all generations.

25Long ago You laid the foundation of the earth,
and the heavens are the work of Your hands.

26They will perish, but You will remain;
they will all wear out like a garment.
Like clothing You will change them,
and they will pass away.

27But You are the same,
and Your years will have no end.

28The children of Your servants will live secure,
and their offspring will be established before You."

Notes

  • The title — not a name or a tune but a description of when to pray it; one of the seven penitential psalms of the church (6, 32, 38, 51, 102, 130, 143).

  • vv25–27 "Long ago You laid the foundation of the earth… You are the same" — Hebrews 1:10–12 quotes these lines from the Greek as spoken to the Son; Hebrews 13:8 echoes v27, Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.

speech.text: Psalms 102
LORD, hear my prayer; let my cry come to You.
Do not hide Your face from me in the day of my distress; incline Your ear to me; in the day I call, answer me quickly.
For my days vanish like smoke, and my bones burn like a furnace.
My heart is struck down like grass and withered, for I forget to eat my bread.
Because of the sound of my groaning my bones cling to my flesh.
I am like a desert owl, like an owl among the ruins.
I lie awake; I am like a lonely bird on a housetop.
All day long my enemies taunt me; those who mock me use my name as a curse.
For I eat ashes like bread and mix my drink with tears,
because of Your indignation and Your wrath, for You have lifted me up and thrown me aside.
My days are like a lengthening shadow, and I wither like grass.
But You, LORD, are enthroned forever, and Your renown is to all generations.
You will arise and have compassion on Zion, for it is time to be gracious to her; the appointed time has come.
For Your servants delight in her stones and pity her dust.
The nations will fear the name of the LORD, and all the kings of the earth Your glory.
For the LORD has built up Zion; He has appeared in His glory.
He has turned to the prayer of the destitute and has not despised their prayer.
Let this be written for a generation to come, so that a people yet to be created may praise Yah.
For He looked down from His holy height; from heaven the LORD looked at the earth,
to hear the groaning of the prisoner, to set free those doomed to die,
so that the name of the LORD may be declared in Zion, and His praise in Jerusalem,
when peoples gather together, and kingdoms, to serve the LORD.
He has broken my strength on the way; He has cut short my days.
I say, "My God, do not take me away in the middle of my days — You whose years go on through all generations.
Long ago You laid the foundation of the earth, and the heavens are the work of Your hands.
They will perish, but You will remain; they will all wear out like a garment. Like clothing You will change them, and they will pass away.
But You are the same, and Your years will have no end.
The children of Your servants will live secure, and their offspring will be established before You."

chapters.title: Bless the LORD, My Soul
chapters.html:
Psalms 103

Of David.

1Bless the LORD, my soul,
and all that is within me, bless His holy name.

2Bless the LORD, my soul,
and do not forget all His benefits —

3who forgives all your iniquity,
who heals all your diseases,

4who redeems your life from the pit,
who crowns you with loyal love and compassion,

5who satisfies your years with good things,
so that your youth is renewed like the eagle's.

6The LORD works righteousness
and justice for all who are oppressed.

7He made known His ways to Moses,
His deeds to the children of Israel.

8The LORD is merciful and gracious,
slow to anger, and abundant in loyal love.

9He will not always accuse,
nor will He keep His anger forever.

10He has not dealt with us according to our sins,
nor repaid us according to our iniquities.

11For as high as the heavens are above the earth,
so great is His loyal love toward those who fear Him;

12as far as the east is from the west,
so far has He removed our transgressions from us.

13As a father has compassion on his children,
so the LORD has compassion on those who fear Him.

14For He knows how we are formed;
He remembers that we are dust.

15As for man, his days are like grass;
he flourishes like a flower of the field;

16when the wind passes over it, it is gone,
and its place knows it no more.

17But the loyal love of the LORD
is from everlasting to everlasting on those who fear Him,
and His righteousness to children's children,

18to those who keep His covenant
and remember His precepts to do them.

19The LORD has established His throne in the heavens,
and His kingdom rules over all.

20Bless the LORD, you His messengers,
mighty in strength, who do His word,
obeying the voice of His word.

21Bless the LORD, all His hosts,
His servants who do His will.

22Bless the LORD, all His works,
in all places of His dominion.
Bless the LORD, my soul.

Notes

  • v8 "merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abundant in loyal love" — the words of Exodus 34:6, as in 86:15, with "The LORD" for "God" and without "and truth."

speech.text: Psalms 103
Bless the LORD, my soul, and all that is within me, bless His holy name.
Bless the LORD, my soul, and do not forget all His benefits —
who forgives all your iniquity, who heals all your diseases,
who redeems your life from the pit, who crowns you with loyal love and compassion,
who satisfies your years with good things, so that your youth is renewed like the eagle's.
The LORD works righteousness and justice for all who are oppressed.
He made known His ways to Moses, His deeds to the children of Israel.
The LORD is merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abundant in loyal love.
He will not always accuse, nor will He keep His anger forever.
He has not dealt with us according to our sins, nor repaid us according to our iniquities.
For as high as the heavens are above the earth, so great is His loyal love toward those who fear Him;
as far as the east is from the west, so far has He removed our transgressions from us.
As a father has compassion on his children, so the LORD has compassion on those who fear Him.
For He knows how we are formed; He remembers that we are dust.
As for man, his days are like grass; he flourishes like a flower of the field;
when the wind passes over it, it is gone, and its place knows it no more.
But the loyal love of the LORD is from everlasting to everlasting on those who fear Him, and His righteousness to children's children,
to those who keep His covenant and remember His precepts to do them.
The LORD has established His throne in the heavens, and His kingdom rules over all.
Bless the LORD, you His messengers, mighty in strength, who do His word, obeying the voice of His word.
Bless the LORD, all His hosts, His servants who do His will.
Bless the LORD, all His works, in all places of His dominion. Bless the LORD, my soul.

chapters.title: How Many Are Your Works
chapters.html:
Psalms 104

1Bless the LORD, my soul.
LORD my God, You are very great;
You are clothed with splendor and majesty,

2wrapping Yourself in light as in a garment,
stretching out the heavens like a tent curtain.

3He lays the beams of His upper rooms on the waters;
He makes the clouds His chariot;
He walks on the wings of the wind.

4He makes the winds His messengers,
flames of fire His servants.

5He set the earth on its foundations,
so that it will never be moved.

6You covered it with the deep as with a garment;
the waters stood above the mountains.

7At Your rebuke they fled;
at the sound of Your thunder they hurried away.

8The mountains rose, the valleys sank down
to the place You appointed for them.

9You set a boundary they may not pass,
so that they will not again cover the earth.

10He sends springs into the valleys;
they flow between the hills.

11They give drink to every beast of the field;
the wild donkeys quench their thirst.

12Beside them the birds of the heavens dwell;
they sing among the branches.

13He waters the mountains from His upper rooms;
the earth is satisfied with the fruit of Your works.

14He makes grass grow for the cattle
and plants for people to cultivate,
to bring forth food from the earth,

15wine that gladdens the human heart,
oil to make the face shine,
and bread that strengthens the human heart.

16The trees of the LORD are well watered,
the cedars of Lebanon that He planted,

17where the birds make their nests;
the stork has its home in the fir trees.

18The high mountains are for the wild goats;
the rocks are a refuge for the rock badgers.

19He made the moon to mark the seasons;
the sun knows its time for setting.

20You make darkness, and it is night,
when all the beasts of the forest creep about.

21The young lions roar for their prey,
seeking their food from God.

22When the sun rises, they withdraw
and lie down in their dens.

23People go out to their work
and to their labor until evening.

24How many are Your works, LORD!
In wisdom You have made them all;
the earth is full of Your creatures.

25There is the sea, great and wide,
teeming with creatures beyond number,
living things both small and great.

26There the ships go,
and Leviathan, which You formed to play in it.

27All of them look to You
to give them their food in due season.

28When You give it to them, they gather it up;
when You open Your hand, they are satisfied with good things.

29When You hide Your face, they are dismayed;
when You take away their breath, they die
and return to their dust.

30When You send out Your Spirit, they are created,
and You renew the face of the ground.

31May the glory of the LORD endure forever;
may the LORD rejoice in His works,

32who looks on the earth, and it trembles,
who touches the mountains, and they smoke.

33I will sing to the LORD as long as I live;
I will sing praises to my God while I have being.

34May my meditation be pleasing to Him;
I will rejoice in the LORD.

35Let sinners be consumed from the earth,
and let the wicked be no more.
Bless the LORD, my soul.
Praise Yah!

Notes

  • The whole psalm — creation sung in roughly the order of Genesis 1: light (v2), the heavens (v2), the waters separated and the land (vv5–9), plants (v14), sun and moon (v19), sea creatures (v25), animals and people (vv21–23), and God's breath giving life (vv29–30).

  • vv29–30 "their breath… Your Spirit" — the same word, ruach: God takes away their breath and they die; He sends His Spirit and they are created (Genesis 2:7; Job 34:14–15).

chapters.title: He Remembered His Covenant Forever
chapters.html:
Psalms 105

1Give thanks to the LORD, call on His name;
make known His deeds among the peoples.

2Sing to Him, sing praises to Him;
tell of all His wonders.

3Glory in His holy name;
let the hearts of those who seek the LORD rejoice.

4Seek the LORD and His strength;
seek His face continually.

5Remember the wonders He has done,
His signs and the judgments of His mouth,

6seed of Abraham His servant,
sons of Jacob, His chosen ones!

7He is the LORD our God;
His judgments are in all the earth.

8He has remembered His covenant forever,
the word He commanded for a thousand generations,

9the covenant He made with Abraham,
His oath to Isaac,

10which He confirmed to Jacob as a statute,
to Israel as an everlasting covenant,

11saying, "To you I will give the land of Canaan
as the portion of your inheritance,"

12when they were few in number,
very few, and guests in it,

13and they wandered from nation to nation,
from one kingdom to another people.

14He allowed no one to oppress them;
He rebuked kings on their account:

15"Do not touch My anointed ones,
and do My prophets no harm."

16He called down famine on the land;
He broke every staff of bread.

17He sent a man ahead of them —
Joseph, sold as a slave.

18They hurt his feet with fetters;
his neck was put in iron,

19until the time his word came to pass;
the word of the LORD tested him.

20The king sent and released him;
the ruler of peoples set him free.

21He made him lord of his house
and ruler over all his possessions,

22to bind his princes at his will
and to teach his elders wisdom.

23Then Israel came to Egypt;
Jacob lived as a guest in the land of Ham.

24He made His people very fruitful
and made them stronger than their foes.

25He turned their hearts to hate His people,
to deal craftily with His servants.

26He sent Moses His servant,
and Aaron, whom He had chosen.

27They performed His signs among them,
and wonders in the land of Ham.

28He sent darkness and made it dark;
they did not rebel against His word.

29He turned their waters into blood
and caused their fish to die.

30Their land swarmed with frogs,
even in the chambers of their kings.

31He spoke, and there came swarms of flies,
and gnats throughout their country.

32He gave them hail for rain,
flaming fire in their land.

33He struck their vines and fig trees
and shattered the trees of their country.

34He spoke, and the locusts came,
young locusts without number,

35which ate up all the plants in their land
and devoured the fruit of their ground.

36He struck all the firstborn in their land,
the first fruits of all their strength.

37He brought them out with silver and gold,
and among His tribes no one stumbled.

38Egypt was glad when they left,
for dread of them had fallen on it.

39He spread a cloud for a covering,
and fire to give light by night.

40They asked, and He brought quail,
and satisfied them with the bread of heaven.

41He opened the rock, and water gushed out;
it flowed through the desert like a river.

42For He remembered His holy promise
to Abraham His servant.

43He brought out His people with joy,
His chosen ones with singing.

44He gave them the lands of the nations,
and they took possession of what the peoples had labored for,

45so that they might keep His statutes
and observe His laws.
Praise Yah!

Notes

  • vv1–15 — the first part of the song David appointed for the ark (1 Chronicles 16:8–22), and the English there is followed. Where the Hebrew differs, so does the English: v6 "seed of Abraham" for "seed of Israel"; v8 "He has remembered" for "Remember"; v12 "when they were" for "when you were." "O" is dropped from v6, as everywhere in the Psalms.

  • vv28–36 — eight of the plagues, beginning with darkness, the ninth in Exodus 10:21–23, and in a different order; the plagues on livestock and the boils are left out.

chapters.title: We Have Sinned, Like Our Fathers
chapters.html:
Psalms 106

1Praise Yah!
Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good,
for His loyal love endures forever.

2Who can speak of the mighty deeds of the LORD,
or make all His praise heard?

3Blessed are those who keep justice,
who do righteousness at all times.

4Remember me, LORD, when You show favor to Your people;
visit me with Your salvation,

5so that I may see the prosperity of Your chosen ones,
rejoice in the gladness of Your nation,
and glory with Your inheritance.

6We have sinned, like our fathers;
we have done wrong; we have acted wickedly.

7Our fathers in Egypt did not consider Your wonders;
they did not remember the abundance of Your loyal love,
but rebelled by the sea, at the Sea of Reeds.

8Yet He saved them for His name's sake,
to make His might known.

9He rebuked the Sea of Reeds, and it dried up;
He led them through the depths as through a wilderness.

10He saved them from the hand of the one who hated them
and redeemed them from the hand of the enemy.

11The waters covered their foes;
not one of them was left.

12Then they believed His words;
they sang His praise.

13But they soon forgot His works;
they did not wait for His counsel.

14They gave in to craving in the wilderness
and tested God in the desert.

15He gave them what they asked
but sent leanness into their souls.

16They envied Moses in the camp,
and Aaron, the holy one of the LORD.

17The earth opened and swallowed Dathan
and covered the company of Abiram.

18Fire blazed among their company;
flame burned up the wicked.

19They made a calf at Horeb
and bowed down to a cast image.

20They exchanged their Glory
for the image of an ox that eats grass.

21They forgot God their Savior,
who had done great things in Egypt,

22wonders in the land of Ham,
awesome deeds by the Sea of Reeds.

23So He said He would destroy them —
had not Moses His chosen one
stood in the breach before Him
to turn away His wrath from destroying them.

24Then they despised the pleasant land;
they did not believe His word.

25They grumbled in their tents
and did not listen to the voice of the LORD.

26So He raised His hand against them
to make them fall in the wilderness,

27to make their offspring fall among the nations
and to scatter them in the lands.

28They joined themselves to the Baal of Peor
and ate sacrifices offered to the dead.

29They provoked Him with their deeds,
and a plague broke out among them.

30Then Phinehas stood up and intervened,
and the plague was stopped.

31It was counted to him as righteousness
from generation to generation forever.

32They angered Him at the waters of Meribah,
and it went badly with Moses because of them,

33for they rebelled against His Spirit,
and he spoke rashly with his lips.

34They did not destroy the peoples,
as the LORD had commanded them,

35but mingled with the nations
and learned their ways.

36They served their idols,
which became a snare to them.

37They sacrificed their sons
and their daughters to demons.

38They poured out innocent blood,
the blood of their sons and daughters,
whom they sacrificed to the idols of Canaan,
and the land was defiled with blood.

39They became unclean by their deeds
and were unfaithful in their practices.

40So the anger of the LORD burned against His people,
and He abhorred His inheritance.

41He gave them into the hand of the nations,
and those who hated them ruled over them.

42Their enemies oppressed them,
and they were brought low under their power.

43Many times He delivered them,
but they rebelled in their schemes
and sank low in their iniquity.

44Yet He looked on their distress
when He heard their cry.

45He remembered His covenant for their sake
and relented according to the abundance of His loyal love.

46He caused them to be pitied
by all who held them captive.

47Save us, LORD our God,
and gather us from the nations,
to give thanks to Your holy name
and to glory in Your praise.

48Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel,
from everlasting to everlasting!
Let all the people say, "Amen."
Praise Yah!

Notes

  • vv1, 47–48 — the close of the song David appointed for the ark (1 Chronicles 16:34–36), and the English there is followed. Where the Hebrew differs, so does the English: v47 "LORD our God" for "God of our salvation," without "and deliver us"; v48 "Let all the people say" for "Then all the people said."

  • v33 "they rebelled against His Spirit, and he spoke rashly" — the Hebrew says only "his spirit"; most take the spirit to be God's (Isaiah 63:10). The one who spoke rashly is Moses (Numbers 20:10–12). The Greek reads "they embittered his spirit," of Moses.

  • v48 — the blessing that closes the fourth book of the Psalms.

chapters.title: Let the Redeemed of the LORD Say So
chapters.html:
Psalms 107

1Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good,
for His loyal love endures forever.

2Let the redeemed of the LORD say so,
those He redeemed from the hand of the foe

3and gathered from the lands,
from the east and from the west,
from the north and from the sea.

4Some wandered in the wilderness, on a desert track;
they found no city to live in.

5Hungry and thirsty,
their soul fainted within them.

6Then they cried out to the LORD in their trouble,
and He delivered them from their distress.

7He led them by a straight way
to reach a city to live in.

8Let them give thanks to the LORD for His loyal love
and His wonders for the children of man.

9For He satisfies the thirsty soul
and fills the hungry soul with good things.

10Some sat in darkness and the shadow of death,
prisoners in affliction and iron,

11because they had rebelled against the words of God
and despised the counsel of the Most High.

12So He humbled their hearts with hard labor;
they stumbled, and there was no one to help.

13Then they cried out to the LORD in their trouble,
and He saved them from their distress.

14He brought them out of darkness and the shadow of death
and broke their chains apart.

15Let them give thanks to the LORD for His loyal love
and His wonders for the children of man.

16For He shatters doors of bronze
and cuts through bars of iron.

17Some were fools through their rebellious ways
and were afflicted because of their iniquities.

18Their soul abhorred all food,
and they drew near to the gates of death.

19Then they cried out to the LORD in their trouble,
and He saved them from their distress.

20He sent His word and healed them
and delivered them from their destruction.

21Let them give thanks to the LORD for His loyal love
and His wonders for the children of man.

22Let them offer sacrifices of thanksgiving
and tell of His works with songs of joy.

23Some went down to the sea in ships,
doing business on the great waters.

24They saw the works of the LORD,
His wonders in the deep.

25He spoke and raised a stormy wind,
which lifted up its waves.

26They rose up to the heavens; they went down to the depths;
their soul melted away in their trouble.

27They reeled and staggered like a drunken man,
and all their skill was swallowed up.

28Then they cried out to the LORD in their trouble,
and He brought them out of their distress.

29He made the storm a whisper,
and their waves were hushed.

30They were glad because they grew quiet,
and He guided them to their desired haven.

31Let them give thanks to the LORD for His loyal love
and His wonders for the children of man.

32Let them exalt Him in the assembly of the people
and praise Him in the council of the elders.

33He turns rivers into a desert,
springs of water into thirsty ground,

34a fruitful land into a salt waste,
because of the wickedness of those who live there.

35He turns a desert into pools of water,
a dry land into springs of water.

36There He settles the hungry,
and they establish a city to live in.

37They sow fields and plant vineyards
and gather a fruitful harvest.

38He blesses them, and they multiply greatly,
and He does not let their cattle decrease.

39When they are diminished and brought low
through oppression, trouble and sorrow,

40He pours contempt on nobles
and makes them wander in a trackless waste.

41But He lifts the needy out of affliction
and makes their families like flocks.

42The upright see it and are glad,
and injustice shuts its mouth.

43Whoever is wise, let him heed these things
and consider the loyal love of the LORD.

Notes

  • v1 — the fifth book of the Psalms opens with the same words as 106:1, answering the prayer of 106:47, gather us from the nations: here the redeemed have been gathered (v3).

  • vv25–30 — the storm and the calm; the Gospels tell of Jesus rebuking the wind and the waves, and there was a great calm (Mark 4:39).

chapters.title: My Heart Is Steadfast
chapters.html:
Psalms 108

A song. A psalm of David.

1My heart is steadfast, God;
I will sing and make music, with all my glory.

2Wake up, harp and lyre!
I will wake the dawn.

3I will give thanks to You, LORD, among the peoples;
I will sing praises to You among the nations.

4For Your loyal love is great, above the heavens,
and Your truth reaches to the clouds.

5Be exalted above the heavens, God;
let Your glory be over all the earth.

6So that Your beloved ones may be rescued,
save with Your right hand, and answer me.

7God has spoken in His holiness:
"I will exult; I will divide Shechem
and measure out the Valley of Succoth.

8Gilead is Mine, and Manasseh is Mine;
Ephraim is the helmet of My head;
Judah is My scepter.

9Moab is My washbasin;
on Edom I throw My sandal;
over Philistia I shout in triumph."

10Who will bring me to the fortified city?
Who will lead me to Edom?

11Have You not rejected us, God?
You do not go out, God, with our armies.

12Give us help against the foe,
for the salvation of man is worthless.

13With God we will do valiantly,
and He will trample our foes.

Notes

  • The whole psalm — joined from two earlier psalms: vv1–5 are 57:7–11 and vv6–13 are 60:5–12, and the English there is followed. Where the Hebrew differs, so does the English: v1 has "My heart is steadfast" once and adds "with all my glory"; v2 drops "Wake up, my glory!"; v3 has "LORD" for "Lord"; v4 has "above the heavens" for "reaching to the heavens"; v9 has "over Philistia I shout in triumph" for "Philistia, shout in triumph over Me!"

I will give thanks to You, LORD, among the peoples; I will sing praises to You among the nations.
For Your loyal love is great, above the heavens, and Your truth reaches to the clouds.
Be exalted above the heavens, God; let Your glory be over all the earth.
So that Your beloved ones may be rescued, save with Your right hand, and answer me.

chapters.title: God of My Praise, Do Not Keep Silent
chapters.html:
Psalms 109

For the director. Of David. A psalm.

1God of my praise,
do not keep silent,

2for a wicked mouth and a deceitful mouth
have opened against me;
they have spoken against me with a lying tongue.

3They surround me with words of hatred
and fight against me without cause.

4In return for my love they accuse me,
but I am prayer.

5They repay me evil for good,
and hatred for my love.

6Appoint a wicked man over him;
let an accuser stand at his right hand.

7When he is judged, let him come out guilty,
and let his prayer become sin.

8Let his days be few;
let another take his office.

9Let his children be fatherless
and his wife a widow.

10Let his children wander about and beg,
seeking food far from their ruined homes.

11Let the creditor seize all that he has,
and let strangers plunder the fruit of his labor.

12Let there be no one to extend loyal love to him,
nor anyone to pity his fatherless children.

13Let his descendants be cut off;
in the next generation let their name be blotted out.

14Let the iniquity of his fathers be remembered before the LORD,
and let not the sin of his mother be blotted out.

15Let them be before the LORD continually,
and may He cut off their memory from the earth,

16because he did not remember to show loyal love,
but pursued the poor and needy man
and the brokenhearted, to put them to death.

17He loved cursing — let it come on him;
he did not delight in blessing — let it be far from him.

18He clothed himself with cursing as with his garment;
let it soak into his body like water,
like oil into his bones.

19Let it be to him like a garment he wraps around himself,
like a belt he always wears.

20This is the reward of my accusers from the LORD,
of those who speak evil against my life.

21But You, GOD the Lord,
deal with me for Your name's sake;
because Your loyal love is good, deliver me.

22For I am poor and needy,
and my heart is wounded within me.

23I am gone like a shadow at evening;
I am shaken off like a locust.

24My knees are weak through fasting;
my flesh has grown lean, with no fat.

25I have become a reproach to them;
when they see me, they shake their heads.

26Help me, LORD my God;
save me according to Your loyal love,

27so that they may know that this is Your hand;
You, LORD, have done it.

28Let them curse, but You will bless;
when they rise up, let them be put to shame,
but let Your servant rejoice.

29Let my accusers be clothed with disgrace;
let them wrap themselves in their shame as in a cloak.

30With my mouth I will give great thanks to the LORD;
I will praise Him among the many.

31For He stands at the right hand of the needy,
to save him from those who judge his soul.

Notes

  • vv4, 6, 20, 29 "accuse… an accuser… my accusers" — all the same root, satan. In v6 the word stands without the article, a prosecutor at the right hand in court (Zechariah 3:1); the Greek has diabolos.

  • v8 "let another take his office" — Peter applies this to Judas (Acts 1:20), with 69:25.

chapters.title: Sit at My Right Hand
chapters.html:
Psalms 110

Of David. A psalm.

1The LORD says to my lord:
"Sit at My right hand
until I make your enemies
a footstool for your feet."

2The LORD will send out from Zion
your mighty scepter;
rule among your enemies!

3Your people will offer themselves freely
on the day of your power,
in holy splendor;
from the womb of the dawn,
the dew of your youth is yours.

4The LORD has sworn
and will not change His mind:
"You are a priest forever
after the order of Melchizedek."

5The Lord is at your right hand;
He will shatter kings on the day of His wrath.

6He will judge among the nations,
filling them with corpses;
He will shatter the head over the wide earth.

7He will drink from the brook by the way;
so he will lift up his head.

Notes

  • v1 "The LORD says to my lord" — neum YHWH la'doni: the LORD speaks to the king, David's "lord." The king's pronouns stay lowercase here, as in Psalms 2 and 45. Jesus asks how David's son can be David's Lord (Matthew 22:41–45), and it is among the Old Testament verses the New Testament quotes most often (Acts 2:34–35; 1 Corinthians 15:25; Hebrews 1:13; 10:12–13).

  • v4 "You are a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek" — the king of Salem who was also priest of God Most High (Genesis 14:18–20); Hebrews 5–7 builds its teaching on Christ's priesthood on this verse.

speech.text: Psalms 110
The LORD says to my lord: "Sit at My right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet."
The LORD will send out from Zion your mighty scepter; rule among your enemies!
Your people will offer themselves freely on the day of your power, in holy splendor; from the womb of the dawn, the dew of your youth is yours.
The LORD has sworn and will not change His mind: "You are a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek."
The Lord is at your right hand; He will shatter kings on the day of His wrath.
He will judge among the nations, filling them with corpses; He will shatter the head over the wide earth.
He will drink from the brook by the way; so he will lift up his head.

chapters.title: The Fear of the LORD Is the Beginning of Wisdom
chapters.html:
Psalms 111

1Praise Yah!
I will give thanks to the LORD with all my heart,
in the council of the upright and in the congregation.

2Great are the works of the LORD,
studied by all who delight in them.

3Splendor and majesty are His work,
and His righteousness endures forever.

4He has made His wonders to be remembered;
the LORD is gracious and merciful.

5He gives food to those who fear Him;
He remembers His covenant forever.

6He has shown His people the power of His works,
giving them the inheritance of the nations.

7The works of His hands are truth and justice;
all His precepts are trustworthy.

8They stand firm forever and ever,
done in truth and uprightness.

9He sent redemption to His people;
He has commanded His covenant forever.
Holy and awesome is His name.

10The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom;
all who practice it have good understanding.
His praise endures forever.

Notes

  • The form — an acrostic: after "Praise Yah!", each of the twenty-two half-lines begins with the next letter of the Hebrew alphabet. Psalm 112 has the same form and is its twin.

  • v10 "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom" — as in Proverbs 9:10 and Job 28:28; Proverbs 1:7 has "knowledge."

speech.text: Psalms 111
Praise Yah! I will give thanks to the LORD with all my heart, in the council of the upright and in the congregation.
Great are the works of the LORD, studied by all who delight in them.
Splendor and majesty are His work, and His righteousness endures forever.
He has made His wonders to be remembered; the LORD is gracious and merciful.
He gives food to those who fear Him; He remembers His covenant forever.
He has shown His people the power of His works, giving them the inheritance of the nations.
The works of His hands are truth and justice; all His precepts are trustworthy.
They stand firm forever and ever, done in truth and uprightness.
He sent redemption to His people; He has commanded His covenant forever. Holy and awesome is His name.
The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom; all who practice it have good understanding. His praise endures forever.

chapters.title: Blessed Is the Man Who Fears the LORD
chapters.html:
Psalms 112

1Praise Yah!
Blessed is the man who fears the LORD,
who greatly delights in His commandments.

2His offspring will be mighty in the land;
the generation of the upright will be blessed.

3Wealth and riches are in his house,
and his righteousness endures forever.

4Light dawns in the darkness for the upright;
he is gracious, merciful and righteous.

5It goes well with the man who is gracious and lends,
who conducts his affairs with justice.

6For he will never be moved;
the righteous will be remembered forever.

7He is not afraid of bad news;
his heart is steadfast, trusting in the LORD.

8His heart is firm; he will not be afraid,
until he looks in triumph on his foes.

9He has scattered abroad; he has given to the poor;
his righteousness endures forever;
his horn will be lifted high in honor.

10The wicked man sees it and is angry;
he gnashes his teeth and melts away;
the desire of the wicked will perish.

Notes

  • The form — an acrostic, the twin of Psalm 111: what 111 says of God, 112 says of the one who fears Him. "His righteousness endures forever" (111:3; 112:3, 9) and "gracious and merciful" (111:4; 112:4) are used of both.

speech.text: Psalms 112
Praise Yah! Blessed is the man who fears the LORD, who greatly delights in His commandments.
His offspring will be mighty in the land; the generation of the upright will be blessed.
Wealth and riches are in his house, and his righteousness endures forever.
Light dawns in the darkness for the upright; he is gracious, merciful and righteous.
It goes well with the man who is gracious and lends, who conducts his affairs with justice.
For he will never be moved; the righteous will be remembered forever.
He is not afraid of bad news; his heart is steadfast, trusting in the LORD.
His heart is firm; he will not be afraid, until he looks in triumph on his foes.
He has scattered abroad; he has given to the poor; his righteousness endures forever; his horn will be lifted high in honor.
The wicked man sees it and is angry; he gnashes his teeth and melts away; the desire of the wicked will perish.

chapters.title: Who Is Like the LORD Our God
chapters.html:
Psalms 113

1Praise Yah!
Praise, servants of the LORD;
praise the name of the LORD.

2Blessed be the name of the LORD
from this time forth and forever.

3From the rising of the sun to its setting,
the name of the LORD is to be praised.

4The LORD is high above all nations,
His glory above the heavens.

5Who is like the LORD our God,
who is enthroned on high,

6who stoops down to look
on the heavens and the earth?

7He raises the poor from the dust;
He lifts the needy from the ash heap,

8to seat them with nobles,
with the nobles of His people.

9He gives the barren woman a home,
a joyful mother of children.
Praise Yah!

Notes

  • v1 and Psalms 113–118 — the Hallel, "Praise," sung at the great feasts and at the Passover meal; the "hymn" Jesus and the disciples sang before going out to the Mount of Olives was likely its second part (Matthew 26:30).

speech.text: Psalms 113
Praise Yah! Praise, servants of the LORD; praise the name of the LORD.
Blessed be the name of the LORD from this time forth and forever.
From the rising of the sun to its setting, the name of the LORD is to be praised.
The LORD is high above all nations, His glory above the heavens.
Who is like the LORD our God, who is enthroned on high,
who stoops down to look on the heavens and the earth?
He raises the poor from the dust; He lifts the needy from the ash heap,
to seat them with nobles, with the nobles of His people.
He gives the barren woman a home, a joyful mother of children. Praise Yah!

chapters.title: When Israel Went Out from Egypt
chapters.html:
Psalms 114

1When Israel went out from Egypt,
the house of Jacob from a people of strange speech,

2Judah became His sanctuary,
Israel His dominion.

3The sea saw and fled;
the Jordan turned back.

4The mountains skipped like rams,
the hills like lambs.

5What ails you, sea, that you flee?
Jordan, that you turn back?

6Mountains, that you skip like rams?
Hills, like lambs?

7Tremble, earth, before the Lord,
before the God of Jacob,

8who turns the rock into a pool of water,
the flint into a spring of water.

Notes

  • v1 and the numbering — the Greek Psalter joins 114 and 115 as one psalm and splits 116 into two; the Hebrew numbering is followed.

speech.text: Psalms 114
When Israel went out from Egypt, the house of Jacob from a people of strange speech,
Judah became His sanctuary, Israel His dominion.
The sea saw and fled; the Jordan turned back.
The mountains skipped like rams, the hills like lambs.
What ails you, sea, that you flee? Jordan, that you turn back?
Mountains, that you skip like rams? Hills, like lambs?
Tremble, earth, before the Lord, before the God of Jacob,
who turns the rock into a pool of water, the flint into a spring of water.

chapters.title: Not to Us, LORD
chapters.html:
Psalms 115

1Not to us, LORD, not to us,
but to Your name give glory,
for the sake of Your loyal love and Your truth.

2Why should the nations say,
"Where is their God?"

3Our God is in the heavens;
He does whatever He pleases.

4Their idols are silver and gold,
the work of human hands.

5They have mouths but do not speak;
eyes, but do not see;

6they have ears but do not hear;
noses, but do not smell;

7they have hands but do not feel;
feet, but do not walk;
they make no sound in their throats.

8Those who make them will become like them,
and so will all who trust in them.

9Israel, trust in the LORD!
He is their help and their shield.

10House of Aaron, trust in the LORD!
He is their help and their shield.

11You who fear the LORD, trust in the LORD!
He is their help and their shield.

12The LORD has remembered us; He will bless us;
He will bless the house of Israel;
He will bless the house of Aaron;

13He will bless those who fear the LORD,
the small together with the great.

14May the LORD give you increase,
you and your children.

15May you be blessed by the LORD,
the Maker of heaven and earth.

16The heavens are the LORD's heavens,
but the earth He has given to the children of man.

17The dead do not praise Yah,
nor do any who go down into silence.

18But we will bless Yah
from this time forth and forevermore.
Praise Yah!

Notes

  • v8 "Those who make them will become like them" — people become like what they worship: blind, deaf and lifeless.

chapters.title: What Shall I Return to the LORD
chapters.html:
Psalms 116

1I love the LORD,
because He hears my voice and my pleas.

2Because He has inclined His ear to me,
I will call on Him as long as I live.

3The cords of death surrounded me;
the distresses of Sheol found me;
I found trouble and sorrow.

4Then I called on the name of the LORD:
"Please, LORD, deliver my soul!"

5Gracious is the LORD, and righteous;
our God is merciful.

6The LORD guards the simple;
I was brought low, and He saved me.

7Return to your rest, my soul,
for the LORD has dealt bountifully with you.

8For You have delivered my soul from death,
my eyes from tears,
my feet from stumbling.

9I will walk before the LORD
in the land of the living.

10I believed, even when I said,
"I am greatly afflicted";

11I said in my alarm,
"All mankind are liars."

12What shall I return to the LORD
for all His benefits to me?

13I will lift up the cup of salvation
and call on the name of the LORD.

14I will pay my vows to the LORD
in the presence of all His people.

15Precious in the sight of the LORD
is the death of His faithful ones.

16Please, LORD, truly I am Your servant;
I am Your servant, the son of Your maidservant;
You have loosed my bonds.

17I will offer You a sacrifice of thanksgiving
and call on the name of the LORD.

18I will pay my vows to the LORD
in the presence of all His people,

19in the courts of the house of the LORD,
within you, Jerusalem.
Praise Yah!

Notes

  • v15 "Precious in the sight of the LORD is the death of His faithful ones" — precious, that is, costly: God does not let it happen lightly (72:14).

chapters.title: Praise the LORD, All Nations
chapters.html:
Psalms 117

1Praise the LORD, all nations!
Extol Him, all peoples!

2For great is His loyal love toward us,
and the truth of the LORD endures forever.
Praise Yah!

Notes

  • The whole psalm — the shortest in the Psalms, and the shortest chapter in the Bible.

  • v1 "Praise the LORD, all nations" — Paul quotes it to show that the nations were always meant to praise Israel's God (Romans 15:11).

speech.text: Psalms 117
Praise the LORD, all nations! Extol Him, all peoples!
For great is His loyal love toward us, and the truth of the LORD endures forever. Praise Yah!

chapters.title: This Is the Day the LORD Has Made
chapters.html:
Psalms 118

1Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good,
for His loyal love endures forever.

2Let Israel say,
"His loyal love endures forever."

3Let the house of Aaron say,
"His loyal love endures forever."

4Let those who fear the LORD say,
"His loyal love endures forever."

5Out of my distress I called on Yah;
Yah answered me and set me in a broad place.

6The LORD is on my side; I will not fear.
What can man do to me?

7The LORD is on my side as my helper;
I will look in triumph on those who hate me.

8It is better to take refuge in the LORD
than to trust in man.

9It is better to take refuge in the LORD
than to trust in nobles.

10All nations surrounded me;
in the name of the LORD I cut them off.

11They surrounded me, yes, they surrounded me;
in the name of the LORD I cut them off.

12They surrounded me like bees;
they were put out like a fire of thorns;
in the name of the LORD I cut them off.

13You pushed me hard so that I was falling,
but the LORD helped me.

14My strength and my song is Yah,
and He has become my deliverance.

15The sound of joyful shouting and deliverance
is in the tents of the righteous:
"The right hand of the LORD does valiantly!

16The right hand of the LORD is exalted;
the right hand of the LORD does valiantly!"

17I will not die, but live,
and tell of the works of Yah.

18Yah has disciplined me severely,
but He has not given me over to death.

19Open to me the gates of righteousness;
I will enter through them and give thanks to Yah.

20This is the gate of the LORD;
the righteous will enter through it.

21I will give thanks to You, for You have answered me
and have become my deliverance.

22The stone the builders rejected
has become the cornerstone.

23This is the LORD's doing;
it is marvelous in our eyes.

24This is the day the LORD has made;
let us rejoice and be glad in it.

25Please, LORD, save us!
Please, LORD, give us success!

26Blessed is he who comes in the name of the LORD!
We bless you from the house of the LORD.

27The LORD is God, and He has given us light.
Bind the festal sacrifice with cords,
up to the horns of the altar.

28You are my God, and I will give thanks to You;
my God, I will exalt You.

29Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good,
for His loyal love endures forever.

Notes

  • v22 "The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone" — Jesus applies it to Himself (Matthew 21:42), and so do Peter (Acts 4:11; 1 Peter 2:7) and Paul (Ephesians 2:20).

  • v25 "Please, LORD, save us!" — hoshi'ah na, "hosanna," the cry of the crowds on Palm Sunday (Matthew 21:9).

Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good, for His loyal love endures forever.
Let Israel say, "His loyal love endures forever."
Let the house of Aaron say, "His loyal love endures forever."
Let those who fear the LORD say, "His loyal love endures forever."
