It is better to take refuge in the LORD than to trust in nobles.
All nations surrounded me; in the name of the LORD I cut them off.
They surrounded me, yes, they surrounded me; in the name of the LORD I cut them off.
They surrounded me like bees; they were put out like a fire of thorns; in the name of the LORD I cut them off.
You pushed me hard so that I was falling, but the LORD helped me.
My strength and my song is Yah, and He has become my deliverance.
The sound of joyful shouting and deliverance is in the tents of the righteous: "The right hand of the LORD does valiantly!
The right hand of the LORD is exalted; the right hand of the LORD does valiantly!"
I will not die, but live, and tell of the works of Yah.
Yah has disciplined me severely, but He has not given me over to death.
Open to me the gates of righteousness; I will enter through them and give thanks to Yah.
This is the gate of the LORD; the righteous will enter through it.
I will give thanks to You, for You have answered me and have become my deliverance.
The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.
This is the LORD's doing; it is marvelous in our eyes.
This is the day the LORD has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it.
Please, LORD, save us! Please, LORD, give us success!
Blessed is he who comes in the name of the LORD! We bless you from the house of the LORD.
The LORD is God, and He has given us light. Bind the festal sacrifice with cords, up to the horns of the altar.
You are my God, and I will give thanks to You; my God, I will exalt You.
Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good, for His loyal love endures forever.

chapters.title: Your Word Is a Lamp to My Feet
chapters.html:
Psalms 119

Aleph

1Blessed are those whose way is blameless,
who walk in the law of the LORD.

2Blessed are those who keep His testimonies,
who seek Him with all their heart,

3who also do no wrong
but walk in His ways.

4You have commanded Your precepts
to be kept diligently.

5Oh that my ways were steadfast
in keeping Your statutes!

6Then I would not be put to shame,
when I look to all Your commandments.

7I will give thanks to You with an upright heart,
when I learn Your righteous judgments.

8I will keep Your statutes;
do not utterly forsake me.

Beth

9How can a young man keep his way pure?
By guarding it according to Your word.

10With all my heart I have sought You;
do not let me stray from Your commandments.

11I have stored up Your promise in my heart,
so that I might not sin against You.

12Blessed are You, LORD;
teach me Your statutes.

13With my lips I have recounted
all the judgments of Your mouth.

14In the way of Your testimonies I have rejoiced
as much as in all riches.

15I will meditate on Your precepts
and look to Your paths.

16I will delight in Your statutes;
I will not forget Your word.

Gimel

17Deal bountifully with Your servant,
so that I may live and keep Your word.

18Open my eyes, so that I may see
wonderful things in Your law.

19I am a guest on the earth;
do not hide Your commandments from me.

20My soul is crushed with longing
for Your judgments at all times.

21You rebuke the arrogant, the accursed,
who stray from Your commandments.

22Take reproach and contempt away from me,
for I have kept Your testimonies.

23Even though princes sit and speak against me,
Your servant meditates on Your statutes.

24Your testimonies are my delight;
they are my counselors.

Daleth

25My soul clings to the dust;
give me life according to Your word.

26I told of my ways, and You answered me;
teach me Your statutes.

27Make me understand the way of Your precepts,
and I will meditate on Your wonders.

28My soul weeps with sorrow;
strengthen me according to Your word.

29Put false ways far from me,
and graciously give me Your law.

30I have chosen the way of faithfulness;
I have set Your judgments before me.

31I cling to Your testimonies;
LORD, do not put me to shame.

32I will run in the way of Your commandments,
for You enlarge my heart.

He

33Teach me, LORD, the way of Your statutes,
and I will keep it to the end.

34Give me understanding, so that I may keep Your law
and observe it with all my heart.

35Lead me in the path of Your commandments,
for I delight in it.

36Turn my heart to Your testimonies
and not to gain.

37Turn my eyes away from looking at worthless things;
give me life in Your ways.

38Confirm to Your servant Your promise,
which is for those who fear You.

39Take away the reproach I dread,
for Your judgments are good.

40I long for Your precepts;
give me life in Your righteousness.

Waw

41Let Your loyal love come to me, LORD,
Your salvation according to Your promise;

42then I will have an answer for the one who taunts me,
for I trust in Your word.

43Do not take the word of truth utterly out of my mouth,
for I hope in Your judgments.

44I will keep Your law continually,
forever and ever.

45I will walk at liberty,
for I have sought Your precepts.

46I will speak of Your testimonies before kings
and will not be put to shame.

47I will delight in Your commandments,
which I love.

48I will lift up my hands to Your commandments, which I love,
and I will meditate on Your statutes.

Zayin

49Remember Your word to Your servant,
in which You have made me hope.

50This is my comfort in my affliction:
that Your promise gives me life.

51The arrogant utterly deride me,
but I do not turn away from Your law.

52I remember Your judgments of old, LORD,
and I take comfort.

53Burning anger seizes me because of the wicked,
who forsake Your law.

54Your statutes have been my songs
in the house where I live as a guest.

55I remember Your name in the night, LORD,
and I keep Your law.

56This has been mine:
that I have kept Your precepts.

Heth

57The LORD is my portion;
I have promised to keep Your words.

58I have sought Your favor with all my heart;
be gracious to me according to Your promise.

59I considered my ways
and turned my feet to Your testimonies.

60I hurried and did not delay
to keep Your commandments.

61The cords of the wicked have wrapped around me,
but I have not forgotten Your law.

62At midnight I rise to give thanks to You
because of Your righteous judgments.

63I am a companion of all who fear You,
of those who keep Your precepts.

64The earth, LORD, is full of Your loyal love;
teach me Your statutes.

Teth

65You have dealt well with Your servant,
LORD, according to Your word.

66Teach me good judgment and knowledge,
for I believe in Your commandments.

67Before I was afflicted I went astray,
but now I keep Your promise.

68You are good and do good;
teach me Your statutes.

69The arrogant smear me with lies,
but with all my heart I keep Your precepts.

70Their heart is thick like fat,
but I delight in Your law.

71It was good for me that I was afflicted,
so that I might learn Your statutes.

72The law of Your mouth is better to me
than thousands of pieces of gold and silver.

Yod

73Your hands made me and formed me;
give me understanding, so that I may learn Your commandments.

74Those who fear You will see me and be glad,
for I hope in Your word.

75I know, LORD, that Your judgments are right,
and in faithfulness You have afflicted me.

76Let Your loyal love comfort me,
according to Your promise to Your servant.

77Let Your compassion come to me, so that I may live,
for Your law is my delight.

78Let the arrogant be put to shame, for they have wronged me with lies;
as for me, I will meditate on Your precepts.

79Let those who fear You turn to me,
those who know Your testimonies.

80Let my heart be blameless in Your statutes,
so that I may not be put to shame.

Kaph

81My soul faints for Your salvation;
I hope in Your word.

82My eyes fail for Your promise;
I say, "When will You comfort me?"

83For I have become like a wineskin in the smoke,
yet I have not forgotten Your statutes.

84How many are the days of Your servant?
When will You execute judgment on those who persecute me?

85The arrogant have dug pits for me,
those who do not live by Your law.

86All Your commandments are faithful;
they persecute me with lies — help me!

87They had almost made an end of me on earth,
but I have not forsaken Your precepts.

88Give me life according to Your loyal love,
and I will keep the testimony of Your mouth.

Lamedh

89Forever, LORD,
Your word stands firm in the heavens.

90Your faithfulness endures to all generations;
You established the earth, and it stands.

91By Your judgments they stand to this day,
for all things are Your servants.

92If Your law had not been my delight,
I would have perished in my affliction.

93I will never forget Your precepts,
for by them You have given me life.

94I am Yours; save me,
for I have sought Your precepts.

95The wicked lie in wait to destroy me,
but I consider Your testimonies.

96I have seen a limit to all perfection,
but Your commandment is exceedingly broad.

Mem

97Oh how I love Your law!
It is my meditation all day long.

98Your commandments make me wiser than my enemies,
for they are ever with me.

99I have more insight than all my teachers,
for Your testimonies are my meditation.

100I understand more than the elders,
for I have kept Your precepts.

101I have held back my feet from every evil path,
so that I may keep Your word.

102I have not turned aside from Your judgments,
for You Yourself have taught me.

103How sweet is Your promise to my taste,
sweeter than honey to my mouth!

104Through Your precepts I gain understanding;
so I hate every false path.

Nun

105Your word is a lamp to my feet
and a light to my path.

106I have sworn an oath and confirmed it,
to keep Your righteous judgments.

107I am severely afflicted;
LORD, give me life according to Your word.

108Accept the freewill offerings of my mouth, LORD,
and teach me Your judgments.

109My life is continually in my hand,
yet I do not forget Your law.

110The wicked have laid a snare for me,
yet I have not strayed from Your precepts.

111Your testimonies are my inheritance forever,
for they are the joy of my heart.

112I have inclined my heart to perform Your statutes
forever, to the end.

Samekh

113I hate the double-minded,
but I love Your law.

114You are my hiding place and my shield;
I hope in Your word.

115Depart from me, you evildoers,
so that I may keep the commandments of my God.

116Uphold me according to Your promise, so that I may live,
and do not let me be ashamed of my hope.

117Hold me up, so that I may be safe
and always look to Your statutes.

118You reject all who stray from Your statutes,
for their deceit is a lie.

119You remove all the wicked of the earth like dross;
so I love Your testimonies.

120My flesh trembles for fear of You,
and I am afraid of Your judgments.

Ayin

121I have done justice and righteousness;
do not leave me to my oppressors.

122Be surety for Your servant's good;
do not let the arrogant oppress me.

123My eyes fail for Your salvation
and for Your righteous promise.

124Deal with Your servant according to Your loyal love,
and teach me Your statutes.

125I am Your servant; give me understanding,
so that I may know Your testimonies.

126It is time for the LORD to act,
for they have broken Your law.

127So I love Your commandments
more than gold, more than fine gold.

128So I count all Your precepts in everything right;
I hate every false path.

Pe

129Your testimonies are wonderful;
so my soul keeps them.

130The opening of Your words gives light;
it gives understanding to the simple.

131I open my mouth and pant,
for I long for Your commandments.

132Turn to me and be gracious to me,
as is Your way with those who love Your name.

133Make my steps firm in Your promise,
and let no iniquity rule over me.

134Redeem me from human oppression,
so that I may keep Your precepts.

135Make Your face shine on Your servant,
and teach me Your statutes.

136My eyes shed streams of water,
because people do not keep Your law.

Tsadhe

137You are righteous, LORD,
and Your judgments are upright.

138You have commanded Your testimonies in righteousness
and in great faithfulness.

139My zeal consumes me,
because my foes forget Your words.

140Your promise is thoroughly refined,
and Your servant loves it.

141I am small and despised,
yet I do not forget Your precepts.

142Your righteousness is righteous forever,
and Your law is truth.

143Trouble and anguish have found me,
but Your commandments are my delight.

144Your testimonies are righteous forever;
give me understanding, so that I may live.

Qoph

145I call with all my heart; answer me, LORD;
I will keep Your statutes.

146I call to You; save me,
so that I may keep Your testimonies.

147I rise before dawn and cry for help;
I hope in Your word.

148My eyes are awake before the watches of the night,
to meditate on Your promise.

149Hear my voice according to Your loyal love;
LORD, give me life according to Your judgment.

150Those who pursue wickedness draw near;
they are far from Your law.

151You are near, LORD,
and all Your commandments are truth.

152Long ago I learned from Your testimonies
that You have founded them forever.

Resh

153Look on my affliction and rescue me,
for I do not forget Your law.

154Plead my cause and redeem me;
give me life according to Your promise.

155Salvation is far from the wicked,
for they do not seek Your statutes.

156Great is Your compassion, LORD;
give me life according to Your judgments.

157Many are my persecutors and my foes,
yet I do not turn aside from Your testimonies.

158I look at the faithless with disgust,
because they do not keep Your promise.

159See how I love Your precepts;
LORD, give me life according to Your loyal love.

160The sum of Your word is truth,
and every one of Your righteous judgments endures forever.

Shin

161Princes persecute me without cause,
but my heart stands in awe of Your word.

162I rejoice at Your promise
like one who finds great spoil.

163I hate and abhor falsehood,
but I love Your law.

164Seven times a day I praise You
for Your righteous judgments.

165Great peace have those who love Your law,
and nothing makes them stumble.

166I hope for Your salvation, LORD,
and I do Your commandments.

167My soul keeps Your testimonies;
I love them exceedingly.

168I keep Your precepts and Your testimonies,
for all my ways are before You.

Taw

169Let my cry come near before You, LORD;
give me understanding according to Your word.

170Let my plea come before You;
deliver me according to Your promise.

171Let my lips pour out praise,
for You teach me Your statutes.

172Let my tongue sing of Your promise,
for all Your commandments are righteousness.

173Let Your hand be ready to help me,
for I have chosen Your precepts.

174I long for Your salvation, LORD,
and Your law is my delight.

175Let my soul live and praise You,
and let Your judgments help me.

176I have gone astray like a lost sheep; seek Your servant,
for I do not forget Your commandments.

Notes

  • The form — the longest psalm and the longest chapter in the Bible: an acrostic of twenty-two stanzas, one for each letter of the Hebrew alphabet, and every verse in a stanza begins with that letter. The letter names are kept as headings, as many Hebrew Bibles print them.

  • v1 and the words for God's word — eight words carry the psalm, and each keeps one English word throughout: torah "law," edut "testimonies," piqqudim "precepts," chuqqim "statutes," mitsvot "commandments," mishpatim "judgments," davar "word," and imrah "promise." Nearly every verse names one of them.

chapters.title: I Am for Peace
chapters.html:
Psalms 120

A song of ascents.

1In my distress I called to the LORD,
and He answered me.

2LORD, deliver my soul from lying lips,
from a deceitful tongue.

3What will He give you,
and what more will He do to you,
you deceitful tongue?

4A warrior's sharp arrows,
with burning coals of the broom tree!

5Woe is me, that I live as a guest in Meshech,
that I dwell among the tents of Kedar!

6Too long has my soul dwelt
with those who hate peace.

7I am for peace,
but when I speak, they are for war.

Notes

  • The title, "A song of ascents" — the first of fifteen (120–134), probably sung by pilgrims going up to Jerusalem for the feasts, or on the steps of the temple.

Too long has my soul dwelt with those who hate peace.
I am for peace, but when I speak, they are for war.

chapters.title: The LORD Is Your Keeper
chapters.html:
Psalms 121

A song for the ascents.

1I lift up my eyes to the mountains —
where does my help come from?

2My help comes from the LORD,
the Maker of heaven and earth.

3He will not let your foot slip;
He who keeps you will not slumber.

4Indeed, He who keeps Israel
will neither slumber nor sleep.

5The LORD is your keeper;
the LORD is your shade at your right hand.

6The sun will not strike you by day,
nor the moon by night.

7The LORD will keep you from all evil;
He will keep your life.

8The LORD will keep your going out and your coming in
from this time forth and forever.

Notes

  • vv3–8 "keeps… keeper… keep" — shamar six times; the English keeps the one word.

speech.text: Psalms 121
I lift up my eyes to the mountains — where does my help come from?
My help comes from the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth.
He will not let your foot slip; He who keeps you will not slumber.
Indeed, He who keeps Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.
The LORD is your keeper; the LORD is your shade at your right hand.
The sun will not strike you by day, nor the moon by night.
The LORD will keep you from all evil; He will keep your life.
The LORD will keep your going out and your coming in from this time forth and forever.

chapters.title: Pray for the Peace of Jerusalem
chapters.html:
Psalms 122

A song of ascents. Of David.

1I was glad when they said to me,
"Let us go to the house of the LORD."

2Our feet are standing
within your gates, Jerusalem.

3Jerusalem, built
as a city bound firmly together,

4where the tribes go up, the tribes of Yah —
as a testimony for Israel —
to give thanks to the name of the LORD.

5For there thrones for judgment were set,
the thrones of the house of David.

6Pray for the peace of Jerusalem:
"May those who love you be secure.

7May there be peace within your walls,
security within your towers."

8For the sake of my brothers and friends
I will say, "Peace be within you."

9For the sake of the house of the LORD our God
I will seek your good.

Notes

  • vv6–8 "peace… secure… security" — a play on the city's name: sha'alu shelom Yerushalayim yishlayu… shalom… shalvah. "Jerusalem" sounds like "city of peace" (Hebrews 7:2).

speech.text: Psalms 122
I was glad when they said to me, "Let us go to the house of the LORD."
Our feet are standing within your gates, Jerusalem.
Jerusalem, built as a city bound firmly together,
where the tribes go up, the tribes of Yah — as a testimony for Israel — to give thanks to the name of the LORD.
For there thrones for judgment were set, the thrones of the house of David.
Pray for the peace of Jerusalem: "May those who love you be secure.
May there be peace within your walls, security within your towers."
For the sake of my brothers and friends I will say, "Peace be within you."
For the sake of the house of the LORD our God I will seek your good.

chapters.title: To You I Lift Up My Eyes
chapters.html:
Psalms 123

A song of ascents.

1To You I lift up my eyes,
You who are enthroned in the heavens.

2As the eyes of servants look to the hand of their master,
as the eyes of a maid to the hand of her mistress,
so our eyes look to the LORD our God
until He is gracious to us.

3Be gracious to us, LORD, be gracious to us,
for we have had more than enough of contempt.

4Our soul has had more than enough
of the scorn of those at ease,
of the contempt of proud oppressors.

Notes

  • v4 "of proud oppressors" — the read form splits the word in two, ligei yonim, "proud ones of the oppressors"; the written form is one word, "the proud." The meaning is close.

speech.text: Psalms 123
To You I lift up my eyes, You who are enthroned in the heavens.
As the eyes of servants look to the hand of their master, as the eyes of a maid to the hand of her mistress, so our eyes look to the LORD our God until He is gracious to us.
Be gracious to us, LORD, be gracious to us, for we have had more than enough of contempt.
Our soul has had more than enough of the scorn of those at ease, of the contempt of proud oppressors.

chapters.title: Our Help Is in the Name of the LORD
chapters.html:
Psalms 124

A song of ascents. Of David.

1If it had not been the LORD who was on our side —
let Israel now say —

2if it had not been the LORD who was on our side
when people rose up against us,

3then they would have swallowed us alive,
when their anger blazed against us;

4then the waters would have swept us away;
the torrent would have gone over our soul;

5then the raging waters
would have gone over our soul.

6Blessed be the LORD,
who has not given us as prey to their teeth.

7Our soul has escaped like a bird
from the snare of the fowlers;
the snare is broken,
and we have escaped.

8Our help is in the name of the LORD,
the Maker of heaven and earth.

Notes

  • v7 "like a bird from the snare of the fowlers" — the snare does not open; it breaks.

speech.text: Psalms 124
If it had not been the LORD who was on our side — let Israel now say —
if it had not been the LORD who was on our side when people rose up against us,
then they would have swallowed us alive, when their anger blazed against us;
then the waters would have swept us away; the torrent would have gone over our soul;
then the raging waters would have gone over our soul.
Blessed be the LORD, who has not given us as prey to their teeth.
Our soul has escaped like a bird from the snare of the fowlers; the snare is broken, and we have escaped.
Our help is in the name of the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth.

chapters.title: As the Mountains Surround Jerusalem
chapters.html:
Psalms 125

A song of ascents.

1Those who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion,
which cannot be moved but stands forever.

2As the mountains surround Jerusalem,
so the LORD surrounds His people
from this time forth and forever.

3For the scepter of wickedness will not rest
on the land allotted to the righteous,
so that the righteous do not stretch out
their hands to do wrong.

4Do good, LORD, to those who are good,
and to those who are upright in their hearts.

5But those who turn aside to their crooked ways
the LORD will lead away with the evildoers.
Peace be on Israel!

Notes

  • v3 "the land allotted to the righteous" — goral, the lot, as the land was divided by lot (Joshua 14:2).

speech.text: Psalms 125
Those who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion, which cannot be moved but stands forever.
As the mountains surround Jerusalem, so the LORD surrounds His people from this time forth and forever.
For the scepter of wickedness will not rest on the land allotted to the righteous, so that the righteous do not stretch out their hands to do wrong.
Do good, LORD, to those who are good, and to those who are upright in their hearts.
But those who turn aside to their crooked ways the LORD will lead away with the evildoers. Peace be on Israel!

chapters.title: Those Who Sow in Tears
chapters.html:
Psalms 126

A song of ascents.

1When the LORD restored the fortunes of Zion,
we were like those who dream.

2Then our mouth was filled with laughter,
and our tongue with shouts of joy.
Then they said among the nations,
"The LORD has done great things for them."

3The LORD has done great things for us;
we were glad.

4Restore our fortunes, LORD,
like streams in the Negev.

5Those who sow in tears
will reap with shouts of joy.

6The one who goes out weeping,
carrying the bag of seed,
will surely come home with shouts of joy,
carrying his sheaves.

Notes

  • v1 "When the LORD restored the fortunes of Zion" — shivat Tsiyyon, perhaps "brought back the returning ones of Zion," the return from exile (Ezra 1); "restored the fortunes" as in 14:7 and 85:1.

speech.text: Psalms 126
When the LORD restored the fortunes of Zion, we were like those who dream.
Then our mouth was filled with laughter, and our tongue with shouts of joy. Then they said among the nations, "The LORD has done great things for them."
The LORD has done great things for us; we were glad.
Restore our fortunes, LORD, like streams in the Negev.
Those who sow in tears will reap with shouts of joy.
The one who goes out weeping, carrying the bag of seed, will surely come home with shouts of joy, carrying his sheaves.

chapters.title: Unless the LORD Builds the House
chapters.html:
Psalms 127

A song of ascents. Of Solomon.

1Unless the LORD builds the house,
its builders labor over it in vain.
Unless the LORD guards the city,
the watchman stays awake in vain.

2It is in vain for you to rise up early
and stay up late,
eating the bread of hard toil;
for He gives to His beloved sleep.

3Children are a heritage from the LORD,
the fruit of the womb a reward.

4Like arrows in the hand of a warrior
are the children of one's youth.

5Blessed is the man
who has filled his quiver with them!
They will not be put to shame
when they speak with enemies in the gate.

Notes

  • v3 "Children are a heritage from the LORD" — banim, "sons"; a play on boneh, "builds," in v1: the LORD builds the house by giving children.

speech.text: Psalms 127
Unless the LORD builds the house, its builders labor over it in vain. Unless the LORD guards the city, the watchman stays awake in vain.
It is in vain for you to rise up early and stay up late, eating the bread of hard toil; for He gives to His beloved sleep.
Children are a heritage from the LORD, the fruit of the womb a reward.
Like arrows in the hand of a warrior are the children of one's youth.
Blessed is the man who has filled his quiver with them! They will not be put to shame when they speak with enemies in the gate.

chapters.title: Blessed Is Everyone Who Fears the LORD
chapters.html:
Psalms 128

A song of ascents.

1Blessed is everyone who fears the LORD,
who walks in His ways.

2You will eat the fruit of the labor of your hands;
you will be blessed, and it will go well with you.

3Your wife will be like a fruitful vine
within your house;
your children like olive shoots
around your table.

4Indeed, this is how the man will be blessed
who fears the LORD.

5May the LORD bless you from Zion,
and may you see the good of Jerusalem
all the days of your life.

6May you see your children's children.
Peace be on Israel!

Notes

  • v3 "olive shoots around your table" — young shoots springing up around an old olive tree, a picture of a family growing up.

speech.text: Psalms 128
Blessed is everyone who fears the LORD, who walks in His ways.
You will eat the fruit of the labor of your hands; you will be blessed, and it will go well with you.
Your wife will be like a fruitful vine within your house; your children like olive shoots around your table.
Indeed, this is how the man will be blessed who fears the LORD.
May the LORD bless you from Zion, and may you see the good of Jerusalem all the days of your life.
May you see your children's children. Peace be on Israel!

chapters.title: They Have Not Prevailed Against Me
chapters.html:
Psalms 129

A song of ascents.

1Many a time they have afflicted me from my youth —
let Israel now say —

2many a time they have afflicted me from my youth,
yet they have not prevailed against me.

3The plowers plowed on my back;
they made their furrows long.

4The LORD is righteous;
He has cut the cords of the wicked.

5Let all who hate Zion
be put to shame and turned back.

6Let them be like grass on the housetops,
which withers before it is pulled up,

7with which the reaper does not fill his hand,
nor the binder of sheaves his arms,

8nor do those who pass by say,
"The blessing of the LORD be on you!
We bless you in the name of the LORD!"

Notes

  • v3 "The plowers plowed on my back" — the lash on a captive's back, cutting long furrows; "their furrows," the read form ma'anitam, is a spelling variant of the written form.

speech.text: Psalms 129
Many a time they have afflicted me from my youth — let Israel now say —
many a time they have afflicted me from my youth, yet they have not prevailed against me.
The plowers plowed on my back; they made their furrows long.
The LORD is righteous; He has cut the cords of the wicked.
Let all who hate Zion be put to shame and turned back.
Let them be like grass on the housetops, which withers before it is pulled up,
with which the reaper does not fill his hand, nor the binder of sheaves his arms,
nor do those who pass by say, "The blessing of the LORD be on you! We bless you in the name of the LORD!"

chapters.title: Out of the Depths
chapters.html:
Psalms 130

A song of ascents.

1Out of the depths I call to You, LORD.

2Lord, hear my voice!
Let Your ears be attentive
to the voice of my pleas.

3If You, Yah, kept a record of iniquities,
Lord, who could stand?

4But with You there is forgiveness,
so that You may be feared.

5I wait for the LORD; my soul waits,
and in His word I hope.

6My soul waits for the Lord
more than watchmen for the morning,
more than watchmen for the morning.

7Israel, hope in the LORD!
For with the LORD there is loyal love,
and with Him is abundant redemption.

8He will redeem Israel
from all its iniquities.

Notes

  • v1 "Out of the depths" — the deep waters, a picture of distress and guilt (69:2, 14); one of the seven penitential psalms, known by its Latin opening, De profundis.

  • v4 "so that You may be feared" — forgiveness does not make God less to be feared but more: the one forgiven reveres the One who forgave.

speech.text: Psalms 130
Out of the depths I call to You, LORD.
Lord, hear my voice! Let Your ears be attentive to the voice of my pleas.
If You, Yah, kept a record of iniquities, Lord, who could stand?
But with You there is forgiveness, so that You may be feared.
I wait for the LORD; my soul waits, and in His word I hope.
My soul waits for the Lord more than watchmen for the morning, more than watchmen for the morning.
Israel, hope in the LORD! For with the LORD there is loyal love, and with Him is abundant redemption.
He will redeem Israel from all its iniquities.

chapters.title: Like a Weaned Child
chapters.html:
Psalms 131

A song of ascents. Of David.

1LORD, my heart is not proud,
and my eyes are not haughty;
I do not occupy myself with great matters,
or things too wonderful for me.

2But I have calmed and quieted my soul,
like a weaned child with its mother;
like a weaned child is my soul within me.

3Israel, hope in the LORD
from this time forth and forever.

Notes

  • v2 "like a weaned child with its mother" — no longer crying to be fed, but content simply to be with her; a child might be weaned at two or three (1 Samuel 1:22–24).

speech.text: Psalms 131
LORD, my heart is not proud, and my eyes are not haughty; I do not occupy myself with great matters, or things too wonderful for me.
But I have calmed and quieted my soul, like a weaned child with its mother; like a weaned child is my soul within me.
Israel, hope in the LORD from this time forth and forever.

chapters.title: Remember, LORD, for David's Sake
chapters.html:
Psalms 132

A song of ascents.

1Remember, LORD, for David's sake
all his hardships,

2how he swore to the LORD
and vowed to the Mighty One of Jacob:

3"I will not enter my house
or get into my bed;

4I will not give sleep to my eyes
or slumber to my eyelids,

5until I find a place for the LORD,
a dwelling place for the Mighty One of Jacob."

6We heard of it in Ephrathah;
we found it in the fields of Jaar.

7"Let us go to His dwelling place;
let us worship at His footstool."

8Arise, LORD, to Your resting place,
You and the ark of Your strength.

9Let Your priests be clothed with righteousness,
and let Your faithful ones sing for joy.

10For the sake of David Your servant,
do not turn away the face of Your anointed.

11The LORD swore to David a sure oath
from which He will not turn back:
"One of the fruit of your body
I will set on your throne.

12If your sons keep My covenant
and My testimonies that I will teach them,
their sons also will sit on your throne forever."

13For the LORD has chosen Zion;
He has desired it for His dwelling:

14"This is My resting place forever;
here I will dwell, for I have desired it.

15I will abundantly bless her provisions;
I will satisfy her poor with bread.

16Her priests I will clothe with salvation,
and her faithful ones will shout aloud for joy.

17There I will make a horn sprout for David;
I have prepared a lamp for My anointed.

18His enemies I will clothe with shame,
but on him his crown will shine."

Notes

  • vv8–10 — nearly the words of Solomon's prayer at the temple's dedication (2 Chronicles 6:41–42), and the English there is followed where the Hebrew is the same: "Arise… to Your resting place, You and the ark of Your strength" and "do not turn away the face of Your anointed." Here the priests are clothed with "righteousness" (there "salvation"), and chasidekha keeps "Your faithful ones," as elsewhere in the Psalms (Chronicles has "loyal ones").

  • vv11–12 — the promise of 2 Samuel 7:12–16, with its condition (1 Kings 2:4); Peter cites v11 at Pentecost (Acts 2:30). The king's pronouns stay lowercase.

speech.text: Psalms 132
Remember, LORD, for David's sake all his hardships,
how he swore to the LORD and vowed to the Mighty One of Jacob:
"I will not enter my house or get into my bed;
I will not give sleep to my eyes or slumber to my eyelids,
until I find a place for the LORD, a dwelling place for the Mighty One of Jacob."
We heard of it in Ephrathah; we found it in the fields of Jaar.
"Let us go to His dwelling place; let us worship at His footstool."
Arise, LORD, to Your resting place, You and the ark of Your strength.
Let Your priests be clothed with righteousness, and let Your faithful ones sing for joy.
For the sake of David Your servant, do not turn away the face of Your anointed.
The LORD swore to David a sure oath from which He will not turn back: "One of the fruit of your body I will set on your throne.
If your sons keep My covenant and My testimonies that I will teach them, their sons also will sit on your throne forever."
For the LORD has chosen Zion; He has desired it for His dwelling:
"This is My resting place forever; here I will dwell, for I have desired it.
I will abundantly bless her provisions; I will satisfy her poor with bread.
Her priests I will clothe with salvation, and her faithful ones will shout aloud for joy.
There I will make a horn sprout for David; I have prepared a lamp for My anointed.
His enemies I will clothe with shame, but on him his crown will shine."

chapters.title: When Brothers Live Together in Unity
chapters.html:
Psalms 133

A song of ascents. Of David.

1How good and how pleasant it is
when brothers live together in unity!

2It is like the precious oil on the head,
running down on the beard,
the beard of Aaron,
running down on the collar of his robes.

3It is like the dew of Hermon,
which falls on the mountains of Zion.
For there the LORD commanded the blessing:
life forevermore.

Notes

  • v2 "the precious oil… the beard of Aaron" — the anointing oil poured on the high priest (Exodus 29:7; Leviticus 8:12), so abundant it runs down to his robe; yored, "running down," is said three times in vv2–3.

speech.text: Psalms 133
How good and how pleasant it is when brothers live together in unity!
It is like the precious oil on the head, running down on the beard, the beard of Aaron, running down on the collar of his robes.
It is like the dew of Hermon, which falls on the mountains of Zion. For there the LORD commanded the blessing: life forevermore.

chapters.title: Bless the LORD by Night
chapters.html:
Psalms 134

A song of ascents.

1Come, bless the LORD,
all you servants of the LORD,
who stand by night in the house of the LORD.

2Lift up your hands to the holy place
and bless the LORD.

3May the LORD bless you from Zion,
the Maker of heaven and earth.

Notes

  • vv1–2 and 3 — the people bless the LORD, and the LORD blesses them in return; the last of the Songs of Ascents ends with a blessing, as the pilgrims leave.

speech.text: Psalms 134
Come, bless the LORD, all you servants of the LORD, who stand by night in the house of the LORD.
Lift up your hands to the holy place and bless the LORD.
May the LORD bless you from Zion, the Maker of heaven and earth.

chapters.title: Praise the Name of the LORD
chapters.html:
Psalms 135

1Praise Yah!
Praise the name of the LORD;
praise Him, servants of the LORD,

2you who stand in the house of the LORD,
in the courts of the house of our God.

3Praise Yah, for the LORD is good;
sing praises to His name, for it is pleasant.

4For Yah has chosen Jacob for Himself,
Israel as His own treasure.

5For I know that the LORD is great,
and our Lord is above all gods.

6Whatever the LORD pleases He does,
in heaven and on earth,
in the seas and all the deeps.

7He makes the clouds rise from the ends of the earth;
He makes lightning for the rain
and brings out the wind from His storehouses.

8He struck down the firstborn of Egypt,
both of man and of beast.

9He sent signs and wonders among you, Egypt,
against Pharaoh and all his servants.

10He struck down many nations
and killed mighty kings —

11Sihon king of the Amorites,
Og king of Bashan,
and all the kingdoms of Canaan —

12giving their land as an inheritance,
an inheritance to Israel His people.

13Your name, LORD, endures forever,
Your remembrance, LORD, for all generations.

14For the LORD will judge His people
and have compassion on His servants.

15The idols of the nations are silver and gold,
the work of human hands.

16They have mouths but do not speak;
eyes, but do not see;

17they have ears but do not give ear,
nor is there any breath in their mouths.

18Those who make them will become like them,
and so will all who trust in them.

19House of Israel, bless the LORD!
House of Aaron, bless the LORD!

20House of Levi, bless the LORD!
You who fear the LORD, bless the LORD!

21Blessed be the LORD from Zion,
He who dwells in Jerusalem.
Praise Yah!

Notes

  • v13 "Your name… Your remembrance… for all generations" — the words God spoke at the burning bush (Exodus 3:15), turned into praise; the English there is followed.

speech.text: Psalms 135
Praise Yah! Praise the name of the LORD; praise Him, servants of the LORD,
you who stand in the house of the LORD, in the courts of the house of our God.
Praise Yah, for the LORD is good; sing praises to His name, for it is pleasant.
For Yah has chosen Jacob for Himself, Israel as His own treasure.
For I know that the LORD is great, and our Lord is above all gods.
Whatever the LORD pleases He does, in heaven and on earth, in the seas and all the deeps.
He makes the clouds rise from the ends of the earth; He makes lightning for the rain and brings out the wind from His storehouses.
He struck down the firstborn of Egypt, both of man and of beast.
He sent signs and wonders among you, Egypt, against Pharaoh and all his servants.
He struck down many nations and killed mighty kings —
Sihon king of the Amorites, Og king of Bashan, and all the kingdoms of Canaan —
giving their land as an inheritance, an inheritance to Israel His people.
Your name, LORD, endures forever, Your remembrance, LORD, for all generations.
For the LORD will judge His people and have compassion on His servants.
The idols of the nations are silver and gold, the work of human hands.
They have mouths but do not speak; eyes, but do not see;
they have ears but do not give ear, nor is there any breath in their mouths.
Those who make them will become like them, and so will all who trust in them.
House of Israel, bless the LORD! House of Aaron, bless the LORD!
House of Levi, bless the LORD! You who fear the LORD, bless the LORD!
Blessed be the LORD from Zion, He who dwells in Jerusalem. Praise Yah!

chapters.title: His Loyal Love Endures Forever
chapters.html:
Psalms 136

1Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good,
for His loyal love endures forever.

2Give thanks to the God of gods,
for His loyal love endures forever.

3Give thanks to the Lord of lords,
for His loyal love endures forever.

4to Him who alone does great wonders,
for His loyal love endures forever.

5to Him who by understanding made the heavens,
for His loyal love endures forever.

6to Him who spread out the earth above the waters,
for His loyal love endures forever.

7to Him who made the great lights,
for His loyal love endures forever.

8the sun to rule by day,
for His loyal love endures forever.

9the moon and stars to rule by night,
for His loyal love endures forever.

10to Him who struck down Egypt in their firstborn,
for His loyal love endures forever.

11and brought Israel out from among them,
for His loyal love endures forever.

12with a strong hand and an outstretched arm,
for His loyal love endures forever.

13to Him who divided the Sea of Reeds in two,
for His loyal love endures forever.

14and made Israel pass through the middle of it,
for His loyal love endures forever.

15but shook off Pharaoh and his army into the Sea of Reeds,
for His loyal love endures forever.

16to Him who led His people through the wilderness,
for His loyal love endures forever.

17to Him who struck down great kings,
for His loyal love endures forever.

18and killed mighty kings,
for His loyal love endures forever.

19Sihon king of the Amorites,
for His loyal love endures forever.

20and Og king of Bashan,
for His loyal love endures forever.

21and gave their land as an inheritance,
for His loyal love endures forever.

22an inheritance to Israel His servant,
for His loyal love endures forever.

23who remembered us in our low estate,
for His loyal love endures forever.

24and rescued us from our foes,
for His loyal love endures forever.

25who gives food to all flesh,
for His loyal love endures forever.

26Give thanks to the God of heaven,
for His loyal love endures forever.

Notes

  • The refrain — ki le'olam chasdo, after every line, twenty-six times; one part may have been sung by a leader and the other by the people (2 Chronicles 7:3, 6; Ezra 3:11). The opening line is the same as 106:1, 107:1 and 118:1.

speech.text: Psalms 136
Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good, for His loyal love endures forever.
Give thanks to the God of gods, for His loyal love endures forever.
Give thanks to the Lord of lords, for His loyal love endures forever.
to Him who alone does great wonders, for His loyal love endures forever.

chapters.title: By the Rivers of Babylon
chapters.html:
Psalms 137

1By the rivers of Babylon,
there we sat down, and we wept
when we remembered Zion.

2On the poplars there
we hung up our lyres.

3For there our captors asked us for songs,
and our tormentors for joy:
"Sing us one of the songs of Zion!"

4How could we sing the LORD's song
in a foreign land?

5If I forget you, Jerusalem,
let my right hand forget!

6Let my tongue cling to the roof of my mouth
if I do not remember you,
if I do not set Jerusalem
above my highest joy.

7Remember, LORD, against the sons of Edom
the day of Jerusalem,
how they said, "Tear it down, tear it down,
down to its foundations!"

8Daughter of Babylon, doomed to destruction,
blessed is the one who repays you
for what you have done to us.

9Blessed is the one who seizes your little ones
and dashes them against the rock.

Notes

  • v7 "the sons of Edom… the day of Jerusalem" — Edom cheered and joined in the city's fall to Babylon (Obadiah 10–14; Lamentations 4:21–22).

  • vv8–9 — the cry of people who had seen it done to their own children (Lamentations 2:11, 20; 2 Kings 8:12); the psalm asks for the very judgment the prophets announced on Babylon (Isaiah 13:16; Jeremiah 51:24, 56). It is a prayer handed to God, not an act taken into their own hands (Romans 12:19).

speech.text: Psalms 137
By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down, and we wept when we remembered Zion.
On the poplars there we hung up our lyres.
For there our captors asked us for songs, and our tormentors for joy: "Sing us one of the songs of Zion!"
How could we sing the LORD's song in a foreign land?
If I forget you, Jerusalem, let my right hand forget!
Let my tongue cling to the roof of my mouth if I do not remember you, if I do not set Jerusalem above my highest joy.
Remember, LORD, against the sons of Edom the day of Jerusalem, how they said, "Tear it down, tear it down, down to its foundations!"
Daughter of Babylon, doomed to destruction, blessed is the one who repays you for what you have done to us.
Blessed is the one who seizes your little ones and dashes them against the rock.

chapters.title: With All My Heart
chapters.html:
Psalms 138

Of David.

1I will give thanks to You with all my heart;
before the gods I will sing Your praise.

2I will bow down toward Your holy temple
and give thanks to Your name
for Your loyal love and Your truth,
for You have exalted Your promise above all Your name.

3On the day I called, You answered me;
You made me bold with strength in my soul.

4All the kings of the earth will give thanks to You, LORD,
for they have heard the words of Your mouth.

5They will sing of the ways of the LORD,
for great is the glory of the LORD.

6For though the LORD is high, He regards the lowly,
but the proud He knows from afar.

7Though I walk in the middle of trouble,
You preserve my life;
You stretch out Your hand against the wrath of my enemies,
and Your right hand saves me.

8The LORD will fulfill His purpose for me;
Your loyal love, LORD, endures forever.
Do not forsake the works of Your hands.

Notes

  • v6 "He regards the lowly" — as in 113:5–7 and Isaiah 57:15.

speech.text: Psalms 138
I will give thanks to You with all my heart; before the gods I will sing Your praise.
I will bow down toward Your holy temple and give thanks to Your name for Your loyal love and Your truth, for You have exalted Your promise above all Your name.
On the day I called, You answered me; You made me bold with strength in my soul.
All the kings of the earth will give thanks to You, LORD, for they have heard the words of Your mouth.
They will sing of the ways of the LORD, for great is the glory of the LORD.
For though the LORD is high, He regards the lowly, but the proud He knows from afar.
Though I walk in the middle of trouble, You preserve my life; You stretch out Your hand against the wrath of my enemies, and Your right hand saves me.
The LORD will fulfill His purpose for me; Your loyal love, LORD, endures forever. Do not forsake the works of Your hands.

chapters.title: You Have Searched Me and Known Me
chapters.html:
Psalms 139

For the director. Of David. A psalm.

1LORD, You have searched me and known me.

2You know when I sit down and when I rise up;
You understand my thoughts from afar.

3You search out my path and my lying down
and are acquainted with all my ways.

4For there is not a word on my tongue
but You, LORD, know it altogether.

5You hem me in, behind and before,
and lay Your hand on me.

6Such knowledge is too wonderful for me;
it is high; I cannot reach it.

7Where can I go from Your Spirit?
Where can I flee from Your presence?

8If I go up to the heavens, You are there;
if I make my bed in Sheol, You are there.

9If I take the wings of the dawn
and dwell at the farthest part of the sea,

10even there Your hand will lead me,
and Your right hand will hold me.

11If I say, "Surely the darkness will cover me,
and the light around me become night,"

12even the darkness is not dark to You;
the night shines like the day,
for darkness is as light to You.

13For You formed my inmost parts;
You knit me together in my mother's womb.

14I give thanks to You,
for I am fearfully and wonderfully made;
wonderful are Your works,
and my soul knows it very well.

15My frame was not hidden from You
when I was made in secret,
intricately woven in the depths of the earth.

16Your eyes saw my unformed body;
in Your book they were all written,
the days that were formed,
and one of them was set for it.

17How precious to me are Your thoughts, God!
How vast is the sum of them!

18If I counted them, they would outnumber the sand.
I awake, and I am still with You.

19If only You would slay the wicked, God!
Men of blood, depart from me —

20those who speak of You with evil intent;
Your enemies take Your name in vain.

21Do I not hate those who hate You, LORD,
and feel disgust at those who rise up against You?

22I hate them with complete hatred;
they have become my enemies.

23Search me, God, and know my heart;
test me and know my anxious thoughts.

24See if there is any grievous way in me,
and lead me in the way everlasting.

Notes

  • v16 "and one of them was set for it" — the read form, velo echad bahem: each of the days was appointed for the unformed body. The written form has velo, "and not," giving the reading most English versions follow: "when as yet there was not one of them."

  • vv23–24 "Search me, God, and know my heart" — the psalm ends where it began (v1), now asking for the searching it first described.

speech.text: Psalms 139
LORD, You have searched me and known me.
You know when I sit down and when I rise up; You understand my thoughts from afar.
You search out my path and my lying down and are acquainted with all my ways.
For there is not a word on my tongue but You, LORD, know it altogether.
You hem me in, behind and before, and lay Your hand on me.
Such knowledge is too wonderful for me; it is high; I cannot reach it.
Where can I go from Your Spirit? Where can I flee from Your presence?
If I go up to the heavens, You are there; if I make my bed in Sheol, You are there.
If I take the wings of the dawn and dwell at the farthest part of the sea,

If I say, "Surely the darkness will cover me, and the light around me become night,"
even the darkness is not dark to You; the night shines like the day, for darkness is as light to You.
For You formed my inmost parts; You knit me together in my mother's womb.
I give thanks to You, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made; wonderful are Your works, and my soul knows it very well.
My frame was not hidden from You when I was made in secret, intricately woven in the depths of the earth.
Your eyes saw my unformed body; in Your book they were all written, the days that were formed, and one of them was set for it.
How precious to me are Your thoughts, God! How vast is the sum of them!
If I counted them, they would outnumber the sand. I awake, and I am still with You.
If only You would slay the wicked, God! Men of blood, depart from me —
those who speak of You with evil intent; Your enemies take Your name in vain.
Do I not hate those who hate You, LORD, and feel disgust at those who rise up against You?
I hate them with complete hatred; they have become my enemies.
Search me, God, and know my heart; test me and know my anxious thoughts.
See if there is any grievous way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.

chapters.title: Rescue Me from Evil People
chapters.html:
Psalms 140

For the director. A psalm of David.

1Rescue me, LORD, from evil people;
preserve me from violent men,

2who devise evil things in their heart
and stir up wars every day.

3They sharpen their tongue like a serpent's;
the venom of vipers is under their lips. Selah

4Guard me, LORD, from the hands of the wicked;
preserve me from violent men,
who have planned to trip up my feet.

5The proud have hidden a trap for me,
and with cords they have spread a net beside the path;
they have set snares for me. Selah

6I say to the LORD, "You are my God;
give ear, LORD, to the voice of my pleas.

7GOD the Lord, the strength of my salvation,
You have covered my head on the day of battle.

8Do not grant, LORD, the desires of the wicked;
do not further their plot, or they will be exalted." Selah

9As for the head of those who surround me,
let the trouble of their lips cover them.

10Let burning coals fall on them;
let them be cast into the fire,
into deep pits, never to rise.

11Let not a slanderer be established in the land;
let evil hunt down the violent man with blow upon blow.

12I know that the LORD will maintain the cause of the afflicted
and justice for the needy.

13Surely the righteous will give thanks to Your name;
the upright will dwell in Your presence.

Notes

  • v3 "the venom of vipers is under their lips" — Paul quotes it in his chain of verses on human sin (Romans 3:13).

speech.text: Psalms 140
Rescue me, LORD, from evil people; preserve me from violent men,
who devise evil things in their heart and stir up wars every day.
They sharpen their tongue like a serpent's; the venom of vipers is under their lips. Selah
Guard me, LORD, from the hands of the wicked; preserve me from violent men, who have planned to trip up my feet.
The proud have hidden a trap for me, and with cords they have spread a net beside the path; they have set snares for me. Selah

I know that the LORD will maintain the cause of the afflicted and justice for the needy.
Surely the righteous will give thanks to Your name; the upright will dwell in Your presence.

chapters.title: Let My Prayer Be Set Before You as Incense
chapters.html:
Psalms 141

A psalm of David.

1LORD, I call to You; hurry to me!
Give ear to my voice when I call to You.

2Let my prayer be set before You as incense,
the lifting up of my hands as the evening offering.

3Set a guard, LORD, over my mouth;
keep watch over the door of my lips.

4Do not incline my heart to any evil thing,
to busy myself with deeds of wickedness
with men who do iniquity,
and let me not eat of their delicacies.

5Let a righteous man strike me — it is loyal love;
let him rebuke me — it is oil on my head;
let my head not refuse it.
For my prayer is still against their evil deeds.

6When their judges are thrown down by the sides of the rock,
they will hear my words, for they are pleasant.

7As when one plows and breaks up the earth,
our bones are scattered at the mouth of Sheol.

8But my eyes are toward You, GOD the Lord;
in You I take refuge; do not leave my soul defenseless.

9Keep me from the hands of the snare they have laid for me,
and from the traps of evildoers.

10Let the wicked fall into their own nets,
while I pass by in safety.

Notes

  • vv5–7 — among the hardest verses in the Psalms; the setting is unknown, and every line has other possible readings. The Hebrew is followed word by word.

speech.text: Psalms 141
LORD, I call to You; hurry to me! Give ear to my voice when I call to You.
Let my prayer be set before You as incense, the lifting up of my hands as the evening offering.
Set a guard, LORD, over my mouth; keep watch over the door of my lips.
Do not incline my heart to any evil thing, to busy myself with deeds of wickedness with men who do iniquity, and let me not eat of their delicacies.
Let a righteous man strike me — it is loyal love; let him rebuke me — it is oil on my head; let my head not refuse it. For my prayer is still against their evil deeds.
When their judges are thrown down by the sides of the rock, they will hear my words, for they are pleasant.
As when one plows and breaks up the earth, our bones are scattered at the mouth of Sheol.
But my eyes are toward You, GOD the Lord; in You I take refuge; do not leave my soul defenseless.
Keep me from the hands of the snare they have laid for me, and from the traps of evildoers.
Let the wicked fall into their own nets, while I pass by in safety.

chapters.title: No One Cares for My Soul
chapters.html:
Psalms 142

A Maskil of David, when he was in the cave. A prayer.

1With my voice I cry out to the LORD;
with my voice I plead with the LORD for mercy.

2I pour out my complaint before Him;
I tell my trouble before Him.

3When my spirit grows faint within me,
You know my path.
In the way where I walk
they have hidden a trap for me.

4Look to the right and see:
there is no one who takes notice of me;
refuge has vanished from me;
no one cares for my soul.

5I cry to You, LORD;
I say, "You are my refuge,
my portion in the land of the living."

6Give heed to my cry,
for I am brought very low;
deliver me from my persecutors,
for they are too strong for me.

7Bring my soul out of prison,
so that I may give thanks to Your name.
The righteous will gather around me,
for You will deal bountifully with me.

Notes

  • The title, "when he was in the cave" — the cave of Adullam (1 Samuel 22:1) or of En-gedi (1 Samuel 24:3), as in the title of Psalm 57.

speech.text: Psalms 142
With my voice I cry out to the LORD; with my voice I plead with the LORD for mercy.
I pour out my complaint before Him; I tell my trouble before Him.
When my spirit grows faint within me, You know my path. In the way where I walk they have hidden a trap for me.
Look to the right and see: there is no one who takes notice of me; refuge has vanished from me; no one cares for my soul.
I cry to You, LORD; I say, "You are my refuge, my portion in the land of the living."
Give heed to my cry, for I am brought very low; deliver me from my persecutors, for they are too strong for me.
Bring my soul out of prison, so that I may give thanks to Your name. The righteous will gather around me, for You will deal bountifully with me.

chapters.title: No One Living Is Righteous Before You
chapters.html:
Psalms 143

A psalm of David.

1LORD, hear my prayer;
give ear to my pleas;
in Your faithfulness answer me,
in Your righteousness.

2Do not enter into judgment with Your servant,
for no one living is righteous before You.

3For the enemy has pursued my soul;
he has crushed my life to the ground;
he has made me dwell in darkness
like those long dead.

4So my spirit grows faint within me;
my heart within me is appalled.

5I remember the days of old;
I meditate on all Your works;
I ponder the work of Your hands.

6I spread out my hands to You;
my soul thirsts for You like a weary land. Selah

7Answer me quickly, LORD!
My spirit fails.
Do not hide Your face from me,
or I will be like those who go down to the pit.

8Let me hear of Your loyal love in the morning,
for in You I trust.
Make me know the way I should go,
for to You I lift up my soul.

9Deliver me from my enemies, LORD;
I take shelter in You.

10Teach me to do Your will,
for You are my God.
Let Your good Spirit lead me
on level ground.

11For Your name's sake, LORD, give me life;
in Your righteousness bring my soul out of trouble.

12In Your loyal love cut off my enemies,
and destroy all who afflict my soul,
for I am Your servant.

Notes

  • v2 "for no one living is righteous before You" — Paul builds on this line: by the works of the law no flesh will be justified in His sight (Romans 3:20; Galatians 2:16). The last of the seven penitential psalms.

speech.text: Psalms 143
LORD, hear my prayer; give ear to my pleas; in Your faithfulness answer me, in Your righteousness.
Do not enter into judgment with Your servant, for no one living is righteous before You.
For the enemy has pursued my soul; he has crushed my life to the ground; he has made me dwell in darkness like those long dead.
So my spirit grows faint within me; my heart within me is appalled.
I remember the days of old; I meditate on all Your works; I ponder the work of Your hands.
I spread out my hands to You; my soul thirsts for You like a weary land. Selah
Answer me quickly, LORD! My spirit fails. Do not hide Your face from me, or I will be like those who go down to the pit.
Let me hear of Your loyal love in the morning, for in You I trust. Make me know the way I should go, for to You I lift up my soul.
Deliver me from my enemies, LORD; I take shelter in You.
Teach me to do Your will, for You are my God. Let Your good Spirit lead me on level ground.
For Your name's sake, LORD, give me life; in Your righteousness bring my soul out of trouble.
In Your loyal love cut off my enemies, and destroy all who afflict my soul, for I am Your servant.

chapters.title: Blessed Be the LORD, My Rock
chapters.html:
Psalms 144

Of David.

1Blessed be the LORD, my rock,
who trains my hands for battle
and my fingers for war;

2my loyal love and my fortress,
my stronghold and my deliverer,
my shield, in whom I take refuge,
who subdues my people under me.

3LORD, what is man, that You know him,
or the son of man, that You think of him?

4Man is like a breath;
his days are like a passing shadow.

5LORD, bend Your heavens and come down;
touch the mountains, so that they smoke.

6Flash forth lightning and scatter them;
send out Your arrows and rout them.

7Stretch out Your hands from on high;
rescue me and deliver me from many waters,
from the hand of foreigners,

8whose mouths speak falsehood,
and whose right hand is a right hand of lies.

9God, I will sing a new song to You;
on a ten-stringed harp I will sing praises to You,

10who gives victory to kings,
who rescues David His servant from the deadly sword.

11Rescue me and deliver me
from the hand of foreigners,
whose mouths speak falsehood,
and whose right hand is a right hand of lies.

12May our sons be like plants
grown tall in their youth,
our daughters like corner pillars
carved for a palace.

13May our barns be full,
supplying every kind of produce;
may our flocks increase by thousands,
by tens of thousands in our fields;

14may our cattle be heavy with young;
may there be no breach in the walls, no going into exile,
and no cry of distress in our streets.

15Blessed are the people for whom it is so!
Blessed are the people whose God is the LORD!

Notes

  • vv1–11 — much of it drawn from Psalm 18, and the English there is followed where the Hebrew is the same: "trains my hands for war" (18:34), "my fortress… my deliverer… my shield, in whom I take refuge" (18:2), "subdues… under me" (18:47), "bend… the heavens and come down" (18:9), "send out… arrows… rout them" (18:14), "from on high… from many waters" (18:16). Here they are prayers, where Psalm 18 told them as things done.

Blessed be the LORD, my rock, who trains my hands for battle and my fingers for war;
my loyal love and my fortress, my stronghold and my deliverer, my shield, in whom I take refuge, who subdues my people under me.
LORD, what is man, that You know him, or the son of man, that You think of him?
Man is like a breath; his days are like a passing shadow.

Flash forth lightning and scatter them; send out Your arrows and rout them.

who gives victory to kings, who rescues David His servant from the deadly sword.
Rescue me and deliver me from the hand of foreigners, whose mouths speak falsehood, and whose right hand is a right hand of lies.
May our sons be like plants grown tall in their youth, our daughters like corner pillars carved for a palace.
May our barns be full, supplying every kind of produce; may our flocks increase by thousands, by tens of thousands in our fields;
may our cattle be heavy with young; may there be no breach in the walls, no going into exile, and no cry of distress in our streets.
Blessed are the people for whom it is so! Blessed are the people whose God is the LORD!

chapters.title: I Will Exalt You, My God the King
chapters.html:
Psalms 145

A praise of David.

1I will exalt You, my God the King,
and bless Your name forever and ever.

2Every day I will bless You
and praise Your name forever and ever.

3Great is the LORD and greatly to be praised,
and His greatness is unsearchable.

4One generation will commend Your works to another
and declare Your mighty acts.

5On the glorious splendor of Your majesty
and on Your wondrous works I will meditate.

6They will speak of the might of Your awesome deeds,
and I will tell of Your greatness.

7They will pour out the memory of Your abundant goodness
and sing joyfully of Your righteousness.

8The LORD is gracious and merciful,
slow to anger and great in loyal love.

9The LORD is good to all,
and His compassion is over all that He has made.

10All Your works will give thanks to You, LORD,
and Your faithful ones will bless You.

11They will speak of the glory of Your kingdom
and talk of Your might,

12to make known to the children of man His mighty acts
and the glorious splendor of His kingdom.

13Your kingdom is an everlasting kingdom,
and Your dominion endures through all generations.

14The LORD upholds all who fall
and raises up all who are bowed down.

15The eyes of all look to You,
and You give them their food in due season.

16You open Your hand
and satisfy the desire of every living thing.

17The LORD is righteous in all His ways
and loyal in all His works.

18The LORD is near to all who call on Him,
to all who call on Him in truth.

19He fulfills the desire of those who fear Him;
He hears their cry and saves them.

20The LORD guards all who love Him,
but all the wicked He will destroy.

21My mouth will speak the praise of the LORD,
and let all flesh bless His holy name
forever and ever.

Notes

  • The form — an acrostic, one verse for each letter of the Hebrew alphabet, except nun, which is missing after v13. The Greek has a nun line there, "The Lord is faithful in His words and holy in all His works," and a Dead Sea Psalms scroll has nearly the same. The Hebrew is followed, and the line is not added.

speech.text: Psalms 145
I will exalt You, my God the King, and bless Your name forever and ever.
Every day I will bless You and praise Your name forever and ever.
Great is the LORD and greatly to be praised, and His greatness is unsearchable.
One generation will commend Your works to another and declare Your mighty acts.
On the glorious splendor of Your majesty and on Your wondrous works I will meditate.
They will speak of the might of Your awesome deeds, and I will tell of Your greatness.
They will pour out the memory of Your abundant goodness and sing joyfully of Your righteousness.

The LORD is good to all, and His compassion is over all that He has made.

They will speak of the glory of Your kingdom and talk of Your might,
to make known to the children of man His mighty acts and the glorious splendor of His kingdom.
Your kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and Your dominion endures through all generations.
The LORD upholds all who fall and raises up all who are bowed down.
The eyes of all look to You, and You give them their food in due season.
You open Your hand and satisfy the desire of every living thing.
The LORD is righteous in all His ways and loyal in all His works.
The LORD is near to all who call on Him, to all who call on Him in truth.
He fulfills the desire of those who fear Him; He hears their cry and saves them.
The LORD guards all who love Him, but all the wicked He will destroy.
My mouth will speak the praise of the LORD, and let all flesh bless His holy name forever and ever.

chapters.title: Do Not Trust in Nobles
chapters.html:
Psalms 146

1Praise Yah!
Praise the LORD, my soul!

2I will praise the LORD as long as I live;
I will sing praises to my God while I have being.

3Do not trust in nobles,
in a son of man, in whom there is no salvation.

4His breath departs; he returns to his ground;
on that very day his plans perish.

5Blessed is the one whose help is the God of Jacob,
whose hope is in the LORD his God,

6the Maker of heaven and earth,
the sea and everything in them,
who keeps truth forever;

7who executes justice for the oppressed,
who gives food to the hungry.
The LORD sets the prisoners free;

8the LORD opens the eyes of the blind;
the LORD raises up those who are bowed down;
the LORD loves the righteous;

9the LORD guards the guests;
He upholds the fatherless and the widow,
but the way of the wicked He turns upside down.

10The LORD will reign forever,
your God, Zion, for all generations.
Praise Yah!

Notes

  • vv1–2 — the first of the five "hallelujah" psalms that close the book (146–150); v2b is the same as 104:33b, and the English there is followed.

  • v4 "he returns to his ground" — adam to his adamah, the man to the ground he was taken from (Genesis 3:19).

speech.text: Psalms 146
Praise Yah! Praise the LORD, my soul!
I will praise the LORD as long as I live; I will sing praises to my God while I have being.
Do not trust in nobles, in a son of man, in whom there is no salvation.
His breath departs; he returns to his ground; on that very day his plans perish.
Blessed is the one whose help is the God of Jacob, whose hope is in the LORD his God,
the Maker of heaven and earth, the sea and everything in them, who keeps truth forever;
who executes justice for the oppressed, who gives food to the hungry. The LORD sets the prisoners free;
the LORD opens the eyes of the blind; the LORD raises up those who are bowed down; the LORD loves the righteous;
the LORD guards the guests; He upholds the fatherless and the widow, but the way of the wicked He turns upside down.
The LORD will reign forever, your God, Zion, for all generations. Praise Yah!

chapters.title: He Heals the Brokenhearted
chapters.html:
Psalms 147

1Praise Yah!
For it is good to sing praises to our God;
for it is pleasant, and praise is fitting.

2The LORD builds up Jerusalem;
He gathers the outcasts of Israel.

3He heals the brokenhearted
and binds up their wounds.

4He counts the number of the stars;
He calls them all by name.

5Great is our Lord and abundant in power;
His understanding is beyond measure.

6The LORD lifts up the humble;
He casts the wicked down to the ground.

7Sing to the LORD with thanksgiving;
make music to our God on the lyre,

8who covers the heavens with clouds,
who prepares rain for the earth,
who makes grass grow on the mountains,

9who gives the beasts their food,
and the young ravens when they cry.

10He does not delight in the strength of the horse,
nor take pleasure in the legs of a man;

11the LORD takes pleasure in those who fear Him,
in those who hope in His loyal love.

12Praise the LORD, Jerusalem!
Praise your God, Zion!

13For He has strengthened the bars of your gates;
He has blessed your children within you.

14He makes peace in your borders;
He satisfies you with the finest of the wheat.

15He sends out His command to the earth;
His word runs swiftly.

16He gives snow like wool;
He scatters frost like ashes.

17He hurls down His hail like crumbs;
who can stand before His cold?

18He sends out His word and melts them;
He makes His wind blow, and the waters flow.

19He declares His words to Jacob,
His statutes and His judgments to Israel.

20He has not dealt so with any other nation;
as for His judgments, they do not know them.
Praise Yah!

Notes

  • v4 "He counts the number of the stars; He calls them all by name" — as in Isaiah 40:26; the God who numbers the stars heals the brokenhearted (v3).

speech.text: Psalms 147
Praise Yah! For it is good to sing praises to our God; for it is pleasant, and praise is fitting.
The LORD builds up Jerusalem; He gathers the outcasts of Israel.
He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.
He counts the number of the stars; He calls them all by name.
Great is our Lord and abundant in power; His understanding is beyond measure.
The LORD lifts up the humble; He casts the wicked down to the ground.
Sing to the LORD with thanksgiving; make music to our God on the lyre,
who covers the heavens with clouds, who prepares rain for the earth, who makes grass grow on the mountains,
who gives the beasts their food, and the young ravens when they cry.
He does not delight in the strength of the horse, nor take pleasure in the legs of a man;
the LORD takes pleasure in those who fear Him, in those who hope in His loyal love.
Praise the LORD, Jerusalem! Praise your God, Zion!
For He has strengthened the bars of your gates; He has blessed your children within you.
He makes peace in your borders; He satisfies you with the finest of the wheat.
He sends out His command to the earth; His word runs swiftly.
He gives snow like wool; He scatters frost like ashes.
He hurls down His hail like crumbs; who can stand before His cold?
He sends out His word and melts them; He makes His wind blow, and the waters flow.
He declares His words to Jacob, His statutes and His judgments to Israel.
He has not dealt so with any other nation; as for His judgments, they do not know them. Praise Yah!

chapters.title: Praise the LORD from the Heavens
chapters.html:
Psalms 148

1Praise Yah!
Praise the LORD from the heavens;
praise Him in the heights!

2Praise Him, all His messengers;
praise Him, all His hosts!

3Praise Him, sun and moon;
praise Him, all you shining stars!

4Praise Him, highest heavens,
and you waters above the heavens!

5Let them praise the name of the LORD,
for He commanded, and they were created.

6He established them forever and ever;
He gave a decree that will not pass away.

7Praise the LORD from the earth,
you sea monsters and all deeps,

8fire and hail, snow and mist,
stormy wind fulfilling His word,

9mountains and all hills,
fruit trees and all cedars,

10beasts and all cattle,
creeping things and winged birds,

11kings of the earth and all peoples,
princes and all judges of the earth,

12young men and young women,
old men and children together.

13Let them praise the name of the LORD,
for His name alone is exalted;
His splendor is above earth and heaven.

14He has raised up a horn for His people,
praise for all His faithful ones,
for the children of Israel, the people near to Him.
Praise Yah!

Notes

  • vv1–6 and 7–12 — the heavens first, then the earth, in the order of Genesis 1: the waters above (Genesis 1:7), sun, moon and stars (1:16), sea monsters (1:21), beasts, cattle and creeping things (1:24), and people.

speech.text: Psalms 148
Praise Yah! Praise the LORD from the heavens; praise Him in the heights!
Praise Him, all His messengers; praise Him, all His hosts!
Praise Him, sun and moon; praise Him, all you shining stars!
Praise Him, highest heavens, and you waters above the heavens!
Let them praise the name of the LORD, for He commanded, and they were created.
He established them forever and ever; He gave a decree that will not pass away.
Praise the LORD from the earth, you sea monsters and all deeps,
fire and hail, snow and mist, stormy wind fulfilling His word,
mountains and all hills, fruit trees and all cedars,
beasts and all cattle, creeping things and winged birds,
kings of the earth and all peoples, princes and all judges of the earth,
young men and young women, old men and children together.
Let them praise the name of the LORD, for His name alone is exalted; His splendor is above earth and heaven.
He has raised up a horn for His people, praise for all His faithful ones, for the children of Israel, the people near to Him. Praise Yah!

chapters.title: Sing to the LORD a New Song
chapters.html:
Psalms 149

1Praise Yah!
Sing to the LORD a new song,
His praise in the assembly of the faithful.

2Let Israel rejoice in its Maker;
let the children of Zion be glad in their King.

3Let them praise His name with dancing;
let them sing praises to Him with tambourine and lyre.

4For the LORD takes pleasure in His people;
He adorns the humble with salvation.

5Let the faithful exult in glory;
let them sing for joy on their beds.

6Let the high praises of God be in their throats
and a two-edged sword in their hands,

7to execute vengeance on the nations
and punishment on the peoples,

8to bind their kings with chains
and their honored men with fetters of iron,

9to carry out on them the judgment written.
This is honor for all His faithful ones.
Praise Yah!

Notes

  • vv6–9 — the praise of God and the sword together, carrying out "the judgment written," the judgment already decreed against the nations that oppressed Israel (Deuteronomy 32:41–43; Isaiah 41:15–16). The New Testament gives God's people the sword of the Spirit, the word of God (Ephesians 6:17; Hebrews 4:12; Revelation 19:15).

speech.text: Psalms 149
Praise Yah! Sing to the LORD a new song, His praise in the assembly of the faithful.
Let Israel rejoice in its Maker; let the children of Zion be glad in their King.
Let them praise His name with dancing; let them sing praises to Him with tambourine and lyre.
For the LORD takes pleasure in His people; He adorns the humble with salvation.
Let the faithful exult in glory; let them sing for joy on their beds.
Let the high praises of God be in their throats and a two-edged sword in their hands,
to execute vengeance on the nations and punishment on the peoples,
to bind their kings with chains and their honored men with fetters of iron,
to carry out on them the judgment written. This is honor for all His faithful ones. Praise Yah!

chapters.title: Let Everything That Has Breath Praise Yah
chapters.html:
Psalms 150

1Praise Yah!
Praise God in His sanctuary;
praise Him in the expanse of His might!

2Praise Him for His mighty deeds;
praise Him for His abundant greatness!

3Praise Him with the blast of the ram's horn;
praise Him with harp and lyre!

4Praise Him with tambourine and dancing;
praise Him with strings and pipe!

5Praise Him with sounding cymbals;
praise Him with clanging cymbals!

6Let everything that has breath praise Yah!
Praise Yah!

Notes

  • The whole psalm — the close of the fifth book and of the Hebrew Psalter: where the other books end with a blessing (41:13; 72:18–19; 89:52; 106:48), this one is all praise; "praise" is said thirteen times.

  • v6 "everything that has breath" — neshamah, the breath God blew into the first human (Genesis 2:7).

speech.text: Psalms 150
Praise Yah! Praise God in His sanctuary; praise Him in the expanse of His might!
Praise Him for His mighty deeds; praise Him for His abundant greatness!
Praise Him with the blast of the ram's horn; praise Him with harp and lyre!
Praise Him with tambourine and dancing; praise Him with strings and pipe!
Praise Him with sounding cymbals; praise Him with clanging cymbals!
Let everything that has breath praise Yah! Praise Yah!

chapters.title: I Was Small Among My Brothers
chapters.html:
Psalms 151

This psalm was written by David himself, though it is outside the number, when he fought Goliath in single combat.

1I was small among my brothers
and the youngest in my father's house;
I tended my father's sheep.

2My hands made an instrument;
my fingers tuned a harp.

3Who will tell my Lord?
The Lord Himself — He Himself hears.

4He sent His angel
and took me from my father's sheep
and anointed me with the oil of His anointing.

5My brothers were handsome and tall,
but the Lord was not pleased with them.

6I went out to meet the Philistine,
and he cursed me by his idols.

7But I drew his own sword from him and beheaded him,
and took away the disgrace from the sons of Israel.

Notes

  • The source — this psalm is not in the Hebrew Bible held here; it is rendered from the Greek of Swete's Septuagint, where it stands after Psalm 150. The Ethiopian Psalter counts it among the Psalms. Kyrios is "Lord," and angelos "angel," as in the other books rendered from the Greek.

  • The title, "outside the number" — the Greek Psalter counts 150 psalms; this one is added after them. A longer Hebrew form, in two parts, was found among the Dead Sea Scrolls (11QPs^a).

  • v4 "He sent His angel" — the Hebrew form found at Qumran reads "His prophet," that is, Samuel (1 Samuel 16:12–13).

speech.text: Psalms 151
I was small among my brothers and the youngest in my father's house; I tended my father's sheep.
My hands made an instrument; my fingers tuned a harp.
Who will tell my Lord? The Lord Himself — He Himself hears.
He sent His angel and took me from my father's sheep and anointed me with the oil of His anointing.
My brothers were handsome and tall, but the Lord was not pleased with them.
I went out to meet the Philistine, and he cursed me by his idols.
But I drew his own sword from him and beheaded him, and took away the disgrace from the sons of Israel.
